stories.title: Ghaziabad sub-inspector Asmita Dey scripts history with judo gold:Judoka beat Canadian in final, thanks UP CM Yogi for police job
stories.summary: Ghaziabad's Sub-Inspector Asmita Dey won a gold medal at the Commonwealth Games-2026 on Friday. She defeated a Canadian player in judo. Asmita Dey is a resident of Tripura and is a Sub-Inspector in the UP Police. After winning the gold, Asmita Dey said, "I am in the UP Police. I want to thank CM Yogi ji because he gave me a job in the UP Police. This job gave me support. It is because of this that I reached here and was able to win the gold medal." Initially trailed, then made a spectacular comeback The start of the final match was not easy for Asmita Dey. Canada's Hady Quach took an early lead by scoring a yuko point. Asmita also received a shido penalty. Despite this, she did not give up and made a brilliant comeback to level the score at 1-1. No player could score a decisive point until the stipulated time, so the match went into golden score. Here, Asmita made a brilliant move at the right moment and scored a second yuko point, winning both the match and the gold medal. Before reaching the final, Asmita had put up a brilliant performance by defeating Scotland's Eva Ewing and Summer Shaw. Asmita said - Yogi ji's support gave me strength Asmita said - Her father passed away in December 2025. My father always supported me. After he left, I felt like everything was over. But two months later, the Asian Games trials took place, in which I secured the first position at the national level. After winning the gold medal, Asmita Dey said - This medal is very important for me, my state, and my country. I dedicate it to my coach and my father. I am very happy with this gold medal. This is for all those people who supported me. She also thanked CM Yogi. Chose Judo over 800-meter race Asmita Dey, a resident of Belonia, Tripura, was initially an 800-meter runner. During a district-level trial, her interest in Judo grew. After that, she left athletics and made Judo her sport, continuously working hard. Asmita trained under the supervision of coach Yashpal Solanki at the Sports Authority of India (SAI) Regional Centre in Bhopal. Currently, she is part of the Development Group of the central government's Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) and is representing India at the international level. Had to stay hungry to maintain weight Asmita also shared the struggle of random weigh-in (weight check) before the championship match. She said that she had to stay hungry in the morning. She said she couldn't eat much because, in a random weigh-in, as the weight should be less than 50 kg. When she woke up in the morning, her weight was 50 kg 300 grams and so she didn't eat anything. When her name came up for the random weigh-in, only then did she eat and drink after the formality was completed, and her fight was just one hour after that. stories.title: 10 CJP supporters arrested for vandalism BJP leader's car:2 Samajwadi Party's MLAs reach police station seeking their release in Prayagraj; Akhilesh alleges govt betrayal
stories.summary: Ten people allegedly involved in vandalism during a protest in support of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Prayagraj on July 25 were arrested by police on Monday. The accused were identified with the help of CCTV footage and videos. One of them is reportedly a resident of Mariyadih, an area once considered a stronghold of gangster Atiq Ahmed. All 10 accused were sent to jail late Monday evening. After learning about the arrests, Samajwadi Party Pratappur MLA Vijma Yadav and Soraon MLA Geeta Pasi reached the police station. They allegedly tried to pressure police to release the detained youths. Police, however, explained the situation to the MLAs and sent them back. Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav alleged that the government was going back on its promise that no action would be taken against students. He said, “When the central government had promised that no action would be taken against any student, then why is this deception happening?” Keshav Maurya: ‘If Samajwadi Party supporters are involved, they will face action’ Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya, who arrived in Prayagraj on Monday morning, said those involved in the NEET paper-related issue were not responsible for the vandalism. He said that if SP supporters had committed the acts during the protest, the matter would be investigated. Vandalism of vehicles belonging to BJP leaders and others was reported in Prayagraj on July 25. Three FIRs have been registered in connection with the vandalism of a Fortuner, including charges of attempted murder and other offences. All 10 accused are between 18 and 26 years old Police said the arrested accused are aged between 18 and 26 years. One of them, identified as Dilshad, is a resident of Mariyadih. During the protest, he was allegedly seen moving around the protest site in a black Thar. The vehicle had no registration number and had black film on its windows. During questioning, Dilshad reportedly told police that he runs a milk-selling business. When asked why he had come to the protest site, he allegedly remained silent. Samajwadi Party MLA says, ‘No innocent person should be framed’ SP MLA Vijma Yadav said some of the detained youths belonged to her constituency. She said family members approached her and claimed that police had forcibly picked up their children. She then reached the police station and asked police why the youths had been detained. Yadav also requested that no innocent person should be implicated in the case. Akhilesh alleges police picked up students At around 6 pm on Monday, Akhilesh Yadav posted a video alleging that several students had been picked up by a special UP Police team in vehicles without registration numbers in the name of the Prayagraj protest. He demanded the immediate release of all detained students and called for the suspension and strict action against police personnel and senior officials allegedly involved in what he termed an illegal operation. However, DCP Manish Kumar Shandilya said none of the arrested people was students. He said CCTV footage and videos clearly showed the accused vandalising property and creating disorder, and that action had been taken against them based on evidence. Keshav Maurya: ‘Those committing crimes will be dealt with strictly’ Deputy CM Keshav Maurya said on Monday that if SP supporters were found guilty during the investigation, strict action would be taken against them. He said the SP, which has repeatedly faced defeat in elections, should not attempt to use violence as a means of political protest. Maurya said the government had adopted different approaches toward students and troublemakers. According to him, the government had decided to withdraw cases against students who had raised concerns over the alleged paper leak. However, he said those involved in criminal activities would not be spared. Maurya said the government respected the sentiments of students and understood young people’s concerns over serious issues such as paper leaks. However, he added that violence, vandalism and attempts to disturb law and order under the cover of protests would not be tolerated. Vehicles vandalised during July 25 protest Students in Prayagraj had also held a protest in support of the CJP movement at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar. On July 25, after Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation, a large gathering of students and young people assembled in the Civil Lines area. During the protest, some people allegedly vandalised a Fortuner, and a video of the incident later went viral on social media. Rohit Dwivedi, son of former MP Ramesh Chandra Dwivedi, alleged that his Fortuner was vandalised and that an attempt was also made to kill his driver. In another case, BJP leader Prashant Pathak from Rewa alleged that his vehicle was vandalised and a computer was taken away. FIRs have been registered in both cases.

stories.title: 'Azam’s university will not be demolished', says Moradabad Commissioner:Stay imposed on Rampur DM’s order; hearing was scheduled for tomorrow
stories.summary: The proposed bulldozer action against Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan’s Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur has been stayed. Moradabad Divisional Commissioner Anjaneya Kumar Singh has granted interim relief to the university and stayed the implementation of the demolition order issued by the Rampur District Magistrate (DM). A hearing in the case is scheduled at the Moradabad Commissioner’s office on July 28, but it could not be held due to a mourning holiday. RDA alleged 38 of 40 buildings were constructed without approved maps The Rampur Development Authority (RDA) had alleged that 38 of the university’s 40 buildings were constructed without approved building maps. On July 15, the university was served a notice ordering demolition. The order stated that the university administration should demolish the buildings itself, failing which the RDA would take action. The university was given 15 days before the demolition action could be carried out. Meanwhile, Nikhat Aflak Khan, chairperson and trustee of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, filed a petition before the court of Moradabad Divisional Commissioner Anjaneya Kumar Singh. Although the hearing was scheduled for July 28, the commissioner granted interim relief based on an application submitted by the university and stayed implementation of the demolition order on Monday evening. Tazeen Fatima Objected to Police Presence at University After the demolition order was issued, Azam Khan’s wife, Dr Tazeen Fatima, reached Jauhar University at around 2 pm on July 16. She became angry after seeing police personnel inside the university campus. Fatima said they had a clear court order granting them 15 days and questioned why the police and administration were entering and staying inside the university premises. She alleged that the entire action was being carried out with malicious intent. Fatima then had the police personnel deployed on duty removed from the university premises. She subsequently went to her office on the university campus, where she met university management members and Samajwadi Party leaders. They discussed a strategy to counter the RDA’s action and also sought advice on challenging the DM’s order in court. SP delegation of 45 leaders met DM On July 23, a delegation of 45 Samajwadi Party leaders, including 20 sitting and former MLAs, met Rampur DM Ajay Kumar Dwivedi under the leadership of SP Leader of Opposition Mata Prasad Pandey. The delegation demanded that the proposed bulldozer action against the university be stopped. Two days later, on July 25, another delegation of 10 MPs reached Rampur. It included Kairana MP Iqra Hasan, Sambhal MP Ziaur Rahman Barq and Moradabad MP Ruchi Veera. The MPs first visited the university and met students sitting in protest. They later met the DM and demanded that the action against the university be stopped. Iqra Hasan: ‘We will put our heads in place of every brick’ During the visit, MP Iqra Hasan said SP legislators had already met the DM and assured the people of Rampur and Azam Khan that they would not allow Jauhar University to be demolished. She said, “If necessary, we will put our heads in place of every brick, but we will not let anything happen to it.” Hasan said Jauhar University was built by Azam Khan and would not be allowed to be demolished at any cost. She added that the delegation would ask the DM to ensure that the university remains intact and suffers no damage. Moradabad MP Ruchi Veera also said they would not allow the university to be demolished under any circumstances. Calling it a “temple of education,” Veera said the demolition order was wrong. She added that if the DM did not accept their demand, they would approach senior officials and, if necessary, the court. How did Azam Khan miss getting the building maps approved? The Rampur Development Authority included Seengan Khedi village within its jurisdiction in March 2026. Jauhar University is located in this village. Before that, the village came under the district panchayat. The Rampur district panchayat’s development fee ranged from ₹100 to ₹300 per square metre. According to the report, if Azam Khan had got the building maps approved before March 2026, maps for all the university buildings could have been approved for approximately ₹5-6 crore. However, he failed to do so. A senior architect said that regardless of whether Azam Khan approaches a higher court, he would still have to approach the Rampur Development Authority to get the university’s building maps approved. The architect said an appeal against an RDA order can also be filed before the Moradabad Commissioner, who is the authority’s chairman. The university’s appeal has been filed under this process. Azam founded Jauhar Trust in 2003, Mulayam cabinet laid university foundation In 2003, Azam Khan became a minister in the Mulayam Singh Yadav government, holding portfolios including Parliamentary Affairs, Urban Development, Employment, Water Supply and Poverty Alleviation. This was the period when Azam Khan’s political influence in Rampur began to grow significantly. That same year, the SP leader established the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust, with members of his family also made trustees. In 2005, Azam Khan decided to establish Mohammad Ali Jauhar University under the Jauhar Trust. He wanted it to become Uttar Pradesh’s largest educational institution. Then Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav, along with his entire cabinet, visited Rampur on September 18, 2005, when the foundation stone of Jauhar University was laid. These developments took place during the Mulayam Singh government between 2005 and 2007, and later during the Akhilesh Yadav government between 2012 and 2015. University had 25 courses by 2017 By 2017, the university had started offering 25 courses, including BA, BSc, BTech and BPharma. A total of 58 separate, large buildings were constructed on the university campus for these courses. During the SP government, the Labour Department estimated their total cost at approximately ₹2,000 crore. The Akhilesh Yadav government ended in March 2017, and Yogi Adityanath became Chief Minister. According to the report, action against Azam Khan’s Jauhar University intensified after the BJP government came to power. 30 of 90 cases against Azam linked to Jauhar University According to the report, 90 cases have been registered against Azam Khan in Rampur, of which 30 are related to Jauhar University. The university is spread over approximately 1,500 bighas of land. Legal disputes over land purchased for the university have continued. The university has faced continuous administrative and legal action for the past seven years.

stories.title: Jobs of 67,000 UP teachers safe:Government in Supreme Court says new eligible candidates will fill vacant posts
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government on Monday filed an affidavit in the Supreme Court in the 69,000-Assistant Teacher Recruitment case. It informed the court that the jobs of 67,867 teachers appointed in 2020 would not be affected. If any new candidates are found eligible under the revised merit list, prepared in accordance with the High Court's directions, they will be appointed against vacant posts. At around 11 am, the government also told the court that the proposed arrangement would be restricted to the 69,000 teacher recruitment case and would not serve as a precedent for future recruitment exercises. Background of the case The government stated that a Government Order issued on 1 December 2018 approved the recruitment of 69,000 assistant teachers for council-run primary schools. The recruitment process was conducted under the Uttar Pradesh Basic Education (Teachers) Service Rules, 1981. The Assistant Teacher Recruitment Examination (ATRE)-2019 was held on 6 January 2019. A day later, on 7 January 2019, the government fixed the minimum qualifying marks at 65% for the General category and 60% for reserved categories. The decision was challenged before the Allahabad High Court, but on 6 May 2020, the court upheld the government's decision. Subsequently, on 18 November 2020, the Supreme Court also dismissed all appeals and upheld the High Court's verdict. Following this, on 1 June 2020, the government published a selection list of 67,867 candidates based on quality points. However, 1,133 posts reserved for the Scheduled Tribe (ST) category remained vacant due to the non-availability of eligible candidates. Dispute over Meritorious Reserved Category After the selection list was published, several candidates approached the High Court. One group argued that Meritorious Reserved Category (MRC) candidates had not been properly accommodated in the General category. MRC candidates are SC, ST or OBC candidates who score above the General category cut-off. Under Supreme Court rulings, such candidates are to be counted against General category seats. The opposing side argued that reserved category candidates who qualified the TET or ATRE after availing the 5% relaxation should not be treated as General category candidates. Meanwhile, following the Supreme Court's order of 18 November 2020, all 67,867 selected candidates were appointed and have been teaching in government schools ever since. Second list of 6,800 candidates put on hold The government said it issued a second selection list of 6,800 candidates on 5 January 2022, but the Allahabad High Court stayed its implementation on 27 January 2022. The stay was later continued in a special appeal on 15 March 2022. Conflicting High Court rulings On 13 March 2023, a Single Bench of the Allahabad High Court ruled that reserved category candidates who had scored more than 60% but less than 65% would not receive migration benefits to the General category. Such candidates would only be appointed against reserved category vacancies. The court directed the government to revise the 1 June 2020 selection list and cancel the 5 January 2022 second list. It also observed that the government could frame a separate policy if necessary for teachers who might lose their jobs. However, on 13 August 2024, the High Court's Division Bench set aside the Single Bench's order. The Division Bench directed that a fresh merit list for all 69,000 posts be prepared. Merit was to be determined first on the basis of quality points, after which reservation rules would be applied. Reserved category candidates who qualified on General merit were to be counted in the General category, followed by the implementation of horizontal reservation for categories such as women, persons with disabilities, ex-servicemen and transgender candidates. The court also said that if any serving teacher was affected by the revised merit list, they should be granted session benefit so that students' education was not disrupted. Supreme Court stayed the revised merit list Several candidates challenged the High Court's Division Bench judgment before the Supreme Court. On 9 September 2024, the Supreme Court granted an interim stay on the preparation of the revised merit list and directed that no action be taken on the High Court's order. It also sought written responses from all parties. The Uttar Pradesh government informed the Supreme Court that during the hearing on 4 February 2026, the court had suggested a possible resolution. After reconsidering the matter, the government informed the court on 19 May 2026 that it was willing to appoint newly eligible candidates against available vacancies if they were included in the revised merit list. However, it laid down three conditions: The Supreme Court subsequently granted the government six weeks to complete the exercise and directed it to submit a status report. Revised merit list prepared The government informed the court that, in compliance with the Supreme Court's directions and the Allahabad High Court's 13 August 2024 judgment, it had prepared the revised merit list. In its affidavit filed before the Supreme Court on 20 July 2026, the government said it had prepared a proposal to accommodate newly eligible candidates included in the revised merit list against available vacant posts, ensuring that the services of the 67,867 teachers already in service remain unaffected. The government told the Supreme Court that it would fully comply with the court's final judgment and was prepared to implement a balanced solution that safeguards the jobs of serving teachers while also providing appointments to newly eligible candidates.

stories.title: Woman PCS officer threatened inside office:Man warns she won't be allowed to live in Prayagraj if ruling doesn't go in his favour
stories.summary: A shocking case has emerged in Prayagraj where Additional Commissioner Jayjeet Kaur was verbally abused and threatened in her office. The Additional Commissioner alleges that a young man, along with his associates, barged into her office. The accused threatened that if the decision in an ongoing matter does not go in his favour, he would not let the Additional Commissioner live in Prayagraj. When she didn't comply, the accused used abusive language and threatened to kill her. Karnalganj police registered an FIR on Monday morning against one named person and 12 unknown individuals. Now read the full story Jaijeet Kaur is posted as Additional Commissioner (Judicial) in Prayagraj. She told the police, "My office is located in the Commissioner's Office complex. On the morning of July 17, around 11 AM, Pawan Kumar Vishwakarma, a resident of Handia, came to my office with 10 to 12 of his associates. He started asking me to rule in his favour in a pending case. To this, I said that any case would be resolved only based on its merits and available evidence. Hearing this, Pawan and his associates became agitated. They abused me and threatened to 'deal with me'. Not only this, Pawan and his associates also raised slogans in the Commissioner's Office complex. This disrupted government work for some time. Two cases already; Goonda Act also applied Jaijeet Kaur also stated in her complaint that another case is already registered against Pawan in Handia under sections related to assault, abuse, threatening, and the Excise Act. Charge sheets have also been filed in both cases. In 2022, action was also recommended against him under the UP Goonda Control Act. The woman officer expressed apprehension in her complaint that some criminal incident might occur against her. DCP Manish Kumar Shandilya said, "An FIR has been registered based on the complaint. Investigation is being conducted using the CCTV footage installed in the office premises." Jayjeet Kaur is the topper of UPPSC 2016 batch 42-year-old Jayjeet Kaur has been the topper of the UPPSC 2016 batch. She is a resident of Kanpur. After completing B.Tech from IET College, Lucknow, she pursued her MBA from Mumbai. Before passing the PCS examination, she was working in the IT sector. Encouraged by her husband Ashutosh, she quit her job and started preparing for PCS. She then topped in her very first attempt. In the same year, her husband Ashutosh was also selected in PCS. Jayjeet's father Sarvjeet Singh is a businessman. Her two sisters-in-law, Vibha and Pooja, are also PCS officers. Jayjeet Kaur was posted as Additional Commissioner Judicial in Prayagraj in March. Before Prayagraj, she had also been posted in Lucknow and Ayodhya.

stories.title: Women stop Minister Dayashankar's convoy, raise 'Murdabad' slogans:Demand written assurances as he visits flood-hit Ballia
stories.summary: State minister Dayashankar Singh has faced strong criticism in his own constituency. On Sunday, Dayashankar arrived with a convoy to meet villagers protesting in a flood-affected area in his constituency. As soon as the minister's convoy entered the village, hundreds of villagers surrounded the minister's car. They started chanting "Dayashankar Singh Murdabad" (Dayashankar Singh die). Seeing the sudden protest, the minister remained seated in his car for a long time. During this time, the policemen in his security detail were trying to appease the villagers with folded hands. Somehow, the police managed to calm the crowd. Only then was Dayashankar able to get out of the car. The incident took place on Sunday afternoon in Byasi village, Bairia area, Sadar constituency of Ballia. Here, due to the overflowing Ganga river, agricultural land has been eroded. Villagers had been protesting for six days at a temple in the village regarding this issue. See 2 pictures of the erosion- What is visible in the video? The video that has surfaced shows Dayashankar sitting in a car. A crowd of over 200 people outside are chanting 'Muradabad' slogans. Meanwhile, policemen are removing villagers who are trying to stop his car. After this, Dayashankar somehow got out of the car. The women started shouting that they don't need assurance. “Give it in writing”, the crowd shouted. After this, people accompanying the minister explained to the villagers not to make noise. Villagers angered by minister's verbal assurance Amidst heavy protest, Minister Dayashankar got out of the car. He met with the protesters. He assured them that the problem would be resolved soon. However, when he started to leave, the villagers flared up again. The villagers started shouting, "Don't make a verbal promise, promise it in writing." The protest continued for about 20 minutes. The women said that every year the Ganges is swallowing their land and many families are forced to leave everything behind. During this time, Dayashankar remained mostly silent. He said, "Give me time. Everyone's work will be done." Why were the villagers so angry? Actually, erosion has been occurring on the banks of the Ganga and Saryu rivers in Ballia for about 10 days. Houses and a primary school in several villages, including Shivpur Diyar Nambari, have been swallowed by the river. Villagers claim that more than 50 bighas of crops have been submerged. A large number of people are being forced to leave their homes. This is why people are angry. Villagers told the minister - Go to the erosion site When Dayashankar met the protesting people and was about to leave, the villagers told him to go towards the cutting. However, the minister got into his car and left from there. The villagers say that permanent arrangements should be made to stop the cutting.

stories.title: Maid steals iPhone, caught on CCTV:Hired to look after child in Ghaziabad, caught stealing on first day
stories.summary: In Ghaziabad, a maid stole an iPhone kept in the house where she was supposed to work. In just 5 seconds, she picked up the iPhone from the table and hid it in her clothes. When the owner asked, she said, "I don't know anything." Then she got angry at the owner and left. The owner searched the house extensively but couldn't find the phone. Later, they checked the CCTV. In it, the maid was seen stealing the phone. The owner filed a complaint with the police for an FIR along with the CCTV footage. The phone is said to be worth around ₹1.4 lakh. The entire incident is from Paramount Symphony Society in the Crossing Republic area. The incident occurred on Sunday evening at 4:31 PM. The CCTV footage came to light on Monday. The accused maid's name is Pooja (32). Police are searching for her. Crossing Republic Police Station in-charge Shweta Singh says: A complaint of iPhone theft has been received. The matter is being investigated. CCTV footage has also been provided. 2 Photos- Husband-Wife Working, Maid Hired to Take Care of 3-Year-Old Son Nitin Kumar lives in Paramount Symphony Society with his wife Shilpa Yadav. They have a 3-year-old son. Nitin is an engineer in a multinational company. Shilpa also works. They had hired a maid named Rajni to take care of their son. Rajni had gone on a 4-5 day leave. In such a situation, Nitin had temporarily hired Poonam alias Pooja, who worked in the same society, to look after his son. Since Pooja worked in nearby flats, they did not investigate much. Nitin had gone out of the flat for 10 minutes on Sunday. When he returned, he couldn't find his iPhone. He kept searching for a long time. Then he asked Pooja. She replied - Sir, we didn't find any phone. Later, when Nitin checked the CCTV installed in the house, Pooja's truth was revealed. Nitin's wife Shilpa stated in the complaint given to the police that Poonam had come to work at the flat for the first time on Sunday. This was the reason she did not know that CCTVs were installed in the house.

stories.title: 28-year-old man dies by suicide over marital dispute:Recorded video before death, father alleges wife was having an affair
stories.summary: In Unnao, a young man, troubled by his wife and brother-in-law, died by suicide by hanging himself. Before dying, the man made a four-minute video. In it, he said, "My wife and her aunt's son are responsible for my death. These people have ruined my life." After saying this, the young man tied a nylon rope to the tin shed rod and hanged himself. The incident occurred around 3:30 PM on Sunday in the Sadar Kotwali area. At the time of the incident, the deceased's parents were sitting near the house gate. A little later, when the father came inside for some work, he saw his son hanging from the noose. His eyes fell on the mobile phone kept on a nearby table, which was recording. He immediately stopped the recording and informed the police. The police arrived at the scene, brought the body down from the noose, and sent it to the district hospital for post-mortem. The incident was also reported to the deceased's in-laws, but no one came from there. They switched off their phones. The aggrieved father alleges that his daughter-in-law was having an affair with her paternal cousin. Based on his complaint, the police registered a case of abetment to suicide against the deceased's wife, mother-in-law, brother-in-law, sister-in-law, and paternal cousin brother-in-law. Now understand the whole matter in a sequential manner 'She used to say - if you die, I will walk over your dead body' Sanjay Rathore, the deceased's uncle, said that his daughter-in-law often fought with Pawan and used to say, "If you die, I will walk over your dead body." Fed up with the continuous harassment from his in-laws, he blamed his wife and brother-in-law for his death in the video. The family members have demanded that the police that all the accused should be given the strictest punishment and sent to jail based on the viral video and evidence. Fed up with harassment from in-laws, he took his own life Meanwhile, father Sunil alleged in his complaint filed at the police station that his daughter-in-law Ragini was having an affair with her paternal cousin Suraj Rathore. Her brother Ravi and sister Soni were also mentally harassing Pawan. Fed up with this harassment, the son took this horrific step. Magarwara Police Post In-charge Ravishankar Pandey says- The post-mortem of the body is being conducted. The matter is being thoroughly investigated based on viral videos, electronic evidence, and statements from family members. By connecting every link of the entire incident, the actual reasons for the suicide are being ascertained.

stories.title: Police stop students inside Lucknow University:Protesters insist on marching out, demand resignation of education ministers in 4 states
stories.summary: Following calls for the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union Education Minister, students are now demanding the resignation of the education ministers of four states. On Monday, students staged a protest at the University of Lucknow, demanding the resignation of the education ministers of Kerala, Jharkhand, Punjab and Karnataka. They attempted to march from the university gate onto the road, but police personnel deployed at the site stopped them and confined them inside the campus. The protesting students alleged that paper leaks were taking place in all states governed by non-NDA governments and said the respective education ministers should resign. They also criticised Opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav, Dimple Yadav and Arvind Kejriwal, for remaining silent over alleged paper leaks in Punjab, Karnataka, Kerala and Jharkhand. The students claimed that Kerala, Jharkhand and Punjab had witnessed paper leak incidents and argued that leaders of the respective parties or alliances should demand the resignation of their own education ministers. They gathered in large numbers at Gate No. 1 (Azad Gate) of the university at around 12 noon and raised slogans.

stories.title: Ram Mandir donation theft case:SC calls for a forensic auditor in SIT; UP govt says new team, led by IG Kiran S, is in place
stories.summary: Hearing the Ayodhya Ram Mandir offering theft case on Monday, the Supreme Court asked the Uttar Pradesh government to include a forensic auditor in the Special Investigation Team (SIT) constituted by the State to probe into the alleged financial irregularities of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust in Ayodhya. Before a Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohan, the Uttar Pradesh government submitted a status report. During the hearing, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta informed the court that the newly constituted Special Investigation Team (SIT) would be headed by Inspector General (IG) Kiran S. The team also includes a Deputy Inspector General (DIG), a Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) and an Additional Superintendent of Police (ASP). At the previous hearing on 20 July, the Supreme Court had directed the Uttar Pradesh government to constitute a fresh SIT and submit a report on the investigation carried out so far. In compliance with the court's directions, the government constituted the new SIT on Saturday, appointing Lucknow Range IG Kiran S. as its head. The earlier SIT had been led by IAS officer Vijay Vishwas Pant, with Kiran S. serving as one of its members. During the previous hearing, Chief Justice Surya Kant had directed that a fresh SIT be formed under the leadership of a senior IPS officer so that the investigation could reach a conclusive stage. During the hearing, the Chief Justice had also observed in strong terms: "We only want to caution that this sensitive matter should not be politicised. At first glance, it appears to be a criminal case. It must be investigated fairly, independently and with complete integrity." Meanwhile, all eight accused in the Ram Temple donation theft case are scheduled to appear before the Anti-Corruption Court today. Owing to security concerns, the hearing will be conducted via video conferencing. The accused — Ramshankar Yadav alias 'Tinnu', Anukalp Mishra, Avinash Shukla, Lavkush Mishra, Karunesh Pandey, Ramashankar Mishra, Manish Yadav and retired bank employee Subhash Srivastava — are currently in judicial custody.

stories.title: Akhilesh targets BJP over education, questions formation of task force:Ram Gopal says tougher law won't end paper leaks
stories.summary: During the Monsoon Session of Parliament today (Monday), the entire Opposition, including the Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Congress, raised the issues of the NEET paper leak and the police lathicharge on protesting students. Speaking to the media outside Parliament, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav said: “The government is filing cases against students and young people. It should not challenge the consciousness and spirit of the youth, because that very spirit has now become the government's biggest challenge.” Before the Lok Sabha proceedings began, Akhilesh Yadav said: “The Opposition is united. All the leaders of the INDIA alliance stand together. This is a major struggle. Ever since the BJP came to power, it has ruined the country's education system. I appreciate the morale and awareness of the youth. The task force that the government has now formed should have been constituted much earlier. What was the government doing from 2014 until now?” Meanwhile, the government introduced the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 in the Lok Sabha to strengthen measures against paper leaks. On the bill, Congress MP Pramod Tiwari said: "The issue is not just about making a law, but about the government's policy and intent. The real culprits behind this malpractice must not be spared under any circumstances." SP MP Ram Gopal Yadav also said: “Paper leaks cannot be stopped merely by enacting stricter laws. This entire problem has increased since the examination process became fully digital. When the system was not digital, such large-scale irregularities were not seen.”

stories.title: Scorpio collides with Ertiga, three brothers killed:Cow suddenly appears on highway in Hapur; Scorpio breaks divider and enters opposite lane
stories.summary: In a tragic incident, three brothers were killed after a collision between an Ertiga and a Scorpio in Uttar Pradesh's Hapur district. Nine people travelling in both cars were injured in the incident. The mishap took place on the Delhi-Lucknow Highway on Sunday night at 9 PM. ASP Vinit Bhatnagar said, “A high-speed Scorpio coming from Delhi on the highway suddenly encountered a cow. In an attempt to save it, the Scorpio went out of control, overturned, broke the divider, and went into the other lane. Just then, it collided with an Ertiga car coming from the opposite direction.” The collision was so severe that the front part of the Ertiga was crushed. The Scorpio was torn to pieces. When screams erupted, people from nearby areas reached the spot. They informed the police. The police somehow cut the car with a gas cutter and pulled out the people. The injured were sent to the hospital, while the bodies were sent for post-mortem. In the accident, three real brothers, Abrar (48), Afzal (35), and Sarfaraz (40), residents of Mulla Colony, Ghazipur, Delhi, died. The accident occurred on Sunday night at 9 PM near Shyana Chaukhla, about 40 kilometers from the district headquarters. Ertiga occupants were returning from a wedding in Bijnor, having come from Delhi According to the police, there were 7 people in the Ertiga and 6 people in the Scorpio. All Ertiga occupants were returning after attending a wedding ceremony in Bijnor. Traffic was low on the highway at night, so the Ertiga's speed must have been around 100 km/h. Suddenly, a Scorpio, overturning from the other lane, appeared in front. After the collision, the Ertiga skidded for about 20 meters on the highway. The bonnets of both vehicles were crushed. The condition of 2 of the injured is serious. Among the injured are Istekhar, Shahbaz, Zubair, Sartaj, and others. ASP Vineet Bhatnagar said Three people have died and nine are injured in a head-on collision between two cars on the Delhi-Lucknow Highway. Upon receiving information about the accident, the police removed the damaged vehicles from the highway and normalized traffic. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem. An investigation is underway.

stories.title: Harassed by in-laws, woman slits her throat:Kanpur victim writhes in pool of blood, dies 20 hours later
stories.summary: Distressed by her in-laws in Kanpur, a woman slit her own throat with a knife. At 4 AM on Sunday, family members admitted her to a private hospital in a serious condition. Rukhsana (33) died during treatment around 12 AM late at midnight. Upon receiving information from the family, the police arrived, took the body into custody, and sent it for post-mortem. Police stated that further action would be taken upon receiving a complaint. The case is from the Narwal police station area. Marriage took place 16 years ago Rukhsana (33), a resident of Narwal, was married 16 years ago in 2009 to Yaseen, a resident of Mardan Naka, Banda. They also have a one-year-old daughter. Rukhsana's family members say that after the marriage, her husband Yaseen, mother-in-law Zinnat, father-in-law Imam Baksh, and brother-in-law Haseen were mentally and physically harassing their daughter. On January 10, 2025, her in-laws beat their daughter and threw her out of the house. “Along with this, the in-laws also took away our daughter's jewellery, clothes, and 'Stridhan' (woman's property). We tried to reconcile many times, but no solution was found,” Rukhsana's family said. Due to mental stress, Rukhsana stabbed herself in the neck with a knife around 4 AM on Sunday. Family members immediately took her to a private hospital, where she died late at night during treatment. Narwal Police Station in-charge Anil Kumar Singh said- Based on the complaint of the family members, the police will thoroughly investigate the matter and take necessary action.

stories.title: Grandparents and two grandchildren killed as speeding truck rams them:Initial investigation indicates driver fell asleep on the wheel
stories.summary: In Sant Kabir Nagar, UP, a truck ran over four members of a family on Monday morning. All of them were sitting outside their house when the speeding truck hit them. It ran over the grandfather, grandmother, grandson, and grand-nephew who were sitting on a cot. The truck's speed was about 60 kmph. As a result, no one had a chance to react. Hearing a sound like an explosion, people from the surrounding area reached the spot. Police used a crane to remove the truck and retrieve the bodies trapped underneath. The accident occurred at 5:30 AM on the Basti-Khalilabad highway, about 15 kilometers from the district headquarters. Lalji (62), his wife Gyanmati (60), grandson Adarsh (12), and grand-nephew Satyam (6) died in the incident. Initial investigation suggests that the accident was caused by the driver falling asleep. After the accident, the truck driver and cleaner fled the scene. Pictures of the accident: Details of the incident Near Kurthiya intersection in Khalilabad Kotwali area, by the highway, is a two-room house belonging to Lalji, son of Ganpat. A tin shed is installed in front of the house. In the morning, Lalji was sitting on a cot under the tin shed with his wife Gyanmati. A little later, grandson Adarsh and maternal grandson Satyam, who were sleeping in the room inside, also woke up and came out. Satyam, son of Rajesh, resident of Pakri Araji, Dudhara police station, had come to his maternal grandfather's house just two days ago. Meanwhile, a truck going towards Basti lost control and veered off the highway. It crushed the cot and went 30 meters further. Screams erupted at the scene. Family members sleeping inside came out. Upon receiving information, Additional SP, CO, Kotwal, and Traffic Inspector reached the spot. Police rescued the people trapped under the truck.

stories.title: Auto driver abandons three children in Varanasi:Tells shopkeeper their mother is standing behind; police search for family
stories.summary: On Sunday evening, around 4 PM in Varanasi, some people riding in an auto rickshaw dropped off three children at a shop and fled. When the shopkeeper asked the auto driver whose children they were, he said their mother was standing behind them. After that, he absconded. When the police asked the children for their names and addresses, they could not tell. After this, the police searched the surrounding area. As no correct information was found, all three children have been sent to a juvenile home. The police are searching for the families of the three children. According to the shopkeeper, the people in the auto rickshaw seemed like child kidnappers. The incident occurred in Nehiya Bazaar, under Gosainpur police outpost, in the Cholapur police station area. Dropped off in Nehiya Bazaar and fled Chola Pur police station in-charge Inspector Jagdish Singh said, “An auto-rickshaw arrived near a tea shop in Nehiya Bazaar. The person sitting in it made three children, a boy and two girls, get down from the auto. When he started to leave after dropping the children, the shopkeeper stopped him and asked who the children were and why he had dropped them there. To this, the auto-rickshaw driver said that their mother was standing behind. She is coming. Saying this much, he left.” When no one arrived for a long time, the shopkeeper asked the children for their names and address. The children could only tell their names: Rakesh (7), Chhoti (6), and Chanchal (5). They could not tell their home address. After this, the shopkeeper informed Dial 112. Shopkeeper could not see the number plate, CCTV footage being scanned The in-charge inspector said, “When we received information from Dial 112, we reached the spot. When the children were questioned, they could not tell anything. The shopkeeper also could not see the auto-rickshaw's number in a hurry. Nearby CCTV footage is being scanned.” The children have been sent to the juvenile home, and information has been sent from the control room to all police stations in the district to search for their families. In addition, nearby districts have also been alerted.

stories.title: Six arrested for ATM cash theft in Varanasi:Accused came from Fatehpur, used iron plates to withdraw money
stories.summary: Varanasi's Bhelupur police have busted a gang that defrauded people by manipulating ATMs. In a press conference on Sunday evening, the police stated that this gang prevents cash from coming out by placing an iron plate at the cash dispensing slot of the ATM. When the ATM user leaves frustrated, the gang would easily remove the plate and take out the cash. As many as six gang members – all residents of Fatehpur – have been arrested. They had been active in Varanasi for a long time. Suspects seen in SBI ATM ADCP Kashi Vaibhav Bangar said, “Satyendra Sharma, Channel Executive of Hitachi Company, had filed an FIR at Bhelupur police station. His company operates and maintains SBI ATMs.” On the night of July 23, some suspects were captured on CCTV at an SBI ATM located in the Kakarmatta area. A complaint of money getting stuck had come from this ATM. However, the investigation revealed that the money was not stuck, but had been withdrawn. Arrest made based on CCTV footage ADCP Kashi said, “Police have arrested six accused from BHU Colony Baijnattha Birdopur based on more than 100 CCTV cameras. All of them are between 18 and 24 years of age.” The arrested accused Himanshu Singh, Adarsh Kumar, Sachin Kumar, Abhay Rajput, Rajkumar, and Prince Kumar are all residents of Fatehpur district. As much as ₹39,800 has been recovered from them. They used to commit fraud with an iron plate During interrogation, the arrested accused Adarsh Kumar said, “We used to place an iron plate at the ATM where money comes out. We would then attach a thick paper in front of it with tape. This prevented the money from falling out. It would stop on the plate itself. When the person would leave frustrated, we would remove the plate, and the money would come out with it. We used to do this work at ATMs located in deserted areas at night." Four iron plates, 1 white tape, and 1 thick black paper were recovered from the arrested thieves.

stories.title: Woman molested in Gorakhpur:Accused bites victim's brother's nose and ear after accused barges into home, breaks CCTV; FIR filed
stories.summary: A youth has been accused of molesting a woman in Gorakhpur's Kotwali police station area. The accused reportedly attacked the victim's brother when he tried to intervene. The accused also broke CCTV cameras at the house of the victim to destroy evidence. Based on the complaint filed by the victim's side, the police registered a case on July 26, around 9 PM, under serious sections including sexual harassment. The victim stated in the complaint given to the Kotwali police that Himanshu Gupta, from the same neighbourhood, came to their house on Sunday evening and tried to molest a woman of the house. He also tried to touch the women in inappropriate places. It is alleged that when they received information and arrived to intervene, Himanshu launched a deadly attack on them. During this, he attacked their younger brother. It is alleged that the accused bit the brother near his nose and ear, severely injuring him and drawing blood. He also hurled abusive language. CCTVs broken to destroy evidence The victim states that Himanshu broke all the CCTV cameras installed in the house to destroy evidence of his act. When she tried to defend herself, he also broke all the household items. The victim told the police that complaints have been lodged against the accused many times before at the police station, but each time he gets away. After coming out, he again launches a deadly attack and threatens to kill. In the complaint, the victim wrote that the entire neighbourhood is troubled by this boy's mischief and everyone is ready to testify against him. The residents of the neighbourhood have demanded from the police that strict action be taken against the accused so that no other woman can be safe in the future. The police are thoroughly investigating the matter. Police started investigation Kotwali Police Station In-charge Chatrapal Singh said that a case has been registered based on the complaint. The investigation has been handed over to Sub-Inspector Bhavesh Kumar Singh. Further action will be taken based on the victim's allegations and the medical report. Raids are being conducted to arrest the accused.

stories.title: Family's joy turns to grief after speedboat crash:Youth dies from head injury in Gorakhpur's Ramgarh Tal
stories.summary: One man died while several people sustained injuries in the speedboat collision at Ramgarh Tal in Gorakhpur's boating area. Lakhmuddin, 21, died from a head injury in the accident. The deceased's entire family had come from Kushinagar for a visit on Sunday night. After this accident, their happiness turned into mourning. There were nine people on the boat that was hit, while there were 6 people on the other. After the incident, all the injured were taken to the district hospital. Five were immediately discharged, while one died and two are serious. Their treatment is ongoing. Police are engaged in finding out the real cause for negligence in this entire incident. Action will be taken after investigating every point in the matter. Also, some necessary rules will be made for boating. See pictures The details of the case On Sunday, late in the evening around 6 PM, a family from Kushinagar came to Gorakhpur for sightseeing. Around 8 PM, they reached Nauka Vihar. After wandering around for a while, everyone decided to go boating. Tickets for the entire family were purchased at Platform No. 5. The children were extremely excited for the boat ride. Everyone sat on the boat. As soon as it started, it had just begun to move when suddenly a speed boat coming from Platform No. 4 collided with it forcefully. This caused screams and shouts at the scene. The security personnel present immediately carried out rescue operations and pulled everyone out. Police, who arrived upon receiving the information, took everyone to the district hospital. There, doctors declared Lakhimuddin dead. Meanwhile, five of the other injured sustained minor injuries. They were sent home after primary treatment. Two others, Qayamuddin and his son Hazma, are admitted. Upon hearing the news of the death, the family erupted in cries. Relatives started weeping. The lives of 15 people were put at risk simultaneously. In this incident, the boat that was hit had nine people on board. While the boat that caused the collision had six people. Thus, the lives of 15 people were simultaneously endangered. Police will conduct medical tests on the drivers. After this incident, the administrative machinery is in full action mode. DM, SP, GDA officials, and others immediately reached the spot. Police detained the driver of one boat. Teams have been formed to search for the other. The police will conduct medical examinations of both to ascertain if they were riding under the influence of alcohol. Additionally, an FIR has been registered against both drivers following a complaint from the family. Preparations are also underway to cancel their licenses. Post-mortem will confirm the real cause of death Additionally, a post-mortem examination of the deceased's body will be conducted to ascertain the real cause behind the death. However, at first glance, the cause of death appears to be a head injury sustained from the boat collision. Police will investigate whose fault caused the collision Police are investigating whose fault caused the collision in this accident, whether there was any prior problem with the boat, whether any driver consumed alcohol, and other reasons. For this, drivers are being interrogated. Further investigation and action underway, says SP City Giving information, SP City Nimish Patil stated that no boat capsized in the incident. Lakhimuddin sustained a head injury in the collision, which led to the youth's death. One driver has been apprehended. A team has been formed to search for the other. An FIR has been registered against both drivers and further action is being taken. A similar accident also occurred last year On July 22, 2025, too, a similar accident occurred around 6 PM. In which husband Ramashish, wife Anjali, and son Himanshu were injured. At that time too, a boat was departing from platform number six when a boat returning to platform number five collided with it. Ramashish sustained a serious leg injury upon falling into the water. Anjali was also injured. Their son had to get stitches on his head. The investigation revealed that the boat driver had consumed alcohol. The entire family had come from Khorabar for sightseeing. The boat that collided also had 8 people on board. However, they narrowly escaped. Naukavihar is an excellent tourist spot The city's Naukavihar is an excellent tourist spot. It is a major centre of attraction for city residents. Most tourists visiting Gorakhpur go there. Whether it's New Year, a festival, or a holiday, it gets very crowded. Additionally, hundreds of people gather here daily, from morning walks to refreshing their mood in the evening. People come here to make reels, videos, selfies, and photos. It's an excellent place for families, friends, and everyone. They also enjoy boating along with the cruise and floating restaurant built in Ramgarh Tal.

stories.summary: Monsoon is set to regain strength in Uttar Pradesh from today, Monday. Since morning, skies have remained cloudy over more than 40 cities, including Lucknow, Kanpur and Ayodhya. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts of the state. Very heavy rainfall has been forecast for Lakhimpur and Bahraich, and people have been advised to step out only if necessary. Meanwhile, rivers across Uttar Pradesh are in spate due to torrential rain in the hills. At around 7 am on Monday, a government school in Ballia was swept away by the overflowing Saryu River. The entire building collapsed into the river's strong current within just three seconds. Half of the school had already come under erosion on Sunday. In another incident, hundreds of acres of paddy fields were submerged after the embankment of the Doharighat canal breached. On Sunday, heavy rain lashed Lucknow, Kanpur, Noida and Bijnor. In Unnao, a section of the Lucknow–Kanpur Greenfield National Elevated Expressway caved in. The NHAI team reached the spot soon after receiving the information and repaired the damaged stretch. Separately, an international flight bound for Kathmandu was diverted to Lucknow due to bad weather. Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said: "The monsoon trough is once again moving towards Uttar Pradesh. At the same time, the low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal is strengthening further. As a result, both eastern and western parts of the state are likely to receive good rainfall. Until 30 July, many districts of Uttar Pradesh may witness light to moderate rain, while some places could receive heavy rainfall. There is also a possibility of thunderstorms and lightning in some areas during this period." See where rain is likely across the state today.

stories.title: 5 held responsible for death of 6-year-old child in Noida:Authority CEO never inspected site; contractor allegedly acted unchecked
stories.summary: 6-year-old Avyan died after drowning in a water-filled pit in Greater Noida. Avyan's family lives in the posh society Kaladham in the Knowledge Park-2 area. He was playing cricket outside his house on Saturday at 6:30 PM. While playing, he reached near the pit. Due to mud around the area, he slipped and fell into the pit and died. This pit was 15 feet deep, which was dug by the Greater Noida Development Authority for boring purposes. After the child's death, the administration installed barricading around the pit. The Authority has filed an FIR against contractor Manoj Jain, contract employee supervisor Johnny, and technical supervisor Akash. Their services have been terminated. The police have arrested all three. Avyan's father, Shivan Yadav, is a Vice Principal at Kendriya Vidyalaya. He is asking who is responsible for this? What was my son's fault? Why did my family and I receive punishment for someone's negligence? My family and I received punishment for someone else's mistake. Whose fault was this? That we had to bear the consequences. The Dainik Bhaskar team went to the ground and spoke to people. Spoke to the child's family. Understood the matter by talking to officials and employees associated with the authority. In the initial investigation, negligence of 5 officials has come to light. Read the report The CEO of Greater Noida Authority is NG Ravi Kumar. His job is to supervise all the work happening in the notified area of Greater Noida Authority. To give instructions to officers. To oversee projects. But, no information was obtained about the pit being dug for the borewell in Kaladham Society. Its progress was not inquired about. Consequently, the location of the pit to be dug in the society was changed, and it was dug up to 15 feet. They were not informed about this. As a result, the child lost his life. After this, their sleep was broken, and they realized their responsibility. The CEO says that my subordinates did not give me any information about the pit. After the accident, Greater Noida Authority's General Manager AK Singh came forward. He stated that it was not the Authority's responsibility, because this was the society's work. The work was started only at the request of the society's people. This tubewell was supposed to be installed 200 meters from here towards the drain. After the work was approved, the contractor said that there are eight trees where the pits need to be dug. Please remove them. We also wrote a letter seven days ago to remove the trees. In the meantime, our staff came. What discussion happened with the contractor? What discussion happened with the people here about how the location was changed? We did not have information about this. After the Yuvraj incident in Noida, there were clear instructions that before doing any work, there should be strong safety arrangements. After this, negligence was committed. This was not done here. There was no barricading here. There was no signboard either, nor was there a board to be put up at the site. The responsibility for this was with Senior Manager Vinod Kumar Sharma and Assistant Manager Manoj Chaudhary. They were supposed to go to the site and check whether standards were being followed in the work or not. But no officer went to the site. The CEO of the authority also admitted this during the investigation. After which the CEO issued instructions to all work circles that work should be started only after implementing all barricading and safety measures. In this incident, the authority's technical supervisor Akash Kumar and supervisor Johnny Kumar played a significant role. Neither of them even informed senior officials about the pit being dug for this borewell. Also, the location where the pit was to be dug for the borewell was changed. Neither of them did not inform their officers about this. They also did not check whether the work was being done according to the prescribed rules and safety standards or not. A borewell was to be constructed in the society to improve water supply. The work was started three days ago. The contract was awarded to Manoj Jain. The project file was prepared, and work began after the officers' signatures. Within three days, a pit was dug at a different location. The contractor did not follow the prescribed rules. Safety standards were disregarded. Daily progress reports were not submitted to senior officers. Consequently, no officer in authority was even aware that such a deep pit had been dug in the society. Action taken in the case so far Know what questions the child's father asked in the FIR Now read the complete case- Had gone to play near the park with friends Shivan Yadav lived in Kaladham Society with his wife and two sons. He is a Vice Principal in Kendriya Vidyalaya. The elder son is 9 years old. Avyan was 6 years old. In the evening, he was playing with friends in an open area 100 meters away from home. While playing, the child reached near the pit. Due to the mud around, he slipped and fell into the pit. The children playing with him raised an alarm. People from nearby came running. Somehow, Avyan was pulled out. He was taken to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead.

stories.title: How big a game changer is 'NEET movement':Rahul and Akhilesh unite at Jantar Mantar; will it translate into political gains in UP?
stories.summary: The ‘two boys’ alliance had failed in the 2017 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, but the 2024 Lok Sabha results gave the Rahul Gandhi–Akhilesh Yadav partnership renewed momentum. Now, their joint offensive over the NEET issue, from Jantar Mantar to Parliament, has become the latest talking point. The growing coordination between the two leaders is also beginning to shape the political narrative in Uttar Pradesh, with both the Congress and the Samajwadi Party taking to the streets in support of students. The key question now is: Can the Rahul–Akhilesh alliance, built around the anger of young people over the NEET issue, become a game changer for the Opposition in Uttar Pradesh? Or will the BJP, backed by its organisational strength and incumbency, will be able to blunt the challenge? Alliance was in crisis due to the rhetoric of UP's boastful leaders In the 2024 UP Lok Sabha elections, the SP-Congress alliance caused the most political damage to the BJP. Both parties have already agreed to contest together in 2027 as well. However, there is a deadlock between the two parties over seat sharing. In recent days, statements from Congress MP Imran Masood to UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam regarding this seat sharing had garnered much attention. Both leaders claimed that Congress would negotiate for equal seats with SP in the UP Assembly elections. Rajendra Pal Gautam even went so far as to call Congress the big brother of SP in UP. Students' protest at Jantar Mantar changed the chronology The dharna of Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) started at Jantar Mantar on June 20. The monsoon session that began on July 20 took this movement to its peak. Rahul Gandhi was the first to join this students' movement. The next day, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav also joined this protest along with MPs. The coordination between both young leaders was visible from the streets to Parliament and even going to jail. Inside Parliament, both parties strongly demanded a discussion on issues like NEET from the government and did not let Parliament function. On July 21, Rahul staged a dharna at the PM's residence. Akhilesh Yadav also joined this dharna with his MPs. Along with Rahul and other Congress leaders, Akhilesh Yadav and other SP leaders were also arrested. Impact of Rahul-Akhilesh's arrest was most visible in UP The impact of Akhilesh-Rahul's arrest was most visible in UP. Here, SP-Congress leaders and workers staged massive protests from Lucknow to different districts. There were clashes with police at several places. Many Congress-SP leaders were arrested. Student organizations of both parties were seen at the forefront in these protests. Sources associated with both parties say that SP-Congress are preparing to hold similar protest demonstrations during the monsoon session of the Assembly as well. This will include issues like Shri Ram Temple offerings, fertilizer shortage, fake medicines and increased electricity load. Strategy to keep unemployment, paper leak issues alive till UP elections Akhilesh standing with Rahul is particularly important for UP politics. Because SP's main vote bank is in UP. Congress is trying to increase its reach among youth and urban middle class at the national level. Both parties have been continuously raising issues like unemployment and paper leaks in UP as well. After the NEET controversy, both parties are now vocal on the issue of unemployment. In such a situation, their effort will certainly be to keep these issues alive till the elections. BJP has been in power in UP for the last two terms. NDA suffered a setback in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, but the by-election results showed that its strength remains intact. Congress had not contested even a single seat then. These results make it clear that only the Akhilesh-Rahul combination can challenge the BJP in the 2027 assembly elections. First, the Muslim-Yadav equation is SP's strong base. Second, if Congress manages to make inroads into Brahmin, Dalit and youth votes, then the prospects of the alliance will increase. Why does this pair matter in UP? Senior journalist Yogesh Mishra answers this by saying - In 2027, the BJP will be in elections for a third term. In such a situation, three scenarios can emerge... First- It is obvious that there is a large number of voters dissatisfied with the government, who can shift towards a new strong alternative. Second- In every election, 10 to 12% floating votes are cast. These votes can go to the SP-Congress alliance camp. Third- Although Akhilesh Yadav may have the Muslim-Yadav label attached to him, Rahul Gandhi's image is not casteist. Congress has not been in power in UP for the last 36 years. This means that in these 36 years, two generations have come who have not seen a Congress government. These voters' inclination could benefit the alliance because of Congress. Will BJP neutralize this challenge on the strength of organization and power? Senior journalist Ratan Mani Lal says- There are still more than 6 months left for the UP Assembly elections. In such a situation, it would be premature to say that the partnership between Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav that is visible in Delhi will also be visible in UP. After the success in Lok Sabha 2024, SP-Congress have spoken about continuing the alliance in the Assembly as well, but an official announcement is yet to be made. Secondly, Congress and SP will first have to resolve the issue of seat sharing. Akhilesh Yadav's party does not seem to be in the mood to give more seats to Congress, while Congress wants to increase its presence.

stories.title: Are you eating flour or powdered stone?:Wheat ground with white stone in UP mills; undercover probe exposes racket
stories.summary: 'This is powdered white stone. It is mixed into flour to increase profits. In the coming years, it will make people so sick that even doctors will say- Brother, there's no treatment for you.' These are the words of Sonu Kumar, an operator at a flour mill near Agra. He alleges that factory owners mix powdered white stone into flour to boost profits. According to him, the adulterated flour is sold across the country under the names of well-known brands. A Dainik Bhaskar undercover reporter spent 25 days working as a labourer inside the flour mill. The reporter gained access to the section where the stone powder was allegedly mixed into the flour. Inside, there was a setup where, at the press of a button, the powdered stone was automatically blended into the flour. Posing as a worker, the Bhaskar reporter secretly recorded the entire setup and the alleged adulteration process using a hidden camera. Read the full investigation… In Firozabad, Bulandshahr and Aligarh, officials recently caught adulteration of stone in branded flour. When we investigated, we found that this black game of adulteration is going on in many factories. Even now, stone powder is being mixed in flour in factories in Hathras and Firozabad. We reached two factories in Hathras and Firozabad disguised as labourers. We built rapport with other workers. We asked contractors for work. After wandering for three days, we got work. On the first day, we lifted sacks of wheat. On the second day, we were put on duty to supervise wheat. Then we got the job of filling sacks with chaff. For the first two weeks, we continued working as labourers. By the third week, we won the supervisor's trust. Finally, we got duty at that secret place for which we had been labouring for 2 weeks. This was a room with various machines installed. In one machine, stone powder was filled, which was being mixed into the flour. The operator and labourers did the work of setting and monitoring the percentage of stone powder to be mixed. We have exposed that stones are being mixed in flour. But, who is involved in this game? On what scale is this work happening? To find this out, we now became flour traders. We met factory operator Sonu Kumar in Tundla. Sonu understands the intricacies of mixing stone powder in flour. We told Sonu that we have got a tender to supply flour in Rajasthan. We need to set up a factory, which we will get done through you. Sonu explained the entire game of adulteration- Reporter: How much stone powder should be mixed in flour... 20% or up to 30%? Sonu: Keep it below 10%, otherwise complaints start coming about the flour. Reporter: What is the maximum percentage that can be mixed? Sonu: Currently, 10% is running in the market. If there's to be no return, you can adulterate up to 15% to 20%. Reporter: Which powder is it? Sonu: Sunsilk, soapstone (a type of stone powder). When you go to buy that powder, taste it to check that it's not gritty. Second, it should be white because some come with a yellowish tint too. Reporter: After mixing stone powder, what difference does it make in the flour roti? Sonu: No, there's no difference. Reporter: In taste? Sonu: No difference in taste either; I've checked the roti made from it. Reporter: You've eaten it? Sonu: Yes, one has to eat it, brother. When we add the material, we check what result will come in the market, right? Actually, let me tell you one thing: this is poison. If we mix rice flour, at least that's grain. With this, in the coming time people will develop so many diseases that doctors will start refusing, saying Brother, there's no cure for you. What is the math of profiteering? To find out, we expressed our desire to meet the flour factory owner. Operator Sonu introduced us to Raman Kumar, who runs a brand called Maharaja Bhog Atta in Tundla, Firozabad. Raman: If you mix 9-10% powder, you will get 70-80 paise per kilogram of flour in your pocket. Reporter: 70-80 paise or even more than that. Raman: Yes, you will get a profit of one rupee. Reporter: Meaning, ₹100 profit per quintal. Raman: Yes, what else? If 70-80 quintals of goods (flour mixed with stone powder) are sold daily, then there will be a profit of ₹7-8K. (Flour factory owner Raman showed adulterated flour) Raman: These are my goods; this number one is running. It's going for ₹28 per kilo. Operator Sonu: My father is running the machine; no problem. Raman: Everyone does mixing (adulteration of stone powder in flour). Otherwise there's no profit. You tell me - wheat is coming at ₹25 per kilo and flour is selling at ₹26.50 per kilo. Only ₹1.50 difference, whereas the cost in this is ₹1.70 per kilo. Like this, 20 paise more is going from us. That's why we're mixing 10% powder. Reporter: Can you keep the powder in the factory? Raman: Privacy has to be maintained. Don't know when, which officer might come? Although whoever comes, comes to take money. They take ₹5,000 every month and go. Now know the mathematics of profiteering by mixing stone powder Wheat rate: ₹2,500 per quintal White stone powder rate: ₹1,400 per quintal Grinding and labour cost: ₹170 per quintal With 10% adulteration Cost: ₹2,560 per quintal Flour will be sold in market: ₹2,700 per quintal Profit: ₹140 per quintal Available in market: Most companies are doing this much adulteration. With 20% adulteration - Cost: ₹2,450 per quintal Flour will be sold in market: ₹2700 per quintal Profit: ₹250 per quintal Available in market: This type of flour is being consumed in large events, community feasts, and mid-day meals. Now know, how much is the profit? A flour mill has four grinders. They grind 100 quintals of wheat in 10 hours. Then the profit for one day- At 10% adulteration: ₹14,000 At 20% adulteration: ₹25,000 They are earning a profit of up to ₹90 lakh per year from one flour mill. How is the stone powder setup installed? To answer this question, we met mechanic Sunil Kumar through a source. Sunil installs setups for mixing stone powder in flour factories. Sunil called us near Shahdara Police Chowki in Agra. Reporter: Need to set up a plant, will you install the adulteration setup? Sunil: I will arrange it in such a way that even if any flying team comes, or food product officials come, they won't find anything. Reporter: What rate will stone powder be available at? Sunil: This will be available for ₹12 to 14 per kilo. How does stone powder come here from Rajasthan? To answer this, we spoke with Vimal Agarwal, a dealer in Hathras. He told us that he would supply us with as much powder as we need to mix in flour. Reporter: We need it for mixing in flour. Is this powder being used in flour? Vimal: Yes, our powder is being used in flour. Everywhere (gesturing about money), this works. Many flour mill operators are mixing it. This is soil from the mountains; you also know this. Businessman Vimal showed us samples of stone powder. He claimed that there is no shortage of it. Vimal took us to the warehouse, where the stock of the powder was stored. Now know, what is white stone powder? This powder is called talc or soapstone. It comes from mines in some districts of Rajasthan. It is used in cosmetic items, face cream, plastic granules, paint, paper, and statue making. It cannot be eaten, but is being mixed in flour for profit. Doctors say- eating stone powder can damage liver and kidneys Lucknow's senior physician Dr. Gyan Tiwari said- stone powder has high calcium carbonate content. If you eat roti made from this flour, it will get stuck in the intestines. This damages the digestive system. Most people are facing such problems these days. Questions sent to Minister Ashish Patel; he did not respond In this matter, we tried to speak with Consumer Protection Minister Ashish Patel. On the first day, his phone was answered, and when the representative asked questions, we provided them. After that, we called 12 times in 7 days, but each time we were not allowed to speak, making excuses that Minister Patel was busy. We also sent questions to PRO Amaresh asking for answers, but he too did not provide any responses. Does your flour contain stone powder? Identify it like this Serving poor quality flour in mid-day meals We tested the flour used in mid-day meals at 3 schools in Western UP. We filled a glass with water and mixed a little flour in it. When doing this, pure flour dissolves in water, and flour with stones settles at the bottom. Here, at all three places, the flour settled at the bottom of the water. This made it clear that the flour being used in children's mid-day meals contains stone powder. Rotis made from this flour mixed with stone powder are being fed to children.
