stories.title: Chandrashekhar sounds poll bugle, appoints 45 Assembly in-charges:18 Dalits and 10 Muslims included; no Brahmin or Thakur leaders nominees
stories.summary: Azad Samaj Party chief and MP Chandrashekhar Azad has kicked off preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. On Friday, he released the first list of 45 Assembly in-charges. The list includes former IPS officer Aditya Prakash Verma from Hathras and former minister Mahendra Singh from Chharra, among other prominent leaders. Of the 45 appointees, 18 are Dalits, 10 Muslims, 16 OBCs, and one is from the Sikh community. No leader from the Brahmin or Thakur communities has been included in the list. Politically, the move is being seen as significant because the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) has also begun announcing candidates through Assembly in-charges. Both parties now appear set to directly challenge each other while competing for the Dalit vote bank and the broader Bahujan political space. See the list--- Maximum focus on Western UP The first list has the highest number of seats from Western UP. Special emphasis has been placed on strengthening the organization in districts like Meerut, Muzaffarnagar, Shamli, Hapur, Agra, Aligarh, Mathura, Bareilly, Badaun and Shahjahanpur. It is believed that the party is working on a strategy to increase its political hold in areas with Dalit-Muslim equations. In the list of 45 in-charges, the party has also taken care of social balance. The highest number, 18 Dalit faces, have been given responsibility. Apart from this, 16 people from OBC communities including Yadav, Gurjar, Prajapati, Valmiki, Maurya and several other communities have been given representation. By giving opportunity to the Muslim community on 10 seats, Chandrashekhar has tried to balance the equation of Western UP and Purvanchal. Former MLAs and prominent faces included in the list The list includes several leaders who have previously contested elections from various parties or hold influence in their regions. These include Deepak Chaudhary from Govardhan, Jagdish Baghel from Fatehpur Sikri, Tulsiram Valmiki from Govind Nagar, and Shivsagar Yadav from the Madhuban seat in Mau. Party says - Appointments made on recommendations of state committee The party claims that these in-charges have been appointed based on recommendations from the state committee. All in-charges have been entrusted with the responsibility of strengthening the organization up to the booth level, along with taking issues of social justice, constitution, and Bahujan Samaj to the public.

stories.summary: Paperless working has officially begun at the University of Lucknow from 31 July. Governor and Chancellor Anandiben Patel inaugurated the e-Office system during the university's 69th convocation ceremony. The event is being held at the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Convention Centre of KGMU. The Chancellor awarded digital degrees to 125,239 students. Vice-Chancellor JP Saini said students from 44 countries are currently studying at the university. The university has 93,536 undergraduate students, 31,006 postgraduate students, 419 diploma students and 30 online education students. In addition, 248 researchers were awarded PhD degrees. A total of 204 medals were presented to 111 meritorious students, including 80 women and 31 men. The convocation is being presided over by Governor and Chancellor Anandiben Patel. NITI Aayog member Prof Abhay Karandikar is the chief guest. Higher Education Minister Yogendra Upadhyay was invited but could not attend the event. Minister of State for Higher Education Rajni Tiwari is among the dignitaries attending the ceremony.

stories.title: MPs stage unique protest over Ram Mandir offerings row:Rahul Gandhi puts money in donation box; Pappu Yadav pretends to flee with it, SP MPs stop him
stories.summary: On the 10th day of Parliament's Monsoon Session on Friday, the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress staged a unique protest in the Parliament complex over the alleged theft of offerings at the Ayodhya Ram Temple. Independent MP Pappu Yadav, who represents Purnia in Bihar, arrived dressed as a Hindu ascetic. Wearing a sandalwood tilak on his forehead and carrying a donation box, he sat on the ground. As SP MPs Dimple Yadav, Dharmendra Yadav and Awadhesh Prasad tried to place offerings in the donation box, Pappu Yadav jokingly snatched the money and put it in his pocket. Congress MP Rahul Gandhi also dropped money into the box. A short while later, Pappu Yadav pretended to run away with the donation box, but SP MPs caught him and took it back. In a light-hearted remark, Pappu Yadav said, "I thought I'd run away with the money, but the SP MPs caught me. Now they're saying they'll hang me." The opposition has been targeting the government over the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Mandir, the alleged lathi-charge on students, and Union Home Minister Amit Shah's absence from the House. stories.title: Kanwariya pulls 8-quintal car-shaped Kanwar with his teeth:Carries parents in palanquin; AI surveillance introduced on Kanwar route
stories.summary: Crowds of Kanwariyas are now visible on roads across Uttar Pradesh. Some devotees are heading to Haridwar to collect holy Ganga water, while others are returning after completing the pilgrimage. In Aligarh, Narendra Jat is pulling an 800kg car-shaped Kanwar with his teeth on his way to Haridwar. A statue of Lord Shiva has been installed on its roof. He said he began the journey with the resolve that the cow should be granted the status of the nation's mother, and believes Lord Shiva will fulfil his wish. In Bulandshahr, Jitendra is carrying his parents in a palanquin while returning from Haridwar with holy Ganga water. He will offer the water at the Shiv temple in Sikandrabad. Prashant Rana, from Hapur, is bringing back holy Ganga water with his grandmother, Sharda Devi, seated in a Kanwar. He is accompanied by 22 fellow Kanwariyas, and all of them will offer the holy water at a Shiv temple in Hapur. In Ghaziabad on Thursday evening, Kanwariyas created a ruckus after a Kanwar was damaged. They accused a Muslim youth of touching the Kanwar and thrashed him. He was slapped and punched repeatedly in the middle of the road before police intervened and managed to calm the crowd. Meanwhile, police remain on high alert for the Kanwar Yatra. Round-the-clock monitoring is being carried out on roads as well as across social media platforms. The Kanwar route is being monitored through CCTV cameras and AI-based surveillance.

stories.title: Woman gives birth 3 hours after her daughter's last rites:10-year-old raped, murdered by constable at crematorium; girl used to say, 'I will tie rakhi to my brother'
stories.summary: A constable raped and killed a 10-year-old girl at a cremation ground in Gorakhpur. Her last rites were performed on Thursday at 6 PM. Three hours later, her mother gave birth to a son. When the mother and sisters saw the baby's face, they burst into tears. They said that the girl had wished to tie a rakhi to her brother on this Raksha Bandhan, but before that could happen, the monster snatched her away. Meanwhile, police investigation revealed that after the rape, constable Abhishek Yadav (35) tied the girl's hands behind her back and threw her alive into the river. Her head hit a stone. She died from drowning and suffocation. The post-mortem revealed that the girl was subjected to brutality. Five bones in her body were found broken, including those in her feet and neck. Her stomach was ruptured. Deep wound marks were found on her private parts. The constable's wife told Dainik Bhaskar - What he has done is unforgivable. He has made me hang my head in shame. Where will I show my face now? We also have a daughter. I will never live with him again. On the night of 28th July, a constable kidnapped a girl from the district hospital. After examining 200 CCTV cameras, the police arrested the accused on 29th July. On Thursday, based on his identification, the police recovered the body after 36 hours. The family has demanded financial assistance of ₹50 lakhs, a job for one member, and the death penalty for the accused. SSP Dr. Kaustubh informed that the accused constable has been dismissed. An FIR has been registered against him under the POCSO Act and other sections. RASUKA (NSA) will also be imposed on him. Read the entire case from the girl's kidnapping to the last rites in 4 points... 1- Went to hospital to give food to his sister, kidnapped from there The girl's father is originally from Azamgarh. He has been living on rent in Gorakhpur with his wife and 5 daughters for 4 years. He runs the household by driving an e-rickshaw. On July 27, his 13-year-old daughter suddenly fell ill. The family admitted her to the district hospital. On July 28, the girl went to the hospital with food for her elder sister. During this time, the constable had also come to the hospital to get medicine. Seeing the girl alone, he started following her. When the girl left the hospital at 10 PM, he coaxed her and made her sit on his bike. He took her to a cremation ground 15 km away from the hospital. There he committed brutality with the girl. He beat her mercilessly. Then threw her in the river. The accused reached the police lines. There were blood stains on his uniform. He washed the uniform and then went to sleep. 2- 200 CCTVs searched, seen taking the girl away on a bike Meanwhile, when the girl did not reach home, the family started searching. The family members searched on their own for 2 hours. Late at night, the police were also informed, but the swift action that should have been taken in the initial hours was not visible. From Wednesday afternoon, police and teams from 10 police stations got engaged in the search operation. During this time, 200 CCTV cameras in the surrounding areas were examined. In the cameras, a constable on a bike was seen taking the innocent child from the district hospital. As soon as the registration number was obtained, the police reached the accused. After getting the bike's registration number from CCTV, the accused was identified on Wednesday afternoon. The police took him into custody. He kept misleading the police for 4 hours. When interrogated strictly, he confessed to the crime. On Thursday at 8:30 AM, the police recovered the girl's body based on the accused constable's identification. 3- Doctors and nurses at the district hospital chased and beat him On Thursday afternoon, the police brought the constable to the district hospital for medical examination. Doctors, nurses, and people present there surrounded the constable. They chased him and beat him severely with kicks and punches. Somehow, the police team calmed them down by explaining. Somehow, by calling heavy force, the constable was taken out in police custody. All work at the district hospital remained suspended for two hours. 4- Sister fainted after seeing the body, father performed last rites On Thursday at 5 PM, after the postmortem, the police did not take the girl's body home but took it directly by ambulance to Rajghat. On receiving this information, her four sisters rushed there. Upon seeing the body, the younger sister fainted. The father performed the last rites for his daughter. Sister used to say - This Raksha Bandhan, I will also have a brother The elder sister said that my younger sister used to tell mother that this Raksha Bandhan, I will also have a brother. I will fulfill my dream by tying him a rakhi. Today, if she were here, she would have been the happiest. She always used to ask her mother for a brother. She always used to say that she would study hard, become a doctor, and treat her mother herself. When the constable's wife learned about the incident, she held her head in despair The constable's wife lives in Molnapur village in Ghazipur with her daughter and son. When the wife received information about this incident, she held her head in shock. The wife said that due to his habits, she left her in-laws' house and lives with her children at her maternal home. Was a 2018 batch constable, had been jailed before for molestation The accused constable Abhishek Yadav is originally a resident of Hansrajpur Chaura village in the Shadiyabad police station area of Ghazipur. Abhishek is a 2018 batch constable. Currently, he is posted in Dial-112. He was appointed in 2016 on a merit basis. His first posting was in Gorakhpur. He had been posted there since then. In January 2025, he had molested a woman from Bengal. He was suspended then as well. He was also sent to jail.

stories.title: Clouds cover Gorakhpur skies:Winds blow at 45 kmph; August to begin with rain
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, the sky has been cloudy since Friday morning. Cold winds blowing at a speed of 40 to 45 km/h have provided great relief to people from humidity and heat. Light sunshine is also appearing intermittently between the clouds, while light rain or drizzle is expected in some parts of the city by evening. According to the Meteorological Department, the maximum temperature of the district on Friday is estimated to be around 32 degrees Celsius and the minimum temperature 27 degrees Celsius. Clouds will continue to move throughout the day, so a significant increase in temperature is not expected. However, in areas where there is no rain and the sun comes out, humidity may be felt for some time due to moisture. Rainfall to increase with the beginning of August Meteorologists say that with the beginning of August, monsoon activities will intensify. For the next few days, clouds will remain over Gorakhpur and its surrounding areas. Light drizzle can be seen in some places, while moderate rain can be seen in others. The scope of rainfall is also likely to gradually increase. Saturday will be cloudy, with scattered drizzles On August 1, i.e., Saturday, the weather is likely to remain almost the same. The sky will be cloudy and light rain or showers may occur in some parts of the district. However, the rain will be intermittent, and the sun may also appear in between. In such a situation, humidity can be troublesome in areas where there is no rain. Rain likely in most parts of the district on Monday From August 2, Sunday, there are signs of an increase in rain activities. According to the Meteorological Department, light to moderate rain may occur in many parts of the district. With increasing rain, the daytime temperature will drop, and people will get more relief from the heat. The monsoon is likely to become more active on Monday, August 3. According to the district-level forecast by the Meteorological Department, most parts of the district may experience rain. Light to moderate rain may be recorded in some areas. The extent of rainfall is expected to continuously increase during the first three days of August. Monsoon effect to continue next week as well The Meteorological Department estimates that monsoon activities will continue in Eastern Uttar Pradesh next week as well. Its effect will also be seen in Gorakhpur. The cycle of dense clouds, rain, and occasional sunshine will continue. Due to rain, the temperature will remain controlled, and the possibility of severe heat is low. Relief from heat, but humidity will not completely disappear People will definitely get relief from the heat due to rain and cold winds, but due to high humidity in the atmosphere, the stickiness will not completely disappear. After the rain stops and the sun comes out, a sticky heat may be felt. However, due to strong winds and intermittent rain, the weather will remain pleasant most of the time. Overall, July is bidding farewell in Gorakhpur with clouds, cold winds, and pleasant weather, while August is expected to begin with an increasing spell of rain. Rain activities will intensify from Saturday, and the impact of the monsoon will be clearly visible in a large part of the district from Sunday to Monday.

stories.title: Youth beaten after allegedly brushing against Kanwar:Slapped and punched; Kanwariya says, 'All my effort has gone to waste'
stories.summary: A dispute broke out in Ghaziabad after a Kanwar carried by Kanwariyas was damaged during the yatra. The Kanwariyas accused a Muslim youth of touching the Kanwar and allegedly assaulted him in the middle of the road with slaps and punches. One of the Kanwariyas said he had followed all the religious rituals throughout the journey, but his efforts went in vain after the Kanwar broke. After being informed, police reached the spot and brought the situation under control. According to religious customs, the Kanwar was worshipped again with proper rituals. The incident took place in the Madhuban Bapudham police station area at around 4 pm on Thursday. See 2 pictures Now, the incident in detail Held hostage for 20 minutes Sonu Kumar, a resident of Bharatpur, Rajasthan, was returning to his village with Ganga water from Haridwar along with 15 fellow Kanwariyas from his village. During this, his Kanwar was touched by a young man. When Sonu asked, the young man told his name as Imran. The Kanwariyas alleged that this broke their Kanwar, after which a quarrel started. The Kanwariyas severely beat Imran. They held him hostage for about 20 minutes. Seeing the commotion, people from nearby areas gathered. This caused a traffic jam for one kilometer on both sides of the road. Some people tried to intervene, but the Kanwariyas did not listen. Kanwariya said - I have to offer water at the Shiva temple Kanwariya Sonu said- I started my Kanwar journey from Haridwar at 5 AM on July 21st. I rested only 3 times on the way. I must reach my village by August 10th and perform Jalabhishek at the village's Shiva temple on August 11th. I was undertaking the entire journey according to the rules. But, my Kanwar got damaged on the way, rendering all my hard work useless. The police somehow pacified the Kanwariyas. The Kanwar was worshipped again with proper rituals. After this, the Kanwariyas resumed their journey. Due to the commotion, traffic near Guladhar station was affected for about 20 minutes. The police cleared the crowd and normalised traffic. Additional Police Commissioner (Law and Order) Rajkaran Naiyar said- After the incident, station in-charges have been instructed to exercise special vigilance during the Kanwar Yatra. Warnings have been issued to stop the movement of heavy vehicles on the Kanwar route from Meerut border to Delhi border, and to strictly implement the diversion system.

stories.title: Rivers swell in UP, rain alert issued for 24 cities:9 swept away after boat capsizes in Sharda; Ganga flows over highway in Bijnor
stories.summary: The monsoon has weakened again in Uttar Pradesh, but heavy rainfall in the hills has caused 10 rivers, including the Ganga and Ghaghara (Saryu), to swell. In Lakhimpur Kheri, a boat capsized in the Sharda River on Thursday evening. 9 people were swept away. 7 were rescued, while a search is underway for the remaining two. In Bijnor, the Ganga is flowing over the Bahsuma–Thakurdwara State Highway, with vehicles seen passing through the floodwater. Nearby fields are also inundated. The administration is monitoring the situation. Since Friday morning, skies have remained overcast in more than 35 cities, including Lucknow, Gorakhpur, Kanpur and Barabanki, with cool winds prevailing. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 24 cities, while Lalitpur, Mirzapur and Sonbhadra are under a heavy rainfall alert. Residents have been advised to step out only if necessary. According to the IMD, the low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal has moved towards Odisha and Chhattisgarh, weakening monsoon activity over Uttar Pradesh. Satellite images show that monsoon clouds have disappeared from nearly 90% of the state. Earlier on Thursday, rain was recorded in 29 cities, including Varanasi, Meerut and Bijnor. In Bijnor, roads were waterlogged and floodwater entered the offices of the Basic Education Officer and the Housing Development Department. In Meerut, an electricity tower along the Ganga riverbank was washed away. Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said: "The monsoon system over central India is expected to weaken soon. After that, the monsoon trough will rapidly shift towards Uttar Pradesh. At the same time, monsoon winds from the Bay of Bengal will strengthen again. As a result, the monsoon is likely to regain momentum from 3–4 August, bringing another spell of heavy rainfall.

stories.title: 'I will have relations with your wife':Sting operation exposes UP Maulanas; defend triple talaq; perform halala themselves
stories.summary: “Your divorced wife will marry me first, then halala will take place. It is my decision whether I keep her for one night or longer. You cannot ask me to divorce her.” These are the words of Maulana Rehmatullah from Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh, who was secretly recorded allegedly promoting halala. Although the triple talaq law has been in force for seven years, a sting operation claims that some maulanas in Uttar Pradesh are still exploiting Muslim women under the cover of religious practices. Under the traditional practice, if a husband divorces his wife by pronouncing talaq three times, they cannot remarry unless the woman first marries another man. The second husband must consummate the marriage and later divorce her of his own free will. Only then can she legally remarry her first husband. This process is known as halala. According to the sting operation, some couples avoid involving relatives in this process. Instead, certain maulanas allegedly offer to perform halala themselves. They are accused of staying with divorced women in hotels and charging money for accommodation and other expenses. During the investigation, Dainik Bhaskar's team approached two maulanas, who allegedly agreed to carry out halala themselves in the name of religion. In Gorakhpur, we contacted Maulana Rahmatullah. The Maulana runs a tailor shop. We told Rahmatullah - we have had a triple talaq. Iddat, meaning 3 months, is about to be completed. Now we want to live together again. What is the way? Halala is necessary and just as husband and wife live, it is necessary to live that way Rahmatullah : The Quran is considered divine. Halala is in it. The woman should stay away from her husband for 3 menses (menstrual periods). Then she should marry a person who is responsible. It should never be kept in mind that he (the new husband) should divorce her; this will not be according to the Quran. This is the will of the new husband. It is necessary to live in the same way that a husband and wife live together. Reporter : Then with whom should Halala be performed? Rahmatullah: If it's a brother or a close relative, they get halala done with him. This happens because he gives a divorce, but sometimes the man (who performed halala) doesn't divorce her at all. There was a 70-year-old man in Meerut. He divorced his wife. There was an acquaintance with whom he arranged a nikah (marriage) under halala. Later, he changed his mind. He said, "Where is your wife? Now she is my wife." The woman also said that she would stay there. The woman was 40-45 years old. Reporter: We don't want to get halala done with anyone from the family. Rahmatullah: Okay, your wife will be married to me. After that, halala. Now it's my will whether I keep your wife for one night or for how long. Whatever expenses are incurred in this, you will have to pay. Reporter: What will be the expense? Rahmatullah: Oh brother, whatever the Maulana's expense will be. You will have to pay for everything. We will inform the gentleman (pointing towards our source). Not much, consider it within 20 to 25 thousand. Reporter: Will I have to bring my wife here? Rahmatullah: Bring her after Muharram, then the marriage will happen. Then I will explain some things to your wife. For example, when you were husband and wife before, you didn't tell anyone each other's secrets. Similarly, you shouldn't tell anyone what I say. Reporter: Will it be physical too? Rahmatullah: This thought should not be in your mind. Tell me, when a Nikah happens, suppose your wife gets her periods on the first night, then you won't do it, then you'll do it on the second night. You will do it after 4 days, won't you? A relationship has to be built. I was just watching on YouTube. A Maulana says that the husband-wife relationship has to be maintained. You have to forget that she is my wife. Reporter: Meaning we have separated, now she has been married anew. Rahmatullah: We get ready for Nikah because of me, the relationship becomes better. Our family is of Pirs (spiritual guides). My maternal grandparents' home is in Maharajganj. There is Khutha Bazaar there. The Pir Sahib there is our biological great-grandfather. That's why we perform prayers and make amulets. Reporter: What time should I come in the morning? Rahmatullah: Come by 11-12 AM. Then leave your wife with me for 4-5 hours. What happens is that to build a relationship, we need to talk a little. I will have to explain things to her. It's not like coming and pouncing like a dog. We can book a hotel. From here, we left saying that we would bring the wife after a few days. Now we were looking for a Maulana whose stature among Muslims was even greater. Our search ended with Mufti Meraj Ahmed Qadri. The source told us that Meraj Ahmed is a Mufti in the Madina Mosque of Gorakhpur. Hundreds of people offer prayers behind him daily. We approached him and discussed Halala. 'It is in the Hadith that physical relations must be established at least once' Meraj Ahmed: In the case of divorce, Halala is the only way. It would have been better if you had not given 3 divorces. If you had given 1 or 2 divorces, you could have called her back and remarried. Since you have given three divorces, she is out of your hands. Now, if you want to have loving conversations with her, it is not permissible. Reporter: What is the way out of this? Meraj Ahmed: The way is that if you want to live with your wife and children, Islam states that the wife should have a second marriage (Nikah). If there's someone from your family, marry her to him, or marry her to someone I tell you about. She just has to spend 1 or 2 nights with him. They just have to consummate the marriage, even if it's just once. That too, because you have given a divorce. If she has completed her Iddat (waiting period), then when the second marriage (Nikah) happens, she will again enter Iddat (after the second divorce). After that, she will be 'fresh' (eligible). Then you can marry her. The only way for this is Halala. There is no other permissible way. If you go to court, they will just finalize the divorce. Iddat means a waiting period. After divorce, one has to wait for about three months. Before that, a remarriage cannot happen. Reporter: Do they have to have the same kind of relations as a husband and wife? Meraj Ahmed: Look, you will have to spend one night with him. What he does, only he knows. But, in Hadith, it is stated that a relationship (physical intimacy) must be established once. You are doing this for Allah's principle. Reporter: In our view, there is no one who is loyal, who would do something at our behest. We don't want to do it at home. Meraj Ahmed: There is a way. If you don't find anyone, let us know. We will talk to such a person who is responsible. But, the condition is that after the Nikah, you will have to take a room in a hotel for 2-3 days. It's possible that the work might be done in one day. It's possible it might take more days. After that, the Mahr (dower) money will also have to be given. And some 'Nazre Inayat' (favors/gifts), whatever they wish, that will have to be given. Whatever expenses arise, you will have to bear them. After one or two nights, they will give divorce. After 4 months pass, then you can perform Nikah (marry again). Reporter: What will be the cost involved in this? Meraj Ahmed: Look, the Mahr (dower) will not be less than 11 thousand. We'll check the rate of Dirham (silver coin). Assume it will be between 11 thousand to 15 thousand. After that, arrangements for food and drink will have to be made. A gift (nazrana) of 10 to 15 thousand will have to be given. If you don't give it, it's possible that it might come to his mind and he won't leave your wife.

stories.title: BJP survey predicts loss of 52–67 seats in UP:Recommends dropping 35% of MLAs to counter anti-incumbency
stories.summary: Before the UP Assembly elections, the BJP has received a major setback from an internal survey conducted by the party. The report indicates that if elections were held in the current situation, the BJP might have to struggle for a majority. There could be a direct loss of 52 to 67 seats for BJP. The BJP is getting 190 to 205 seats. 202 seats are needed for a majority. In 2022, the BJP received 255 seats. In by-elections, 2 more seats were added to the BJP's account. Currently, the BJP has a total of 257 MLAs. The survey agency has also given suggestions to avoid this loss. For this, the party will have to deny tickets to 35% of its current MLAs. There is maximum discontent regarding MLAs in the Purvanchal region. BJP conducted a survey through the Nation With Namo agency before the assembly elections. This is a registered organization. It conducts political surveys for BJP. I n this, experts and researchers included in the team reached all assembly constituencies from March to the second week of July and took predetermined samples. Some questions were asked to people- 2 types of discontent were seen in the survey In the survey report, people's discontent has been divided into 2 types. The first category includes discontent with the government, i.e., central and state government policies. The second category includes anger towards MLAs. During the survey, the policies and incidents related to the government on which the public expressed dissatisfaction are as follows- Displeasure with MLAs emerged due to these reasons- Team gave 2 types of suggestions in the survey report Suggestion 1- Tickets of 30 to 35% MLAs should be cut The survey revealed resentment against 30% to 35% of BJP MLAs. People clearly told the team that came to conduct the survey that if old faces are given another chance in the Assembly elections like the Lok Sabha, we will look for other options. The survey suggests that to reverse these results, the BJP will have to deny tickets to 30 to 35% of its current 257 MLAs. This will reduce people's anger towards the ruling party's MLAs. The BJP can cross the majority mark. Currently, the party is strong on 190 to 205 seats. However, based on the right selection of candidates, balancing caste equations, and issues that emerge just before the elections, there could be a fluctuation of 10% in this estimate. Faces were changed in 2022 as well Before the 2022 assembly elections, the BJP had commissioned surveys from 2 agencies. Based on that report, the BJP had denied tickets to more than 120 MLAs. New candidates were fielded on 165 out of 403 seats. Despite this, the BJP's seats decreased from 312 in 2017 to 255. This resulted in a loss of 57 seats for the BJP. Suggestion 2- Advantage in fighting elections on issues like nationalism The survey team believes that if the election remains focused on issues like religion, nationalism, and law and order, the BJP will benefit. However, if the SP succeeds in making caste equations and PDA (Backward, Dalit, Minority) politics a major issue, like in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP could suffer losses. Resentment against Yadavs has decreased among the new generation A member of the survey team stated that Yadavs have been considered traditional voters of the SP. During SP rule, Yadavs' matters were often heard quickly in many cases. This led to resentment against them among non-Yadav people. However, this resentment has decreased over the past 5 years. Especially Gen-Z (the new generation) does not consider the Yadav versus non-Yadav concept to be correct. Yogi's team is also conducting a separate survey The BJP organization's survey has been completed. However, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath is conducting a separate election survey. A private agency is going village to village collecting feedback from people about the government, MLAs, and the Chief Minister's image. This situation has arisen after the disqualification of MLAs, by-elections, and deaths following the 2022 elections

stories.title: 'Today is a dark day in history':Allahabad HC judge says attempt was made to influence him; rescuses himself from ₹900 cr codeine case
stories.summary: 'An attempt was made to reach the judge for bail. Such attempts are a direct attack on the independence and impartiality of the judiciary. These cannot be accepted under any circumstances. This is a black day in the history of the judiciary.' This comment was made by Allahabad High Court Judge Krishna Pahal on Thursday in the codeine cough syrup case. He sent 80 petitions, including the bail application of accused Bhola Prasad, to the Chief Justice and recused himself from all cases. Judge Krishna Pahal said at the start of the hearing - After the judgment was reserved, the accused attempted to reach the presiding judge personally. Calling it an assault on judicial dignity, he said such tendencies cannot be accepted in the court premises under any circumstances. Bhola Prasad is the father of Shubham Jaiswal, the kingpin of the codeine cough syrup gang. Shubham is absconding. He has already been declared a fugitive. The next hearing will now be on 7th August. Judge said- If ignored, trust will be shaken Actually, about 80 accused in the codeine cough syrup case have filed bail petitions in the High Court. For their hearing together, the court had fixed Thursday, July 30 at 10 AM. Along with the lawyers of the accused, Additional Advocate General Anoop Trivedi and AGA First Paritosh Kumar Malviya were also present on behalf of the state government. As soon as the hearing began, the court said that the order could have been reserved after the hearing was completed, but later attempts were made by the accused to reach and contact the presiding judge. The court said that if such conduct is ignored, it will weaken the roots of judicial independence and the common people's faith in the justice system will be shaken. Judge said - Prestige of the judiciary cannot be put under the cloud of doubt Judge Krishna Pahal said, ‘If in such circumstances the decision had come in favor of the party whose arguments appeared strong, then despite the legal strength of the judgment, this doubt could have arisen that the decision was the result of some external influence or improper attempt rather than judicial discretion.’ The reputation of the judiciary earned over years cannot be put under the shadow of such doubt. The court said - Justice is not only sufficient to be done, but it should also be clearly and unequivocally seen that justice has been done impartially. Attempting to make personal contact with a judge in a pending case is against the ethics of advocate conduct and the constitutional values of an independent judiciary. The High Court, calling it an assault on judicial dignity, said that such a tendency cannot be accepted in the court premises under any circumstances. The court warned lawyers and accused, saying - Judicial independence is not a special privilege, but a constitutional right granted to every citizen. Any attempt to weaken it should be strongly condemned. High Court has already refused to cancel the case In the codeine cough syrup case, the accused first filed petitions to have the case cancelled, but these petitions were rejected by three different division benches of the High Court and one division bench of the Lucknow bench. The court said that there is sufficient basis for investigation in the matter. After this, the accused filed applications for anticipatory bail. Even on these anticipatory bail petitions, no relief was granted to any petitioner by the High Court, and arrests continued. Following this, petitions were filed for regular bail. In these too, the regular bail petitions of four accused have been rejected by different benches of the High Court. Case was registered on 15 November, 2025 In the case registered at Kotwali police station on 15 November, about 40 people, including Shubham Jaiswal and his father Bhola Jaiswal, were named. As the investigation progressed during the inquiry, many names came to light. Many of them have already been arrested. Now know what are the charges against Shubham A case has been registered at Kotwali against 28 drug traders of Kashi, including interstate gang leader Shubham Jaiswal and his father Bhola Jaiswal. The allegation is that 89 lakh bottles of banned cough syrup worth ₹100 crores were bought and sold. In the name of 93 medical stores in Kashi alone, 84 lakh bottles of banned cough syrup were bought and sold. Most of the medical stores in whose names the business was shown were not found at the location. Later, the fraud of this illegal business network spread across Bengal and Bangladesh was exposed. The investigation revealed that cough syrup was sold to 9 closed firms. These include Messrs Srishti Pharma, GT Enterprises, Shivam Pharma, Harsh Pharma, DSA Pharma, Mahakal Medical Store, Nishant Pharma, VPM Medical Agency and Shri Balaji Medical. According to the Commissioner, fake firms were created only for the purchase and sale of codeine-containing syrup. Cases are also registered against Shubham Jaiswal in other districts including Sonbhadra, Jaunpur, Varanasi, Ghaziabad, and Chandauli.
