stories.summary: Indigenous communities in Arunachal Pradesh are now earning livelihoods from a native spice. This wild Himalayan spice, known locally as Khagi, is helping over two hundred families. The community-led system for harvesting and marketing the spice supports forest patrols and biodiversity monitoring. This initiative provides a direct economic incentive for people to protect their forests and agricultural land. The project also contributes to the conservation of important transboundary wildlife habitats.

stories.title: Indian national in US on visitor visa jailed for $3.7 million fraud scheme targeting elders
Scientists trained 182 pet dogs to sniff out one of America's most destructive invasive insects, and most successfully found its hidden eggs
Archaeologists discovered Spain's oldest known Roman library inside a villa in Córdoba
stories.summary: Archaeologists identified a room at Fuente Álamo as the oldest Roman library. This space was previously thought to be a shrine to the god Mithras. The library's architecture matches known Roman library designs and is the westernmost in the empire. Its discovery highlights the cultural ambitions of its wealthy owner. This finding offers a unique glimpse into Roman intellectual life in Baetica.

stories.title: TASMAC corruption case: Supreme Court grants DMK's Senthil Balaji interim protection from arrest
14-year-old Montana boy uses Rodeo Lasso to save drowning man on camping trip
stories.summary: A family camping trip in Montana turned into a dramatic rescue when 14-year-old Jory Thomas used his rodeo lasso skills to save a man from the fast-moving Yellowstone River. After a raft and paddleboard crashed into a bridge pillar, one person was swept downstream. Jory roped the man on his first attempt and pulled him safely to shore before emergency responders arrived.

stories.title: U.S. avocado imports cut chemical use, reduce nitrogen pollution by 10%
stories.summary: New United States import rules for Mexican avocados prompted growers to reduce chemical use. This change significantly lowered nitrogen pollution in nearby Mexican waterways. Stricter inspections and phytosanitary certificates encouraged more careful pest management practices. The market access incentivized cleaner production methods without halting trade. This demonstrates how trade policies can yield unexpected environmental benefits.

stories.title: World's first power plant: Salt water meets fresh water to generate electricity
Supreme Court grants Omar Abdullah divorce after settlement with estranged wife Payal
Solved water crisis by turning seawater into drinking water using solar power
In 2003, a retired man planted trees on forgotten land alone; 20 years later, it had become one of Sao Paulo's largest urban forests
SP pressures opposition to take up Ayodhya donation scam, Congress focuses on police crackdown
BJP trying to force Muslims, minorities to worship Hindu deities, says Owaisi; DMK slams Vande Mataram bill as 'fraud'
stories.summary: AIMIM leader Asaduddin Owaisi slammed the bill criminalizing insult to Vande Mataram. He stated the bill forces minorities to worship Hindu deities and violates religious freedom. DMK MP A Raja called the legislation a fraud against India's secular fabric. Congress questioned the Home Minister's absence during the bill's passage. Opposition parties argue the government is imposing its views on citizens.

stories.title: Teen lifeguard saves 3 in massive waves on first day, earns Trump’s praise
stories.summary: A 16-year-old lifeguard named Ryder Williams performed a dramatic ocean rescue in Santa Cruz. He bravely pulled a 10-year-old boy from powerful surf at Seabright Beach. After his shift, Williams also helped save two more individuals in a separate incident. This heroic teenager received nationwide praise for his actions and bravery. His dedication highlights the importance of lifeguard training and quick response.

stories.title: America cancelled the world's most powerful particle collider, leaving a 22.5-km tunnel hidden beneath Texas for more than 30 years
400 hours counting caterpillars changed what we knew about LED lighting
Help families file compensation with Russian embassy, match DNA of Indians killed in war: SC to govt
stories.summary: The Supreme Court ordered the MEA to appoint a nodal officer for families. This officer will coordinate with families of Indians who joined the Russian military. The court also asked for DNA matching and assistance with compensation claims. The Centre previously stated 217 Indians joined the Russian military, with 49 deaths reported. Efforts are ongoing to verify deaths and trace missing individuals.

stories.title: 14-year-old Indian American girl builds system to predict driver fatigue, eyes $25,000 prize
stories.summary: Fourteen-year-old Indian-American student Sharvi Mahajan has developed NeuroDrive Alert, an EEG-based machine learning system that tracks brain activity to predict driver fatigue before microsleep occurs. Her innovation has earned her a place among the 10 finalists of the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge, where she will compete for a $25,000 prize.

stories.title: Exiled Bangladeshi writer Taslima Nasreen returns to Kolkata after 19 years
stories.summary: Exiled writer Taslima Nasreen returned to Kolkata after nearly two decades. She described her visit as an emotional homecoming to her own country. Nasreen is scheduled to attend a public program in the city on August 1. This marks her first public appearance in Kolkata since 2007. Protests over her memoir "Dwikhandito" had forced her departure then.

stories.title: 'Aap BJP ke ho kya?' Rahul Gandhi's response to question on cops injured during student protest
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi questioned a reporter's affiliation after families of injured police personnel shared their experiences. These families recounted traumatic incidents and sought justice for the injured officers. Earlier, Gandhi had demanded a Supreme Court-monitored probe into alleged police actions against students. Meanwhile, opposition MPs protested in Parliament, demanding home minister Amit Shah's resignation.

stories.title: Texas engineers are building fish-like nano-robots that could harvest lithium from seawater and transform the future of clean energy
stories.summary: Texas A&M engineers are developing fish-like nano-robots to harvest lithium from seawater. These autonomous microscopic robots use specialised particles activated by light for movement. This innovative approach offers a sustainable alternative to traditional land-based mining methods.

stories.title: US Summer heat leaves multiple hikers dehydrated in New York's Adirondacks
stories.summary: New York Forest Rangers responded to a series of rescues across the Adirondacks in June, helping dehydrated hikers, treating medical emergencies, locating lost visitors and tackling a wildfire. Several incidents were linked to hot weather, prompting officials to remind people to carry enough water, prepare properly and follow hiking safety guidelines.

stories.title: 'Vendetta by filing FIRs against students': Kharge demands Amit Shah's resignation over police action
Bihar Police arrest STF jawan in Bharat Bhushan Tiwari 'fake encounter' probe — What was the case
34 killed as methane explosion tears through coal mine in Pakistan's Balochistan
stories.summary: A methane gas explosion in Pakistan's Balochistan province killed at least thirty-four miners. Ten miners remained trapped underground after the blast ripped through the coal mine. Rescue teams worked against time to locate and recover the remaining trapped workers. Authorities announced compensation for the families of the deceased miners. The incident highlights ongoing safety concerns within Pakistan's coal mining industry.

stories.title: The Southern Ocean may be Earth’s safest place to remove carbon from the atmosphere, scientists find
After decades of drought, water is returning to the south of Sahara Desert as ancient farming techniques and the Great Green Wall breathe new life into the Sahel
BJP's Shehzad Poonawalla drops party name from X bio, fuels exit speculation
stories.summary: Shehzad Poonawalla's X bio change has sparked rumors about his departure from the BJP. His updated profile omits any mention of the political party affiliation. However, his Instagram bio still lists him as a BJP Spokesperson. Poonawalla joined the BJP in December 2017 and has been a vocal supporter. There has been no official confirmation regarding his status with the party.

stories.title: German proverb of the day: "A fence lasts 3 years, a dog lasts 3 fences, a horse lasts 3 dogs, and a man lasts…"
stories.summary: An old German proverb highlights life's transient nature and the importance of valuing time. It uses symbolic lifespans to show everything has a limited existence. This message remains relevant as daily life continues to change rapidly. The proverb encourages appreciating ordinary moments and relationships over possessions. It reminds us that life's meaning comes from how years are spent, not just their length.

stories.title: Punjab opens applications for second batch of anti-drug mental health fellowship
'Head of family PM Modi listens': BJP's Raghav Chadha hails 'historic' anti-paper leak Bill
stories.summary: Raghav Chadha spoke in Rajya Sabha supporting the anti-paper leak Bill. He stressed institutional solutions are needed to resolve the crisis. The Bill introduces stricter penalties for paper leaks and exam malpractices. Individuals face jail terms and significant fines for unfair means. Parliament approved the Public Examination Amendment Bill after Lok Sabha clearance.

stories.title: Tiny reef fish thrived near seabird islands; where rats wiped birds out, marine food chains changed
stories.summary: Tropical islands are facing a surprising ecological shift as invasive rats disrupt the balance of coral reef ecosystems. By decimating seabird numbers, these rats cut down on essential nutrient contributions to the reefs. As a result, tiny cryptobenthic fish flourish in nutrient-rich spots, while invertebrates find success in less fertile regions, reshaping the food web and highlighting the vulnerable nature of these priceless underwater habitats.

stories.title: 'First you broke their bones, now filing FIRs': Rahul Gandhi warns PM Modi, Amit Shah to not 'threaten Gen Z into silence'
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi criticized Prime Minister Modi and Home Minister Shah for actions against students. He alleged the government is silencing Generation Z through FIRs and account takedowns. Gandhi demanded a Supreme Court-monitored probe into alleged police brutality at Jantar Mantar. Opposition MPs also protested alleged police action and financial irregularities. The protests occurred before a bill on public examinations was considered.

stories.title: 'Your skin brighter than country's future': Abhijeet Dipke's jab at PM Modi's late night video
stories.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, CJP founder, mocked Prime Minister Narendra Modi's recent video message. The Prime Minister discussed the new anti-paper leak Bill passed by Parliament. This legislation aims to create a more reliable examination system for students. PM Modi highlighted decades of paper leak issues affecting governments nationwide. The government is implementing reforms and using technology to ensure exam integrity.

stories.title: Spain migrant crisis: Military deployed as thousands cross border; 9 killed
stories.summary: Spain deployed its military to Ceuta after thousands of migrants crossed from Morocco. The sudden influx overwhelmed security forces, leading to a severe border crisis. Authorities confirmed an agreement with Morocco for the return of illegal migrants. The reason for the surge remains unclear, with various factors suggested. Ceuta, a Spanish enclave, is a key point for migration into Europe.

stories.title: 10 climbers, including Nirmal Purja, missing after avalanche on Broad Peak in PoK's Gilgit-Baltistan
stories.summary: Ten international climbers, including renowned Nepal-born mountaineer Nirmal Purja are missing after an avalanche struck Broad Peak. A tracking device shows Purja's location has shifted, offering a small hope for rescuers. Poor weather has so far prevented helicopters from taking off, delaying aerial search-and-rescue operations. Authorities were preparing to deploy helicopters on Friday morning if weather conditions improved.

stories.title: Russian strikes across Ukraine kill 10; missiles hit Poland too
stories.summary: Russian missile and drone attacks killed at least ten civilians, including children, and injured over fifty. Nato scrambled warplanes after a Russian missile briefly crossed into Poland's western airspace. Ukrainian President Zelensky stated North Korean missiles were used in the attack on Thursday. Russia targeted Ukrainian air bases and arms factories, while Ukraine attacked Russia's oil sector.

stories.title: xAI sues US state over law banning 'nudification' tech
stories.summary: Elon Musk's xAI company has sued Minnesota over its new law. This law bans AI nudification technology on websites and applications. The lawsuit challenges the state's authority to regulate AI-generated content. xAI argues the law is too broad and unconstitutional. The case could set a precedent for AI regulation by states.

stories.title: Man hikes out of mountains to get help after getting impaled by a trekking pole
stories.summary: A nurse impaled himself on a trekking pole while climbing Montana's highest peak. He decided to self-rescue after assessing his condition and considering costs. The group carefully descended the mountain for over six hours. They reached a vehicle and drove to a clinic, then a hospital. Doctors removed the pole, and the nurse returned to work.

stories.title: Parts of Manusmriti now part of 'curriculum', says Mallikarjun Kharge
stories.summary: Rajya Sabha saw a heated debate during the Public Examinations Bill discussion. Opposition leader Mallikarjun Kharge cited Manusmriti, alleging its influence on BJP's curriculum. JP Nadda challenged Kharge to produce the original manuscript for authentication. Kharge quoted alleged discriminatory verses against Shudras from the ancient text. BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi countered, referencing Ambedkar's writings on the era.

stories.title: NEET leak row: Opposition politicising issue, government has brought in strict law, says BJP
stories.summary: Government MPs criticized opposition for politicizing the NEET-UG paper leak issue. They highlighted government dialogue with students and a proposed stronger law. Senior ministers held talks with students and activist Sonam Wangchuk. A fast-track court and task force were established to address concerns. The proposed bill aims for stringent punishment and time-bound investigations.

stories.title: ‘Normal’ July rain defies forecast of El Nino impact
stories.summary: India's July monsoon rainfall exceeded expectations, defying earlier forecasts of below-normal precipitation. This unexpected recovery eased fears of a significant monsoon shortfall for the nation. However, rainfall distribution remained uneven across different regions of the country. Experts now emphasize that El Nino alone cannot explain India's changing rainfall behaviour. Climate change is increasingly altering monsoon patterns, making predictions more complex.

stories.title: Why’s CJI not on panel to pick CEC, Supreme Court asks government
stories.summary: The Supreme Court questioned Parliament's decision to exclude the Chief Justice of India from the selection panel. Justices noted the CJI's inclusion in other key appointment committees. The court heard arguments challenging the 2023 Act's appointment process. The government urged the court not to question legislative wisdom. The bench clarified it was not questioning the Prime Minister's trustworthiness.

stories.title: Why is DeenTheGreat reportedly facing up to 15 years in prison? Streamer’s lawyer makes fresh claim
stories.summary: Streamer DeenTheGreat, whose real name is Nurideen Shabazz, is facing felony robbery and misdemeanor battery charges linked to an alleged yacht incident in Miami. If convicted, he could face up to 15 years in prison. His lawyer says prosecutors are expected to dismiss the case soon, but the charges remain active ahead of his August 4 court hearing.

stories.title: Despite unrest, PM Modi, Amit Shah haven't spoken on NEET protests: Opposition
stories.summary: Rajya Sabha saw a political storm after Mallikarjun Kharge questioned Amit Shah's absence and silence. He clarified his remarks meant people's power for accountability, not physical force. Opposition MPs questioned the effectiveness of the new anti-paper leak bill. Several parties demanded the government scrap the NEET exam. The debate highlighted ongoing concerns about student protests and exam integrity.

stories.title: Trump announces 'historic' Gaza deal as Board of Peace agrees on Hamas disarmament
stories.summary: Donald Trump announced a historic agreement for Hamas disarmament and Israeli withdrawal. This phased deal will establish a new Palestinian administration in Gaza. The Board of Peace facilitated this monumental step toward lasting peace and security. Mediators Egypt, Qatar, and Türkiye were thanked for their important efforts. Gaza will no longer pose a security threat after this significant progress.

stories.title: Anti-paper leak bill clears Parliament; PM Modi says it will build a credible exam system
stories.summary: Parliament approved a bill to amend the anti-paper leak law. This legislation introduces stricter punishments for individuals involved in exam malpractices. Prime Minister Modi stated this is a crucial step for a credible exam system. The bill proposes significant jail terms and substantial fines for offenders. It also empowers governments to establish special fast-track courts for these cases.

stories.title: 16 Indians, including 10 seamen, killed in Middle East conflict: Government
stories.summary: Sixteen Indian nationals, including ten seafarers, have died in the West Asia conflict. Seventy-five other Indian nationals sustained injuries in the same regional conflict. In a separate incident, twelve Indian nationals perished at Qatar's Ras Laffan Gas Facility. The government is coordinating with host nations to repatriate mortal remains. Injured individuals received medical treatment and necessary assistance from Indian missions.

stories.title: Parliament passes Vande Mataram bill
stories.summary: Parliament passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Bill on Thursday. This amendment extends legal protection to the national song Vande Mataram. The DMK opposed the bill, citing concerns about national division and imposition. The BJP defended the amendment, emphasizing respect for the complete Vande Mataram song. This action places Vande Mataram on par with the national anthem for legal protection.

stories.title: Release 3,500 cusecs of water to Tamil Nadu: Cauvery authority to Karnataka
stories.summary: The Cauvery Water Management Authority ordered Karnataka to release 3,500 cusecs daily. This directive mandates a total release of 4 TMC of water to Tamil Nadu. Karnataka had appealed the committee's order citing low reservoir levels and drought conditions. State officials stated reservoir levels were significantly lower than last year. Tamil Nadu representatives argued against Karnataka's plea, citing sufficient flow.

stories.title: BJP submits breach of privilege notice against Rahul Gandhi
stories.summary: BJP submitted a privilege notice against Rahul Gandhi in Lok Sabha. He is accused of demeaning Parliament and insulting citizens with his remarks. BJP seeks an unconditional apology from the Congress leader. The notice cites rules regarding defamatory allegations against individuals. The matter has been sent to the privilege committee for inquiry.

stories.title: Ukraine dials India, seeks peace role amid ship attack concerns
stories.summary: India's External Affairs Minister discussed Black Sea shipping attacks with Ukraine's counterpart. He reiterated India's stance that such attacks are unacceptable and unequivocally condemned. The minister also highlighted the global impact of multiple conflicts on security. Ukraine's representative briefed him on recent developments and peace efforts. India consistently advocates for dialogue and diplomacy to resolve conflicts.

stories.title: 215 academicians slam Priyanka for 'gaumutra' remark
stories.summary: Over two hundred academicians have written an open letter criticizing Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's remark. They stated that dismissing scholars with labels undermines the nation's scientific temper. The academicians defended the IIT Madras director's advocacy of cow urine's potential benefits. They emphasized that scientific temper involves objective examination of claims before acceptance. Mockery is not a substitute for reasoned engagement in public debate, they added.

stories.title: From 617 to 2,000 in 2025, Indians deported from US triple since 2023
stories.summary: Four hundred fourteen Indians faced deportation from the US by March 2026. Deportations from the US significantly increased from 2023 to 2025. The United Kingdom and Cyprus also deported Indians, with fifty-seven and fifty-three respectively. Government data shows thousands of unregistered agents were notified on the eMigrate portal. Indian truckers arrested in Arizona are also facing deportation proceedings.

stories.title: After PM row, new Meta protocols for VIP accounts
stories.summary: Meta has introduced new protocols for handling prominent individuals' accounts. This follows the temporary removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Facebook video. The company expressed regret and is examining the reasons behind the video's removal. Government officials are scheduled to meet with Meta's global representatives soon. Discussions will cover policy and technical aspects of the incident.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Khaled Hosseini: 'A man who has no conscience, no goodness, does not suffer' and why guilt is the starting point for redemption
Middle East conflict: PM Modi reviews safety of seafarers, supply chain constraints
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired a special security meeting concerning the West Asia crisis. He directed the establishment of a mechanism to aid seafarers and their families. Discussions also covered ensuring uninterrupted fertilizer supply for the upcoming rabi season. The government's strategy to diversify energy sources has mitigated risks effectively. A whole-of-government approach is being continued to safeguard citizens' interests.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Pablo Picasso: "When I was as old as these children, I could draw like Raphael, but it took me a lifetime to learn to…"
stories.summary: Pablo Picasso admired children's uninhibited artistic expression and their natural imagination. He believed true mastery combined technical skill with this fearless approach. Older artists often lose this freedom due to fear of judgment and criticism. Picasso's journey shows simplicity achieved through experience is a higher achievement. Rediscovering this childlike curiosity is key to lifelong innovation and creativity.

stories.title: Supreme Court: No blanket ban on use of pellet guns for crowd control
stories.summary: The Supreme Court ordered the Delhi government to treat all injured protesters. It questioned the feasibility of banning pellet guns for crowd control. The court directed the preservation of ammunition logs for effective investigation. It also emphasized the need for police to have adequate safety gear. The bench reiterated that peaceful protests can sometimes be hijacked by miscreants.

stories.title: Quote by Bertrand Russell: 'There are two motives for reading a book; one, that you enjoy it...'
stories.summary: Reading serves a dual purpose: it offers personal satisfaction while also catering to the desire for intellectual recognition among peers. This blend of motivations can drive individuals to choose books based on public perception rather than genuine interest. Psychological theories identify this as the contrast between intrinsic and extrinsic motivations. In our digital age, online platforms enhance this performative nature of reading.

stories.title: Space department and Isro begins hiring for 746 posts, 92 will be scientist/engineers
stories.summary: Isro and DoS have initiated a significant recruitment drive for 746 positions. These openings include regular posts and apprenticeship opportunities for future talent. The drive aims to address a notable vacancy rate within the space department. Administrative roles and scientist/engineer positions are being filled across various centers. This effort seeks to bolster Isro's workforce and operational capabilities.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Anton Chekhov: 'If you are afraid of loneliness, don't marry', and a surprising take on human psychology and relationships
Jammu and Kashmir: Government clears funds for pellet survivor Insha’s gas agency after 8-year wait
stories.summary: The J&K government approved a gas agency for Insha Mushtaq eight years later. This rehabilitation pledge was approved on Thursday, reviving a commitment made in 2016. Insha lost her eyesight at fourteen after a pellet gun incident during protests. She has since learned Braille and is pursuing a bachelor's degree. The approval marks a significant turning point for her future.

stories.title: 23 heritage sites in Ladakh declared protected monuments
stories.summary: Ladakh's Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena declared twenty-three heritage sites protected monuments. This initiative provides legal protection for Ladakh's rich archaeological and historical heritage. Sites in Leh and Kargil districts were notified as protected monuments under a specific act. The administration will now undertake conservation measures and prevent encroachments on these sites. This move reflects a commitment to preserving Ladakh's unique historical legacy for future generations.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Leo Tolstoy: 'Everyone thinks of changing the world, but no one...'
stories.summary: According to Leo Tolstoy, true societal change begins with personal evolution. He asserted that individuals must first address their own imperfections. This mindset has significantly shaped leaders like Mahatma Gandhi and Martin Luther King Jr. However, in our contemporary society, there is a trend toward prioritizing external grievances over internal growth. To achieve meaningful advancements, it is essential to blend personal honesty with systemic change.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Properties of 5 Pakistan-based terrorist handlers attached in Reasi
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Police attached properties belonging to five Pakistan-based terrorist handlers in Reasi district. This action aims to prevent the misuse of these assets for terror financing activities. The attached land was linked to a case registered under stringent anti-terror laws. Investigations revealed the accused had exfiltrated to Pakistan for terrorist training and now operate as handlers.

stories.title: Scientists transplanted 42 sea sponges into a polluted Spanish marina; 91.7% of one species survived
stories.summary: In a remarkable experiment, scientists have introduced sea sponges into a polluted marina in Spain to investigate their resilience. The chicken kidney sponge, a particularly robust species, not only survived for an impressive 455 days but also showcased its remarkable ability to reproduce mobile clones. These developments indicate that sponges may play a critical role in ecological restoration, potentially aiding in the detoxification of contaminated coastal areas.

stories.title: Before they were famous: “The moment you think you’ve made it, you stop growing”: How did Kai Cenat become one of the biggest streamers in the world?
stories.summary: Kai Cenat’s rise began with comedy videos on Instagram before expanding to YouTube, joining AMP, and later becoming one of Twitch’s biggest stars. His success came through years of consistent work rather than one viral moment. Today, his personality, audience connection, and creative live streams have made him one of the most influential digital creators in the world.

stories.title: Vikram Misri meets Bhutan counterpart, reviews India-backed development projects
Burnham says he told Trump UK would take 'pragmatic approach' on North Sea oil
Boreal forests shade permafrost so effectively that summer thaw stays about one metre shallower
stories.summary: Thick forest canopies keep northern permafrost cool, safeguarding vast carbon stores. This natural shade prevents soil thawing and the release of greenhouse gases. Researchers discovered this vital cooling service has been largely overlooked in climate models. Losing these forests means losing this crucial protection for underground carbon. Protecting these boreal forests is therefore extremely important for global climate stability.

stories.title: 'Children's future won't be compromised': PM Modi hails anti-paper leak Bill in new late-night video
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced Parliament passed a new bill to prevent unfair means in public examinations. This legislation aims to build a more trustworthy examination system across the nation. The government has taken continuous steps to improve examination processes and address paper leaks. This new law will ensure no paper leak mafia or gang playing with students' futures is spared.

stories.title: Calling registered AYUSH doctors 'quacks' has no legal basis: NCISM
stories.summary: The National Commission for Indian System of Medicine issued a warning regarding AYUSH doctors. It stated that calling registered practitioners 'quacks' lacks legal basis. Such descriptions may infringe upon their constitutional and professional rights. Duly qualified and registered AYUSH doctors are legally recognized healthcare professionals. The commission reiterated that these practitioners deserve legal protection and respect.

stories.title: Montana man impales himself on trekking pole, hikes 10 miles to safety instead of calling helicopter
stories.summary: A hiking trip to Montana's highest mountain turned into a remarkable survival story after a nurse accidentally impaled himself on a trekking pole but still managed to hike nearly 10 miles to safety instead of waiting for a helicopter rescue. There, surgeons safely removed the trekking pole and treated the wound. Just days later, Cifaldi had already returned to work.

stories.title: Arizona Sheriff rejects Kash Patel's claim that FBI was kept out of Nancy Guthrie probe for four days
Bangladesh's request to extradite Sheikh Hasina 'being examined', Centre tells Parliament panel
'Marriage of convenience' by Indian students in Canada mentioned in internal email: Even advertised on dating apps
Woman injured during NEET protest discharged from RML after 10 days
Quote of the day by Joan of Arc: "All I have done is by Our Lord's command… I have done nothing in the world but…"
stories.summary: Joan of Arc attributed her extraordinary courage to divine command, not personal ambition. She faced her trial with humility, placing all credit with God. Her conviction provided strength through imprisonment and intense pressure. Purpose, rather than recognition, fueled her unwavering dedication to her mission. This historical figure's story continues to resonate due to her steadfast faith.

stories.title: Scientists drilled 1,640 feet beneath Michigan and found 689 kinds of fungi living in water
stories.summary: A fascinating discovery in Michigan reveals 689 fungal species living in ancient groundwater that hasn't touched the surface since the last Ice Age 11,000 years ago. This unique ecosystem, concealed within deep rocks and water, also harbors tiny organisms like worms and tardigrades. Such findings could revolutionize our understanding of subsurface life and fundamentally alter how scientists track the movement of underground carbon.

stories.title: 'Can pellet guns be used against peaceful protesters under any circumstances?' CJP slams SC
China spent $13.8B restoring wetlands—benefits now valued up to $434B
stories.summary: China's coastal wetland restoration projects between 2000 and 2020 showed substantial economic gains. Investments of up to $13.8 billion generated ecosystem benefits valued as high as $434 billion. Mangrove restoration projects, in particular, offered exceptional benefit-cost ratios of 47 to 1. These restored wetlands provide vital carbon storage and coastal protection services. The research highlights restoration as a valuable nature-based solution for climate action.

stories.title: Tourist feeding helped push Japan’s famous Rabbit Island beyond its natural limits
stories.summary: The unchecked practice of tourists feeding rabbits on Okunoshima has led to an overwhelming rise in their population, creating serious ecological concerns. This steady food source is altering animal behaviors, with wild boars starting to hunt rabbits more frequently. The plant life suffers, evident in the stark 'rabbit line' marking the landscape. Experts suggest implementing regulated feeding practices and formulating long-term conservation strategies for the island.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi under fire: Anurag Thakur moves privilege notice over Lok Sabha speech
Why Bankipur bypoll grabbed national attention and what it means for Prashant Kishor
'How is unelected minister continuing for over six months?' SC raps Bihar govt
stories.summary: The Supreme Court questioned the Bihar government regarding a minister's continued service. This minister has served beyond the six-month constitutional limit without legislative election. The court seeks an explanation for this continuation under Article 164(4) of the Constitution. A petition challenges the minister's reappointment after a government change. The court referenced a prior judgment on similar constitutional provisions.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia's one-year multiple-entry Umrah visa explained
'You need to go home': Canada leader reacts to protesting Indian student of Portage College, says 'our view is that...'
From LPG to Rabi fertilisers: PM Modi reviews Middle East crisis preparedness
China has added 447,500 Sq km of planted forest, but lost 219,100 sq km of natural forest
stories.summary: China's large-scale tree planting programmes helped increase overall forest cover over three decades, but a new study says they also coincided with growing fragmentation of natural forests. Researchers found plantations often expanded near natural forest edges, breaking up connected habitats. The study also found China's Natural Forest Protection Program helped slow this fragmentation in protected areas.

stories.title: Hyderabad techie killed in US road accident days before India trip
15 elephants suspected to have died after eating pesticide-sprayed tomatoes near Kenya's Amboseli National Park
NEET-UG 2026 case: CBI links leak to teachers who set paper, did translation work - report
stories.summary: In a shocking revelation, subject experts are accused of memorizing and leaking NEET-UG 2026 exam questions after receiving daily access from home. These reconstructed queries found their way into private coaching classes, with a beautician reportedly formatting them for sale. The scheme's spread across multiple states is now under scrutiny, leading the CBI to file a chargesheet against thirteen individuals implicated in this alleged scam.

stories.title: In 1600, Oaken Wood was already an established English woodland; in 2026 Kent proposed quarrying...
stories.summary: Kent County Council intends to extract stone from Oaken Wood, an ancient woodland rich in rare flora and fauna. Detractors express deep concern over the irreversible damage to this precious ecosystem in the pursuit of building materials. The removal of soil won't bring back what is lost. A public consultation is set to determine the future of this plan, weighing community opinions heavily before final approval.

stories.title: California woman bitten by rattlesnake taken to hospital by husband after three 911 calls fail
stories.summary: A Californian woman experienced a rattlesnake bite during her gardening routine, highlighting the perils of nature. Unfortunately, her attempts to reach out for help via 911 were met with failure, prompting her husband to drive her to the nearest hospital swiftly. Experts reveal an increase in venomous snake incidents statewide, urging the public to stay composed and obtain timely medical care in the aftermath of bites.

stories.title: India's solar problem isn't generation anymore. It's what to do with all that power
4 migrants die attempting to cross English Channel on overloaded 'taxi boats'
Evening news wrap: Lok Sabha passes Vande Mataram Bill, Iran says destroyed 3 US F-35 jets & more
Saturn’s largest moon Titan experiences clouds, rain, rivers and changing seasons like Earth
stories.summary: Titan showcases an intriguing, elongated seasonal pattern due to Saturn's leisurely orbit. This fascinating moon is shrouded in a dense atmosphere with liquid methane rapidly flowing on its surface. Insights gathered from the Cassini spacecraft highlight not only the dynamic weather changes but also the enigmatic disappearance of lakes on Titan. Observations of varied wind directions and shifting sand dunes unveil the moon's remarkable seasonal climate transformations.

stories.title: Meet Matthew Myerscough: The man who survived a 20-minute avalanche and discovered a 201-million-year-old sea dragon
Vande Mataram Bill clears Parliament as Kharge, Nadda lock horns in RS - key highlights
Quote of the day by Bhagat Singh: ‘Study so that you are able to meet the arguments of your opponents,’ and why knowledge is the strongest answer to disagreement
stories.summary: In his advice, Bhagat Singh champions the importance of informed study as a tool for constructive disagreement. Engaging with significant questions thoughtfully allows for deeper discussions, moving past simplistic slogans. This intellectual approach not only makes debates more fruitful but also enhances one's ability to effect lasting change and embrace civic responsibility.

stories.title: Govt summons Meta executives again over temporary restriction of PM Modi's Facebook post
stories.summary: India's government has summoned Meta executives to explain a temporary restriction on Prime Minister Modi's video. The social media giant acknowledged the error and has restored the content. New protocols are being introduced for prominent public figures' accounts. This incident highlights ongoing scrutiny of content moderation by tech firms. The government seeks explanations for platform governance and content handling.

stories.title: Indian-American couple announces graduate fellowship for University of Texas students, says it's 'simply an open door'
stories.summary: Indian-American philanthropists are making significant contributions to American universities this year. Anil Kochhar and his wife Marilyn paid the education loans for graduating students at North Carolina State University. Jyoti and Nishi Bhatia established an endowment for graduate fellowships at the University of Texas. This fellowship will support students with expanded resources and financial aid. The Bhatias hope their contribution will inspire future generosity among recipients.

stories.title: Priyanka's 'gaumutra expert' remark stirs row, over 200 academicians slam LS MP
E20 petrol can reduce vehicle mileage by up to 6%: Nitin Gadkari in Parliament
stories.summary: E20 petrol may reduce vehicle mileage by two to six percent. Extensive testing has found no engine failures linked to this fuel. Studies indicate improved acceleration and better ride quality with E20. Carbon emissions are reduced by approximately thirty percent compared to E10. Automobile manufacturers continue to honor warranty claims for vehicles using E20.

stories.title: For centuries, scientists couldn't explain why flamingos aren't born pink until a breakthrough in the 1960s revealed the answer
stories.summary: Flamingos obtain their striking pink color from dietary carotenoids found in algae and brine shrimp. These pigments are converted by the birds into compounds that accumulate in their feathers. Young flamingos hatch with muted colors and gradually develop pink as they mature. Different species exhibit varying shades of pink based on their specific food sources. This coloration plays a vital role in their survival and reproductive success.

stories.title: Invasive Mussels cleaned Great Lakes, but put native Whitefish at risk of vanishing forever
stories.summary: Invasive zebra and quagga mussels have transformed the Great Lakes ecosystem by reducing the tiny organisms that young lake whitefish depend on for food. While the mussels made the water cleaner, they disrupted the food chain, causing whitefish numbers to fall sharply. Scientists warn the species could vanish from some areas within five years.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Amal Clooney: "There is lots of my work that takes place behind closed doors that is…" – the hidden truth about dedication and lasting success
stories.summary: Amal Clooney highlights that much important legal work remains unseen by the public. Most of her efforts involve private meetings and extensive case preparation. This hidden groundwork forms the essential foundation for any successful outcome. The quote encourages valuing the entire process, not just the final visible result. This perspective applies broadly to many professions and their quiet dedication.

stories.title: Jharkhand CM writes to PM over Rs 700-crore scholarship funding gap, seeks urgent intervention
Japan's latest earthquake damages Kumamoto Castle, the 400-year-old fortress still battling nature after centuries of survival
Meet Ryder Williams: The 16-year-old lifeguard who saved a drowning boy from towering California waves and was invited to the White House by Donald Trump for a civilian honour
Arika Kundu, 13, turns peanut shell waste into pesticide remover, competes for $25,000 prize
stories.summary: Thirteen-year-old Minnesota student Arika Kundu has designed a method that uses discarded peanut shells to help remove pesticide residues from fresh fruits and vegetables. Her project, called LIGNEX, has made her one of 10 finalists in the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge. She will now compete for the $25,000 grand prize with guidance from a 3M scientist.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Franz Kafka: ‘By believing passionately in something that still does not exist, we create it,’ and why imagination is the first step towards innovation
stories.summary: Innovation and change are ignited by imagination, as our belief in the unseen brings them to life. Many realities begin as mere concepts in the mind before emerging into existence. Breakthroughs frequently arise from ideas that others deem impossible, often met with skepticism. These ideas need nurturing and persistence, evolving through revision while overcoming disappointments. Our future materializes first in our dreams before it becomes a part of our reality.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Jane Goodall: Why "Even that great scientist Albert Einstein sustained a mystical outlook on life" reminds us that wonder and humility go hand in hand
US court orders deportation of Indian national Mitul Patel after sentencing in visa fraud case
Study finds monkeys recognise shapes in ways surprisingly similar to humans
stories.summary: New research indicates monkeys and humans process geometric shapes similarly. This suggests geometric intuition evolved long before modern humans appeared. Rotated shapes revealed abstract reasoning abilities in monkeys and children. The study found shared cognitive mechanisms rather than separate systems. Human geometric abilities build upon primate foundations, not entirely new reasoning.

stories.title: 'May do same with Army': Opposition attacks BJP for India Hockey's saffron jersey
US Senate unanimously opposes Presidential pardon for Epstein associate Ghislaine Maxwell
'20 traitors of Bengal': TMC's Kalyan Banerjee wears poster with rebel MPs' photos in Parl, seeks swift ECI decision
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress MP Kalyan Banerjee protested against 20 rebel MPs in Parliament. These defectors joined the Nationalist Citizens Party of India, pledging support to the NDA. The Trinamool Congress has labeled these MPs as traitors for their actions. Rebel MPs had approached the Election Commission regarding the party split. A swift decision is needed to resolve the ongoing political uncertainty.

stories.title: In 1898, Tesla’s mysterious boat stunned New York with a secret wireless invention
World’s oldest near-complete Roman armour may reveal a lost soldier’s fate
stories.summary: Archaeologists conserved an intact Roman armour suit from the Kalkriese battlefield. This armour represents the earliest known lorica segmentata, revealing sophisticated engineering. CT scans helped uncover the armour's hidden structure without causing damage. A Roman restraint found with the armour raises questions about a captured soldier. The discovery provides a rare personal glimpse into a disastrous Roman military campaign.

stories.title: Seattle police chief Shon Barnes fired over absence during mass shooting that killed 3
Qatari Diar lists $64 million London penthouse at redeveloped Chelsea Barracks site
stories.summary: A new duplex penthouse at London's Chelsea Barracks is now for sale. This luxury property is listed for forty-eight million pounds, making it very expensive. The development transformed a historic British Army barracks into a high-end residential neighborhood. Buyers can move into the fully furnished home which includes extensive outdoor terraces. This listing highlights London's ultra-prime housing market's renewed momentum.

stories.title: eBay to pay $56 million to settle harassment lawsuit brought by US couple
Bhojshala complex row: SC asks government to provide nearby site for Friday namaz
Why did Marlon's ex break up with him? Heartbreaking reason behind Chanida's IG story explained
stories.summary: Marlon Lundgren Garcia and Chanida Natalie's engagement has officially come to an end. In an Instagram Story, Chanida shared the reason behind her decision, saying she couldn't stay with someone who wasn't over his ex. Her statement has also brought renewed attention to Marlon's past connection with streamer Yonna Jay, along with months of online speculation surrounding their relationship history and recent engagement.

stories.title: Washington teenager wins $75,000 after creating sponge to trap salmon-killing tyre pollutant
stories.summary: An eighteen-year-old student developed a jute waste sponge for pollution control. This innovation removes a toxic tire pollutant harming salmon in waterways. The biodegradable sponge offers a sustainable and low-cost filtration alternative. It effectively filters 6PPD-quinone and other contaminants from water. This project won a major science award for its environmental impact.

stories.title: 'Remains an active site': Delhi Police dismiss rumours of Jantar Mantar closure
stories.summary: The Delhi Police has refuted rumors circulating on social media regarding the closure of Jantar Mantar, confirming it remains an approved site for lawful demonstrations. According to court rulings, up to one thousand individuals may gather there for protests. Permissions are issued based on formal requests and must comply with specified conditions. Authorities advise the public to trust official channels for accurate updates about protest activities.

stories.title: 'Join BJP to avoid trouble for family': CJP's Dipke alleges threats, says Centre 'supports rapists'
Inside China's new $517 million natural history museum that takes visitors from the cosmos to human evolution, featuring meteorites, dinosaurs and a river-inspired design
stories.summary: Shenzhen Natural History Museum opened on July 28, 2026, becoming southern China's first major institution dedicated to natural history. The museum's design draws inspiration from a river delta, creating a flowing, curvilinear structure. Visitors will journey from the cosmos through Earth's history and dinosaur eras and eventually learn about the delicate balance of our natural world.

stories.title: Space for secular thought in Bangladesh has shrunk: Exiled writer Taslima Nasreen ahead of Kolkata return
Twitch Streamer Mitch Jones faces legal threat after recreating $500K Deal or No Deal game show
stories.summary: Twitch streamer Mitch Jones says he received a cease and desist just days after hosting a real-life version of Deal or No Deal featuring Sodapoppin, Nmplol, and cash prizes worth up to $500,000. According to Mitch, the official production demanded money over the unauthorized recreation of the show's format. No lawsuit has been reported so far, and there has been no public resolution as of July 30.

stories.title: An Oklahoma wind farm is creating an invisible river of wind that reaches much higher than scientists once thought
stories.summary: Scientists mapped wind farm wakes in Oklahoma with detailed observations. The study revealed upward momentum transfer extending far beyond turbine blades. These atmospheric disturbances spread vertically, creating a "river of wind" effect. Low-level jets and gravity waves influenced wake recovery significantly. Findings will improve future wind energy production and farm layout models.

stories.title: 'Home minister can't hide behind closed doors': Kharge attacks Centre on anti-paper leak Bill
NCP to merge with Sharad Pawar faction? What party veteran Chhagan Bhujbal said
stories.summary: Speaking to reporters during a visit to Pune, the Maharashtra minister was asked whether the rival NCP factions could come together. Responding to the question, Bhujbal said the decision rested with party president Sunetra Pawar and suggested there was little point in debating the matter until the leadership took a call.

stories.title: King Charles cracks an joke after being told he ‘looks good’
stories.summary: During the RHS Sandringham Flower Show, King Charles embraced the challenges of ageing with humor while discussing his cancer treatment and progress. His heartfelt remarks resonated, especially when he was likened to his mother, Queen Elizabeth. This appearance, alongside Queen Camilla, showcases his honest and approachable demeanor in royal engagements.

stories.title: In 2008, MSU scientists discovered a tiny fungus hiding inside a rainforest tree that naturally produced diesel-like fuel
JasonTheWeen gets thrashed by Ryan Garcia after claiming he could "beat the f*ck out of" him
stories.summary: Ryan Garcia and Twitch streamer JasonTheWeen finally settled their online trash talk inside a boxing ring. After claiming he could "beat the f*ck out of" the WBC welterweight champion, Jason stepped into a sparring session that turned heavily one-sided. The session ended early after his corner threw in the towel, before Garcia later shared advice and praised him for getting inside the ring.

stories.title: 'Expresses regret': Meta agrees to meet govt clarifying policy after PM Modi video glitch
New Zealand is investing $202 million in a mega-operation aimed at restoring three islands destroyed by invasive species
stories.summary: In an inspiring ecological restoration project, New Zealand is teaming up with Māori natives to tackle invasive mammal populations on three major islands, including Maukahuka, Rakiura, and the Chatham archipelago. This extensive collaboration among governmental bodies, local communities, and Indigenous organizations aims to breathe new life into native wildlife. The success of this project could highlight New Zealand's pioneering methods in environmental restoration on the world stage.

stories.title: Japan's 600-year-old Daisugi forestry method lets a single tree produce timber for centuries
stories.summary: Japan's 600-year-old Daisugi technique offers a unique way to produce timber without cutting down entire trees. Developed in Kyoto during the 14th century, the method allows a single cedar tree to grow multiple straight trunks that can be harvested for centuries. The ancient practice is now drawing attention as an example of sustainable forestry amid growing concerns over global deforestation

stories.title: A teenager stole five Civil War cannonballs from a historic Alabama fort and tried to fly home with them in a suitcase, but TSA caught the unusual haul
'Why is Amit Shah scared?' Rahul Gandhi on 'brutal' violence against student protesters
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi intensified his attack on Union home minister Amit Shah. He alleged that Shah's absence from Parliament reeks of guilt. Gandhi demanded a Supreme Court-monitored probe into alleged police brutalities. He shared videos purportedly showing police action against student protesters. Opposition MPs also protested alleged police action and temple donation embezzlement.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Clint Eastwood: "You have to steal a lot. You have to have a criminal mentality to be a…" - a fascinating lesson on creativity, influence and originality
stories.summary: Clint Eastwood suggests directors must absorb many influences to create original work. This involves studying techniques and styles from others, then adapting them. Real inspiration means transforming principles into something distinctly your own. Curiosity and personal perspective are key to genuine creative output. Experienced professionals continuously learn and build upon existing ideas.

stories.title: 11 police personnel, 15 militants killed in overnight attack in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
stories.summary: A major militant attack occurred overnight on a police post in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. Eleven police personnel and fifteen attackers died during the fierce exchange of gunfire. The Khazina police post in Hangu district was the target of this significant assault. Security forces fought back, killing the militants and repelling the attack. This incident highlights the ongoing rise in militant violence in the region.

stories.title: Africa is pouring in $50 billion to redirect water from Congo River Basin to Lake Chad which has shrunk by 90% since 1960
stories.summary: Lake Chad's dramatic shrinkage has brought about severe impacts on the lives of millions. To counteract this crisis, governments are investing in initiatives aimed at rehabilitating the lake's ecosystem. A noteworthy solution includes the ambitious Transaqua project, which seeks to channel water from the Congo River back into Lake Chad. This vital endeavor aims not only to replenish the lake but also to foster economic growth in the surrounding regions.

stories.title: The last woolly mammoths survived for 6,000 years after the Ice Age. In 2024, scientists challenged the idea that inbreeding caused their extinction
stories.summary: Recent genetic studies have revised the understanding of woolly mammoth extinction. These ancient DNA analyses suggest inbreeding alone did not cause their demise. The last mammoths on Wrangel Island survived for millennia despite genetic isolation. A sudden event, not gradual genetic decline, likely ended their final chapter. This research offers insights for modern endangered species conservation efforts.

stories.title: 'Criticise govt, don't denigrate India': Harish Salve on dissent and social media
stories.summary: Speaking at the AK Sen Memorial Lecture and Photograph Unveiling Ceremony organised by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA), Salve said holding those in power accountable is necessary in a constitutional democracy. Several senior members of the legal fraternity attended the ceremony. SCBA President and Senior Advocate Vikas Singh paid tribute to Sen's contribution to the legal profession, while Attorney General for India R. Venkataramani also spoke about his legacy.

stories.title: How a giant iceberg reached Iowa for Saudi Arabia's freshwater dream
stories.summary: A 1977 conference in Iowa explored transporting large icebergs for water. Saudi Arabia backed this event, seeking alternatives to desalination. An Alaskan iceberg was transported to Iowa for delegates to inspect. This unusual demonstration aimed to prove the concept's feasibility. The grand plan to tow Antarctic icebergs never fully materialized.

stories.title: Plaqueboymax vs Zoe Spencer controversy explained as streamer responds to homophobic F-slurs
stories.summary: Recent revelations of inappropriate Discord messages from Zoe Spencer aimed at Plaqueboymax have ignited discussions online. While some viewers critique or troll him, Plaqueboymax maintains his composure, asserting he won’t escalate the situation. This calm reaction has drawn mixed reactions, and notable creator Wardrobe has opted to unfollow Zoe amidst the ongoing controversy that continues to trend on social platforms.

stories.title: 'Proud of railways, want to be proud of govt promises too': Sonam Wangchuk hints at pending govt assurances
stories.summary: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk praised Indian Railways for its services. He urged the government to honor commitments made to student protesters. The recent NEET-UG paper leak debate was welcomed by the activist. Wangchuk also highlighted the success of peaceful non-violent resistance. The student-led agitation concluded after the government accepted key demands.

stories.title: An Italian man built a fake Roman amphitheatre, fooled tourists for nearly 10 years and charged €40 for guided tours
Trump invites teen lifeguard Ryder Williams to White House after heroic beach rescue
stories.summary: President Donald Trump has invited 16-year-old California lifeguard Ryder Williams and his family to the White House after the teenager rescued a young boy from powerful waves at Seabright State Beach. Trump said Williams deserves a high civilian honour for his bravery. The dramatic rescue, captured on video, has drawn widespread praise from officials, witnesses and social media users, with many calling the rookie lifeguard true hero

stories.title: Ethanol blending rolled out through phased, scientific process: Gadkari to Lok Sabha
Hidden deep within the Swiss Alps, this structure was built with 60,000 stone slabs to disappear into the mountain and is now considered one of the greatest works of modern architecture
stories.summary: Therme Vals situated in the Swiss Alps, was designed by Peter Zumthor in 1996. This structure hides within the rugged mountain landscape, using 60,000 local stone slabs. Visitors experience a cave-like atmosphere through dark passages and varied stone textures. This design respects the mountain ecosystem while providing a unique human experience.

stories.title: Meet Peter Beck: From NASA rejection to building a $2.9 billion rocket company
'Pellet guns can be used in exceptional situations': SC seeks RAF ammunition log from Jantar Mantar protest
stories.summary: The Supreme Court observed that when in extreme violent situations police are permitted to use bullets if violence does not get controlled by lathicharge and tear gas, how can they be barred from using pellet guns if a protest, which has turned violent after being hijacked by miscreants for ulterior purposes.

stories.title: This Swiss town will fine dog owners who do not wash away their pets' urine from streets and building facades
Is Pakistan facilitating Chinese missile shipments to Iran? Islamabad responds
stories.summary: Pakistan's military has strongly denied reports of facilitating Chinese weapons transit to Iran. These claims emerged amid ongoing tensions between Iran and the United States. The Pakistani army dismissed all such speculations as baseless and untrue. This situation highlights Pakistan's careful balancing act between China and Washington. The denial comes after reports suggested Iran would receive air defense systems soon.

stories.title: Inside Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg's $100 million-plus property empire spread across US
stories.summary: Mark Zuckerberg's real estate ventures span several remarkable properties within the USA. His portfolio showcases opulent compounds in Palo Alto and Hawaii, alongside grand estates in Lake Tahoe and Washington D.C. Recently, he broke records with the purchase of a Miami beach estate, emphasizing his attraction to expansive and secluded living environments. These acquisitions solidify Zuckerberg's reputation as a notable figure in the luxury property market.

stories.title: 'Students deserve justice': Rahul Gandhi shares video claiming police brutality during NEET protest
In 1995 Yellowstone began bringing back wolves; 30 years later young aspens returned, but the wider recovery remains uneven
stories.summary: Thirty years after wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone National Park, researchers say aspen trees are showing stronger signs of recovery. The findings add to growing evidence that restoring a top predator can reshape an entire ecosystem.

stories.title: An ancient Mexican city once home to 90,000 people vanished nearly 1,000 years ago. Scientists think a 650-year drought may explain why
Millions of birds follow a 9,000-kilometre invisible highway every year, crossing mountains, deserts and oceans without a map
850 exhibitors to take part in Delhi gifting, stationery expo
stories.summary: Paperworld Delhi, being held in the Capital for the first time after five editions in Mumbai, will focus on stationery, writing instruments, school and office supplies, art materials, paper products, packaging, educational solutions and workplace essentials. The exhibitions will also have dedicated spaces for start-ups, product innovations and sustainable solutions.

stories.title: US Iran War Live Updates: US-Iran conflict enters new phase with fresh strikes and stalled diplomacy
Getting 'carried away' again? Musk's million-dollar plan to rescue Trump in mid-elections
stories.summary: Elon Musk is reviving his political action committee, America PAC, for the 2026 elections. This group previously spent over $260 million to support Donald Trump's 2024 campaign. America PAC will now focus on increasing Republican voter turnout through various outreach methods. The organization plans to collaborate with other Republican groups to boost their efforts. Musk's involvement signals a significant financial push for the GOP's midterm goals.

stories.title: 'Even Mughals called Shivaji a chuha': Uddhav likens Gen Z to Maratha warrior
Quote of the day by Tiger Woods: "Talent is something you are born with, and a skill is something you…" - a lesson on why practice matters more than natural ability
stories.summary: Tiger Woods emphasizes that skill, not just talent, drives success in golf. He argues that consistent practice and discipline build essential skills over time. Woods himself exemplifies this by dedicating decades to relentless training and improvement. Natural ability provides a starting point, but sustained effort determines ultimate achievement. This lesson applies broadly, highlighting the power of deliberate practice in any field.

stories.title: Shared beds, shrinking budgets: China’s young workers feel economic squeeze
stories.summary: Young Chinese workers are sharing beds to reduce living expenses. This practice highlights growing financial pressures and job insecurity among them. Stagnant wages and economic slowdown contribute to this difficult situation. Many young people lack stable employment and clear income prospects. This trend reflects a significant societal challenge for urban dwellers.

stories.title: US court convicts Salman Rushdie attacker of providing 'material support' to Hezbollah
stories.summary: A US man already serving a lengthy sentence was convicted on new federal charges. He was found guilty of providing material support to the militant group Hezbollah. Prosecutors linked his actions to a 1989 fatwa and a later speech. The author Salman Rushdie testified during the federal trial about the attack. This conviction adds to his existing sentence for attempted murder.

stories.title: Need to address some irritations in Bangladesh-India relations: Dhaka
stories.summary: Bangladesh foreign minister Khalilur Rahman met with the Indian envoy in Dhaka. He highlighted the need to resolve existing irritations in bilateral relations. The government is reviewing India's invitation for Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to the BRICS summit. Relations will advance based on sovereign equality and mutual interests. Both nations agree on resetting and moving forward their bilateral ties.

stories.title: Sri Lanka investigates Chinese triad angle in port city murder
stories.summary: A violent gang war erupted in Colombo Port City, Sri Lanka. This incident exposed potential links to a transnational cyber fraud network. Three Chinese nationals were ambushed and abducted while fishing on a bridge. One victim's body was later found blindfolded after the attack. Authorities are investigating and have increased security for Chinese residents.

stories.title: Supreme Court relaxes order mandating Coalgate appeals only before itself, allows Delhi high court to hear them
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has modified its prior order regarding coal block scam cases. Appeals against trial court acquittals or convictions can now go to Delhi High Court. This decision revises a twelve-year-old directive mandating all appeals in the Supreme Court. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal argued that the Supreme Court should not be the first appeal forum. The court agreed to categorize cases for future hearings starting August eighteenth.

stories.title: Automakers silent on E20 petrol due to government pressure: Kejriwal
stories.summary: Arvind Kejriwal claims the Centre pressures auto companies regarding E20 petrol. He alleges firms fear agency action if they disclose E20 risks. Kejriwal stated officials confirmed potential engine damage in older vehicles. Delhi BJP chief Harsh Malhotra challenged Kejriwal to present damaged vehicles. Malhotra demanded mechanic certification proving E20 caused the damage.

stories.title: Over 1 lakh schools in India functioning with a single teacher
stories.summary: More than one lakh schools operate with a single teacher nationwide. Andhra Pradesh leads with over sixteen thousand such institutions. This highlights significant teacher deployment gaps despite national averages. Vacancies arise from retirements, resignations, and changing student enrollments. States are advised to fill posts and use technology for needs.

stories.title: Supreme Court bars government from post facto green clearance to projects
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has protected projects worth Rs 20,000 crore from demolition. It permanently prohibited the government from granting post-facto environmental clearances. The court quashed a 2021 office memorandum that kept a window open indefinitely. Prior environmental clearance under the 2006 notification is now mandatory for all projects. The judgment will operate prospectively, validating past clearances granted under earlier rules.

stories.title: 2 years after death, Supreme Court clears former PM Manmohan Singh in Coalgate case
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has cleared former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh in a coal block scam case. This decision comes more than eleven years after a Delhi court summoned him as an accused. The court closed the case nearly two years after his demise in November 2024. The apex court quashed the trial court's order taking cognisance of the crime.

stories.title: Supreme Court curbs powers of SC panel, says it can’t pass adjudicatory orders
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled the National Commission for Scheduled Castes is advisory. It cannot pass binding adjudicatory orders in service-related matters. The commission can only send recommendations to the state or central government. It can inquire into complaints and record factual findings. However, it lacks the power to make final orders.

stories.title: ADGCA-ordered probe cleared Dreamliner fuel switch: Government
stories.summary: A Boeing probe found no abnormality in the B787 fuel control switch locking mechanism. This examination was ordered by the DGCA after a crew reported an issue post-landing. The switches control fuel supply and have faced scrutiny after a past crash incident. Further inspection of the complete thrust control module at the OEM facility is currently underway.

stories.title: IIT Bombay alumnus Jagdish Aphale named Ram temple trust’s first secretary, will oversee transactions
stories.summary: Jagdish Aphale, an IIT Bombay alumnus, has been appointed the Ayodhya Ram temple trust's first secretary. He will also serve as a joint signatory for financial transactions, enhancing accountability. This appointment follows recent resignations and alleged donation theft issues. Aphale previously supervised construction at the temple complex for nearly four years. His integration into the trust's internal processes has been ongoing for two weeks.

stories.title: Denied seat, student hacks IIT-Kanpur website to show his 'merit'
stories.summary: A BTech applicant hacked IIT Kanpur's website seeking admission consideration. He claimed he was denied a fair chance in the selection process. The IIT director invited the candidate to campus for an assessment. He stressed that hacking was not the correct approach to gain entry. The institute will consider him if genuine talent is demonstrated.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi remarks row: BJP hits back, calls Congress MP's claim 'a pack of lies'
stories.summary: The BJP strongly objects if Rahul Gandhi called students an idiot. They welcome the remark if it was self-directed by the Congress leader. BJP leaders accused Rahul Gandhi of spreading falsehoods and misleading the nation. They stated no bullets were fired during the student protests. The party highlighted government dialogue and efforts to strengthen laws against paper leaks.

stories.title: Now, just one visit for NEET-UG counselling
stories.summary: NEET-UG counselling now requires only one physical reporting for candidates seeking admission. Aspirants can complete subsequent document verification online while retaining their allotted seats. The Medical Counselling Committee also introduced online resignation for surrendered seats. NRI category admissions are now fully digitized, improving verification processes. The government aims for a transparent and merit-based counselling system.

stories.title: Delhi high court refuses HPV shots stay, but seeks Centre's response
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court declined to halt the HPV immunisation campaign. Authorities must now explain the vaccine's introduction within four weeks. The court emphasized the need for proper protocols before administering vaccines. A Public Interest Litigation raised concerns about long-term safety and consent. The next hearing for this matter is scheduled for October 29.

stories.title: Candace Owens drops unseen Charlie Kirk video, Alex Jones claims assassination story is ‘100% dead’
stories.summary: Candace Owens has released new rooftop footage that she says raises questions about whether Tyler Robinson was the person who shot Charlie Kirk. Alex Jones backed her claims, arguing the video contradicts the official case against Robinson. However, authorities still identify Robinson as the accused, and a judge has not yet ruled on whether the case will move to trial.

stories.title: Government: North-east cartels shifting towards synthetic drugs
stories.summary: Northeast drug syndicates are shifting towards synthetic drugs from Myanmar. They are increasingly using social media and encrypted apps for coordination. Traffickers exploit porous borders and forest routes for cross-border smuggling. Narcotics are concealed in legitimate cargo and passenger vehicles. Moreh-Tamu border remains a key transit point for these drugs.

stories.title: No district affected by Naxalism anymore: Ministry of home affairs
stories.summary: The number of Left-wing extremism-affected districts has fallen to zero by March 2026. This marks a significant reduction from 126 districts prior to April 2018. Maoist violence has seen a steep decline, with few incidents recorded this year. Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand remain the only states with reported Maoist incidents. However, 37 districts are still classified as legacy and thrust areas.

stories.title: With 90 out of 128 companies & 64% of investments, Karnataka top beneficiary of Centre's Electronics Development Fund
stories.summary: Karnataka received the most funding from the central government's Electronics Development Fund. The fund's associated venture funds invested over Rs 1,335 crore in 128 companies. Karnataka-based firms secured Rs 854.5 crore, representing nearly two-thirds of total investments. Telangana, Maharashtra, and Delhi also saw significant investments in technology startups. The fund, managed by Canbank Venture Capital Fund, is now in its divestment phase.

stories.title: Here's why many MBBS graduates can't take foreign licensing exams
stories.summary: Thousands of MBBS graduates cannot take foreign licensing exams. Their colleges have not secured ECFMG sponsor notes for global recognition. This formal note is essential for students seeking international medical practice opportunities. Many students discover this issue only after completing their medical degrees. The National Medical Commission is processing updates for several Indian medical colleges.

stories.title: 'Not going to let him get away': Rahul Gandhi targets Amit Shah over police action on NEET protesters; BJP says 'prove it or apologise'
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi accused Home Minister Amit Shah of police excesses against protesters. He demanded Shah's dismissal and a Supreme Court-monitored probe into the actions. Gandhi also blamed the RSS for the education sector's current problems. Government ministers challenged Gandhi to provide proof or issue an apology. The Lok Sabha experienced disruptions over these serious allegations.

stories.title: Quote of the day by The Notorious B.I.G: 'Stay far from timid, only make moves when your...'
stories.summary: Christopher Wallace, aka The Notorious B.I.G., imparted wisdom that resonates even after his passing. He emphasized the importance of pursuing authentic passions and being fearless in one's pursuit of dreams. Encouraging the belief that the sky's the limit, he highlighted ideals rooted in intrinsic motivation and bravery. His posthumous album embodies these lasting messages that continue to inspire generations.

stories.title: Amid opposition walkout, Rajya Sabha gives approval to Vande Mataram bill
stories.summary: The Rajya Sabha passed a bill proposing jail time for disrupting Vande Mataram. Opposition MPs walked out, demanding a statement on police action against protesters. Junior home minister Nityanand Rai piloted the bill, criticizing Congress's stance on the national song. MP Sanjay Singh questioned the RSS's past refusal to hoist the tricolour. AIADMK MPs noted the practice of playing state anthems after national songs.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Tupac Shakur: 'Death is not the greatest loss in life. The greatest loss is...'
stories.summary: Experiencing the decline of one's inner spirit while still existing is a significant tragedy. This internal defeat surpasses physical death, which is a part of life. The profound insights of Norman Cousins and Tupac Shakur resonate here. Psychologists associate this phenomenon with learned helplessness. To avoid burnout, it is essential to make conscious, daily decisions that nurture and maintain one's inner energy.

stories.title: Ahead of dengue vaccine rollout, all 4 strains found in circulation
stories.summary: India's first dengue virus mapping shows all four serotypes circulating in eight states. This finding could influence the country's upcoming dengue vaccine strategy. Researchers found DENV-2 to be the dominant circulating strain across the nation. Concurrent infections with multiple strains are linked to more severe dengue disease. Continuous molecular surveillance is essential for monitoring virus circulation and guiding policy.

stories.title: Guard's accidental gunshot kills man visiting bank in city
stories.summary: A customer was killed Tuesday after a security guard's gun discharged accidentally. Manish Kumar, a farmer, was updating his Aadhaar card at the Union Bank branch. The ex-serviceman guard, Vinod Kumar, was loading cartridges when the firearm discharged. The bullet struck Manish in the back, and he was rushed to the hospital. Police have arrested the guard and are investigating the incident further.

stories.title: Canada’s 2023 wildfires burned 15.1 million hectares and released 554 million tonnes of carbon
stories.summary: In 2023, Canada faced an unprecedented wildfire season that unleashed staggering carbon emissions from ancient underground soil and peat. These fires devastated extensive landscapes, liberating long-stored carbon accumulated over thousands of years. The challenge with subterranean fires lies in their resilience, transforming carbon sinks into sources of emissions, which exacerbates global warming and intensifies future wildfire risks.

stories.title: No ban on Jagannath movie, artists must enjoy creative liberty, says Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court rejected a plea to ban an animated film on Mahaprabhu Jagannath. Justices emphasized artists' creative expression and tolerance for depicting deities. They noted that preventing such depictions would halt many religious television programs. The court stated that the Censor Board's approval meant no judicial interference was needed. It refused to restrict artistic creativity based on the objections of a few.

stories.title: Twitch streamer Ludwig makes surprise cameo in Road to Empress 2 as Prince of Fuling in Chinese live-action visual novel
stories.summary: Popular streamer Ludwig has surprised fans with an unexpected appearance in Road to Empress 2. He portrays the Prince of Fuling, an envoy with long blonde hair and blue royal attire. Players can unlock this special character after completing the game's main story. This collaboration highlights innovative ways game developers connect with online creators. Ludwig's unique role offers a fun bonus for both his fans and gamers.

stories.title: Continue with your duties fearlessly, CRPF chief tells troopers amid pellet gun row
stories.summary: CRPF Director General G P Singh supports troops acting in good faith during duty. He assures responsibility for all decisions made in the public interest. An internal probe found standard operating procedures were followed by RAF personnel. Pellet guns were used after other crowd dispersal methods failed. This investigation may prevent charges against the RAF personnel involved.

stories.title: Lok Sabha passes anti-paper leak bill after row over Rahul Gandhi's remarks
stories.summary: The Lok Sabha passed a bill to make paper leak punishments more stringent. This legislation aims to expedite trials and deter unfair means in public examinations.
