As Maldives president seeks SAARC summit, India says cooperation requires goodwill
Demand for MSP, reforms: Protesting farmers breach police barricades enroute to Bhopal
American gambler spent $90 million buying 54,000 acres of logged Florida land
'Clock it', 'delulu': How Gen Z lingo took over Parliament during anti-paper leak Bill debate
Indian-origin postal worker collapses during shift in Texas, probe announced to find out if it was due to heatwave
Peccaries return to Uruguay after 17-year effort, first wild births recorded
stories.summary: Collared peccaries are returning to Uruguay after a century-long absence. The species disappeared locally in the late 1800s due to hunting and habitat loss. Conservationists began a careful reintroduction program around the year 2000. Camera traps and young animals confirm the species is establishing itself again. This effort aims to restore ecological functions and biodiversity in the country.

stories.title: British swam Antarctica's freezing sea and helped protect 1.55 million square kilometres
Gandhi siblings vs Pralhad Joshi: 'Defender of rapists' charge meets 'authenticate it' challenge
stories.summary: Congress leaders Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Rahul Gandhi criticised the Prime Minister's choice for education minister. They alleged the minister expressed happiness over the release of convicted rapists. This accusation stems from remarks made regarding the Bilkis Bano case convicts. The opposition leaders demanded substantiation of these serious allegations. The Union minister denied the claims and sought an apology from the Congress MP.

stories.title: 'Here's a more natural, flowing version...': Canada politician accidentally reads AI reply in his speech, remains oblivious and continues
'Sexiest Man Alive': Five big revelations from Dr Anthony Fauci's Covid diary
stories.summary: The 1,141-page archive records Fauci’s private doubts, scientific disagreements, battles with two White Houses and fascination with his own celebrity. It also contains entries that complicate some of his later public statements.

stories.title: Boeing posts bigger-than-expected Q2 loss as Air Force One costs rise by $280 million
Boeing posts bigger-than-expected Q2 loss as Air Force One costs rise by $280 million
Once known as the 'Sea of Death', China's Taklamakan Desert is turning greener with drone technology
Evening news wrap: Govt, oppn clash as Lok Sabha discusses new anti-paper leak law; India rejects PoK legislative polls, and more
How planet's 'blue forests', mangroves, protect coastlines, support wildlife and store up to four times more carbon than tropical rainforests
'His personal thoughts': RSS distances itself from Kerala right-wing activist over Delhi student protest remarks
stories.summary: The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh has distanced itself from TG Mohandas's recent comments. Mohandas is not an official office-bearer of the organization at any level. His remarks on student protesters were described as personal thoughts and condemned. These comments had triggered widespread protests and outrage on social media platforms. A police complaint was filed alleging Mohandas called for protesters to be shot.

stories.title: 'Even her own party doesn't take her seriously, why should we?' CJP hits back at Kangana Ranaut
'Garlanded as if he won a war': Opposition attacks BJP over Dharmendra Pradhan's felicitation after resignation
Scientists capture first wild footage of rare Arctic squid with its eggs
stories.summary: Scientists documented a rare Arctic bobtail squid guarding its eggs in Northeast Greenland. This marks the first confirmed in situ record of Rossia moelleri in its natural habitat. The observation occurred in the world's largest national park, a remote Arctic fjord. This finding fills a gap in understanding Arctic cephalopods and their reproduction. It provides a baseline for tracking marine life in a rapidly warming Arctic region.

stories.title: Singapore built a floating solar farm in the sea, but thousands of barnacles turned it into an engineering challenge that could sink its 13,000 solar panels
stories.summary: Singapore uses floating solar farms to overcome land scarcity for renewable energy goals. Marine organisms like barnacles attach to pontoons, adding significant weight and reducing buoyancy. This biofouling accelerates corrosion and can damage electrical components of the solar arrays. Maintaining these offshore solar plants requires constant maintenance and inspections.

stories.title: Scientists are turning seawater into a ‘blood test’ that could reveal coral reef damage before it becomes visible
stories.summary: Researchers are using water chemistry and microbes to monitor coral reef health. Ocean currents significantly influence these chemical and microbial patterns. This approach mirrors human medicine's early disease detection methods. It allows for detecting changes before visible stress appears on corals. This interdisciplinary work aims to protect vital ocean ecosystems.

stories.title: Will Smith once used this $2.5 million, 1,200-square-foot motorhome on film sets; the two-storey vehicle is now a luxury stay near Austin: Why it remains so special
stories.summary: Will Smith's custom-built luxury motorhome, 'The Heat,' is now available for rent. This impressive 53-foot double-decker RV offers extensive living space and advanced features. It previously served Smith during major film productions like 'Ali' and 'Suicide Squad.' The motorhome now anchors a glamping resort outside Austin, Texas. Guests can experience a taste of Hollywood luxury at a significantly reduced price.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Socrates: ‘Beware the barrenness of a busy life,’ and why constant activity can leave little room for a meaningful life
stories.summary: Modern societies often equate busyness with achievement and productivity. This perspective contrasts with ancient Greek philosophy which valued leisure for thought. Constant activity can reduce concentration and hinder learning and creativity. Meaningful experiences require time for reflection and appreciation of what matters. A life rich in meaning is not necessarily the busiest one.

stories.title: ITC Hotels signs Welcomhotel by ITC Hotels, Rajgir; strengthens presence in Bihar
'Cosmetic exercise to camouflage illegal occupation': MEA rejects Pak-organised polls in PoK
17-year-old proposes hybrid nuclear system to cut Antarctic CO₂ emissions by 3,254 tons
stories.summary: A young Chilean student has proposed an innovative energy system for Antarctica. This concept combines renewable sources with a nuclear microreactor for reliable power. The system aims to significantly reduce diesel fuel dependence and carbon emissions. It offers a potential solution for powering remote research stations in extreme conditions. This student-led idea highlights future possibilities for sustainable Antarctic energy.

stories.title: 'Not an in-house probe ': AAIB explains to SC why AI171 crash report is getting delayed, to submit dossier in October
Costa Rica covered a dead pasture with 12,000 tonnes of orange peel. Sixteen years later, scientists found a thriving forest
Divers once believed the Great Blue Hole was bottomless; then explorers discovered human remains deep inside
Scientists are planting 30 million oysters in the Chesapeake Bay to restore water quality and marine life in one of America's largest restoration projects
The pig that almost started a war: How a pig shot in 1859 turned a San Juan Island farm dispute into a 12-year Britain-America standoff
'Modiji clocked it': BJP MP's Gen Z-style praise for PM during anti-paper leak Bill debate
Quote of the day by Kobe Bryant: "I don't want to be the next Michael Jordan, I only want to be…" - a timeless lesson on authenticity, self-belief and creating your own legacy
stories.summary: Kobe Bryant famously stated he only wanted to be Kobe Bryant, not the next Michael Jordan. This quote highlights the importance of self-belief and avoiding living in another's shadow. Bryant studied great players but focused on developing his unique strengths and game. Constant comparison can hinder personal growth and obscure individual talents. Authenticity and self-belief ultimately lead to lasting impact and individual success.

stories.title: 'Milestone legislation' vs 'Pradhan saved Pradhan Mantri': Centre, Oppn clash as Lok Sabha debates new anti-paper leak bill - top developments
stories.summary: The Lok Sabha is discussing a proposed amendment to the anti-paper leak law. This legislation aims to strengthen safeguards against examination fraud following the NEET exam leak. Union minister Jitendra Singh introduced the bill, reaffirming government commitment to student welfare. Congress criticized the government's response and the handling of student protests. The opposition also questioned the prioritization of social media over education reforms.

stories.title: US base in South Korea reports white phosphorus leak; residents urged to evacuate
Burkina Faso tightens gold mining control; official gold worth $6 billion recorded
stories.summary: Burkina Faso recorded more than$6 billion worth of goldthrough official channels in the first half of 2026 after producing and procuring over55 tonnes of gold. The military-led government says its mining reforms aim to bring more artisanal gold into the formal economy, reduce smuggling, improve transparency and increase state revenue. It has also expanded mining oversight, formed new cooperatives and continued investments in electricity infrastructure.

stories.title: California eradicated these 20-pound rodents decades ago; DNA suggests someone deliberately brought them back
stories.summary: California believed nutria were eradicated, but they reappeared in the Central Valley. A new genetic study indicates these rodents were reintroduced by humans. Nutria damage wetlands and weaken vital flood control structures. Their feeding and burrowing habits cause significant ecological and agricultural harm. This discovery highlights the critical need for prevention alongside removal efforts.

stories.title: After rescuing woman from shark attack, Charlie Verco sets world paddleboard record
Billionaire Steve Wynn's Beverly Hills estate sells for $47.75M after five years on the market
stories.summary: Billionaire Steve Wynn's Beverly Hills mansion has finally sold for $47.75 million. The lavish estate, known as Villa Lulu, was on the market for over five years. After extensive renovations and price adjustments, the property found a buyer. This sale highlights challenges in the ultra-luxury real estate market. The transaction concludes a significant chapter in Los Angeles' high-end property sales.

stories.title: Scientists find 30% of catfish population in Vermont lake affected by a transmissible cancer
stories.summary: A groundbreaking study has unveiled a new transmissible cancer affecting catfish populations, characterized by skin lesions that can spread from one fish to another, which is an unusual occurrence in the animal kingdom. Researchers are now delving into the mechanisms of this disease's transmission, which has already affected numerous lakes throughout New England and Canada, placing catfish among a rare group of animals susceptible to transmissible cancers.

stories.title: 'Not reasonable, issue far from settled': Govt rejects Meta's explanation on brief removal of PM Modi's Facebook video
stories.summary: The Centre finds Meta's explanation for Prime Minister Modi's post removal unsatisfactory. Government sources stated the issue requires deeper discussions with the social media company. Meta's response was deemed unreasonable by officials after the post was briefly unavailable. The ministry summoned Meta's global head of public policy regarding the incident. Discussions with Meta will continue as the matter is far from settled.

stories.title: PM Modi reviews Assam floods as over 4.45 lakh remain affected; Centre steps up relief
Mekedatu row: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay writes to PM Modi; challenges Centre’s 'no consent needed' reply
Workers building dam uncover 15th-century burials in Angola before flooding submerged them
stories.summary: Archaeologists excavating a site in central Angola before it is flooded by a hydroelectric dam have uncovered the country's oldest radiocarbon-dated burials, earliest known stone structures and only known ancient urn cremation. Dating to the early 1400s, the discoveries provide new evidence of organised communities and burial traditions before European arrival.

stories.title: 'Fictional, unfounded': BJP dismisses report of portfolio change offer to Dharmendra Pradhan
stories.summary: BJP MP Sambit Patra has denied reports concerning Dharmendra Pradhan's ministerial portfolio. He stated these claims were entirely fictional and published solely to sensationalize. Pradhan resigned as Union education minister following widespread protests over the NEET paper leak. The Cockroach Janta Party delegation called off their protest after talks. Union ministers Jagat Prakash Nadda and Jitendra Singh met with the delegation.

stories.title: Meet Baba Lena: At 83, this Siberian grandmother finally chased her lifelong dream, travelling to around 20 countries after waiting a lifetime for the right moment
German scientists discovered naturally occurring microbes that removed 95% of dissolved uranium from contaminated water
July 20 protest: RAF used tear gas, anti-riot guns and plastic pellets
Inside $85M James Bond mansion 'Villa Skyfall' in Florida
stories.summary: Villa Skyfall, a stunning estate available for $85 million in Delray Beach, Florida, epitomizes luxury living. This mansion presents an entire ecosystem tailored for its affluent owner, including equipped closets and a fully functioning kitchen. Its design channels a James Bond aesthetic, prioritizing security and privacy. Stone Creek Ranch is becoming a magnet for global elite, enhanced by the allure of Florida's lack of a state income tax.

stories.title: More than 4,000 Kenyan students came together to plant mangroves in a bid to set a Guinness World Record
After World War II, a few snakes reached Guam; they now number up to 30,000 per square mile, and scientists found 19,000 hidden genetic changes
stories.summary: Brown tree snakes invaded Guam after World War II, causing ecological damage. These snakes now exist in extremely high densities across the island. New research reveals thousands of hidden DNA changes in the snakes. This genetic flexibility helps them adapt to new environments and survive. The findings challenge previous understandings of invasive species and inbreeding.

stories.title: San Francisco tenant hears strange noises before Raccoon breaks into bedroom
stories.summary: Two San Francisco roommates spent nearly two months trying to identify strange scratching noises coming from inside their apartment walls. The mystery ended when a mother raccoon that had built a nest inside the wall gave birth to babies and later broke through into one tenant's bedroom. The roommates eventually moved out after the animals were removed and received about $4,600 in reduced rent and expenses. The incident highlights how wild animals can sometimes find shelter inside buildings without residents realising it until the problem becomes impossible to ignore.

stories.title: Two Ohio YouTubers behind Creek Kings Outdoors sentenced to jail after pleading guilty to 40 deer poaching charges, fined more than $37,000 and banned from hunting for five years
'Six major paper leaks in five years in Punjab': Swati Maliwal's 'super CM' swipe at Kejriwal
A 400-year-old Native American pot lay buried beneath a Spanish mission in Florida
July 20 NEET protest: SC asks states to release student protesters under 18 with no criminal records
stories.summary: The Supreme Court said a prima facie case had been made out for a transparent inquiry by a commission and added that the exercise should help frame a protocol for handling such situations in the future. The hearing also brought before the court allegations of police excesses from several states, including claims that a police officer in Bihar used an AK-47 against peaceful protesters.

stories.title: Knepp Estate Rewilding Project: Failing farm lets nature take over; wildlife numbers soar
'Ankit Sharma died with 51 injuries': Death penalty sought for Tahir Hussain in 2020 Delhi riots case
stories.summary: Special public prosecutor Madhukar Pandey told the court that Sharma was subjected to a planned and relentless assault before his body was dumped in a drain instead of being taken for medical treatment. Speaking to reporters after the hearing, Pandey said the prosecution's demand for capital punishment was based on the nature of the crime and the manner in which it was carried out.

stories.title: New York spent 8 years planting one million trees. Now the city is aiming for 30% tree cover by 2040 to transform its fight against rising heat
'Removed in error': Meta responds after PM Modi's video was blocked on Facebook; govt summons company official
stories.summary: Meta admitted to mistakenly deleting Prime Minister Narendra Modi's video. The content was removed in error and has since been restored by the company. This video assured stricter government actions against paper leaks across the nation. The Union Cabinet will discuss these stringent measures in Parliament soon. The government aims to get the Bill passed to address the issue.

stories.title: 'Don't mess with students': Kejriwal takes 'emperor Modi' jibe at PM over reported AK-47 use during Bihar protest
Czech Republic President Petr Pavel spotted at Hungarian GP as a professional photographer
stories.summary: Czech President Petr Pavel nurtures a deep passion for sports photography, recently capturing the thrilling moments at the Hungarian Grand Prix with his official photographer's badge. His lens has also chronicled prestigious events such as the Le Mans 24 Hours and Dakar Rally. Pavel's captivating photography not only tells a story but also contributes to charitable causes, beautifully complementing his esteemed career in politics and the military.

stories.title: Kerala Right-wing activist faces police complaint over 'shoot protesters' remark
stories.summary: In its complaint, the AISF argued that TG Mohandas' statements went far beyond political criticism and instead encouraged the use of violence against peaceful protesters. The organisation said publicly advocating that state forces open fire on students could lead to deaths, grievous injuries and widespread fear, while undermining constitutional values and the democratic right to protest.

stories.title: 'Generation gutter': Kangana on 'young Hindu women' who took part in CJP protest
stories.summary: Kangana Ranaut dubbed Gen Z women as "so-called westernised Indian women", who are "not good at studies, but they are so ugly and corrupt that they cannot be homemakers either", yet they "proudly flaunt their freedom to use drugs, consume alcohol, or have endless body counts". Lashing out at the "behaviour of young Hindu women", the actress-turned-politician said those female protesters wanted to "imitate the lives of independent career women without earning that freedom".

stories.title: 39 pilgrims injured as Amarnath Yatra bus skids off road in J&K's Ganderbal
'No protester will be left alone': CJP claims Centre promised no FIRs in NDA states after midnight talks
stories.summary: Government representatives met with CJP and shared draft notifications. Bihar and Assam governments will withdraw FIRs and release arrested protesters. Future legal action against demonstrators will also be prevented. Union government and other BJP/NDA states will release similar notifications soon. Protesters will not be left alone as all are in this together.

stories.title: MBBS admissions: NMC puts focus on ability, not disability
NMC asks medical colleges to set up support units for students with disabilities
'Can't bribe them': Trump's 'will beat them' warning to Iran despite talks
stories.summary: Despite Trump's remarks, tensions remained high across the region. Saudi Arabia, Jordan and Iraq reported drone attacks on Monday, suggesting that hostilities had not completely subsided despite the pause in the US bombing campaign. Washington halted its two-week air campaign against Iran on Saturday in a surprise policy shift by Trump after nearly five months of conflict. Iran said it had not abandoned diplomacy but denied reports that it had sought talks with Washington.

stories.title: 'Could result in injuries': FAA flags incorrectly installed seats on several Boeing 737 Max jets
stories.summary: The FAA has proposed mandatory inspections for 453 Boeing 737 MAX aircraft seats. Improperly installed seat assemblies could disengage during turbulence or emergency landings. This condition might injure passengers and crew or block the evacuation aisle. Boeing supports the FAA's decision to make these recommendations mandatory. The directive applies to US-registered aircraft, with no deadline specified yet.

stories.title: French wildfire created a monster cloud, unleashing lightning that ignited more fires
stories.summary: A powerful wildfire in France generated its own thunderstorm, creating new fires. This rare pyrocumulonimbus phenomenon produced violent winds that drove the flames unpredictably. The blaze near Saumos burned over 420 square kilometers and forced many evacuations. This event marks the first recorded instance of such a storm in France. Scientists are studying these extreme fire events and their connection to climate change.

stories.title: Keigo Higashino, author of 'The Devotion of Suspect X', dies at 68
stories.summary: Japanese mystery author Keigo Higashino has died at age sixty-eight. His publisher announced his passing on Monday, which caused widespread grief. Higashino wrote over one hundred books, translated into many languages worldwide. His works were adapted for film and television, gaining him a large following. He was known for merging science and detective fiction with human observations.

stories.title: Study shows world spoke tens of thousands more languages in antiquity than today
CJP accuses government of breaching promises, warns of protests
Kasol raves: Supreme Court orders transfer of Kullu DC, SP
stories.summary: The Supreme Court upheld the Himachal High Court's order for transfers. Kullu Deputy Commissioner Anurag C Sharma and SP Madan Lal must be transferred. This action follows their alleged failure to prevent rave parties in Kasol. The court stayed further action on FIRs and the SIT probe. However, impartial departmental inquiries necessitate their relocation from Kullu.

stories.title: Delay in paying land compensation proves costly for Tamil Nadu
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ordered Tamil Nadu to pay market rate compensation for acquired land. Alternatively, the state must return 970 acres of land to landowners within six weeks. This decision impacts Tamil Nadu's already strained fiscal situation significantly. The court emphasized landowners should not suffer due to government inaction. The state faces a substantial financial burden from this directive.

stories.title: Need out-of-box thinking to plug paper leaks, says Supreme Court
stories.summary: A high-powered committee for education reform has been formed. The Supreme Court seeks "out-of-box thinking" to address sector problems. The court will hear the NEET paper leak petition on August 3. Government needs to examine additional safeguards for online exams. The system's ad hocism is troubling and requires institutionalization.

stories.title: INS Sudarshini departs Boston for Portugal after participating in US's 250th Independence Day anniversary celebrations
stories.summary: Indian Naval Ship Sudarshini concluded its US visit and sailed for Portugal. The vessel participated in America's 250th independence anniversary celebrations in Boston. Representing India, the ship showcased its rich maritime heritage and strengthened partnerships. Sudarshini joined an international fleet of tall ships as a goodwill ambassador. This voyage continues India's maritime strength and professionalism on the global stage.

stories.title: Anti-defection law: Supreme Court ready to hear plea for its interpretation
stories.summary: The Supreme Court will examine the anti-defection law's interpretation concerning political party mergers. Kapil Sibal argued that electoral verdicts can be altered through such merger provisions. The court acknowledged significant issues with the Tenth Schedule's current working. It issued notice to the Centre seeking its response on the matter. This legal challenge could have major repercussions for the country's political landscape.

stories.title: Supreme Court: Insolvency shield is for firm, not promoters
What is Tana Mongeau and Clavicular’s feud? Podcast remarks explained
stories.summary: Tana Mongeau criticised Kick streamer Braden “Clavicular” on her Brand Safe podcast after his livestreamed breakup with Lily Snyder. She questioned why anyone would accept being “immoral and cruel” for views and revenue while stressing that she wanted to understand the psychology behind such behaviour rather than simply judge him.

stories.title: Ex-top Chhattisgarh official behind paper leaks, appointed kin as deputy collector, DSP: ED
stories.summary: Taman Singh Sonwani, a retired IAS officer, faces custodial remand for alleged CGPSC paper leak. He allegedly amended recruitment rules in 2021 to benefit his family members. Sonwani appointed relatives as deputy collector and DSP after rule changes. The Enforcement Directorate arrested the former CGPSC chairperson on July 25. A special court granted seven days of ED custody for further investigation.

stories.title: 'I am a street fighter': Combative Dharmendra Pradhan arrives in Parliament to a rousing welcome
stories.summary: Former minister Dharmendra Pradhan asserted his street fighter identity after resigning from his post. He arrived in Parliament as a Member of Parliament, receiving strong support from fellow MPs. Colleagues raised slogans and offered traditional honours, showcasing solidarity with the ex-minister. This public display aimed to convey that his resignation was not a reflection of his work. Pradhan's response indicated readiness to address discussions on the paper leak issue.

stories.title: India summons Ukraine envoy for ship attack, Kyiv seeks talks
PM Modi, Amit Shah laud CRPF for wiping out Naxalism
End to Parliament impasse in sight, Lok Sabha may take up bill on exam reforms today
stories.summary: Parliamentary proceedings may resume Tuesday after Lok Sabha Speaker's outreach to break impasse. The government's bill on paper leaks is likely to be discussed in the lower House. A discussion on the Vande Mataram bill may begin in the Rajya Sabha. Opposition members have moved many amendment notices to the public exams bill. Both sides continued to trade charges while inching towards a resolution.

stories.title: Ayodhya Ram mandir donation row: On Supreme Court suggestion, temple SIT to include a forensic auditor
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the UP government to add a forensic audit expert to the SIT. This special investigation team will probe alleged embezzlement of Ayodhya Ram Mandir donations. The court wants an expeditious, fair, and transparent investigation into all aspects. The SIT has been asked to submit its probe status report within two weeks. The court will monitor the investigation directly without retired judge supervision.

stories.title: Supreme Court: No bail in digital arrest cases barring exceptional grounds
Quote of the day by Marco Rubio: 'American Dream is a term that is often used but also often misunderstood' and the story of An American Son
Quote by Bob Ross: 'The very fact that you're aware of suffering is enough reason to...'
stories.summary: Bob Ross expressed a powerful notion regarding suffering as a testament to being alive. He suggested that without the dark shades in our lives, the brighter colors wouldn’t shine as vividly. This thought resonates with both ancient Stoic philosophers and contemporary thinkers, reinforcing that embracing pain can lead to deeper understanding and purpose amidst life's trials. Ross's insightful philosophy serves as a beacon for those facing their own challenges.

stories.title: Who is HMBLZAYY? The Twitch streamer who walked 3,000 miles across America and raised nearly $200K for charity
stories.summary: Twitch streamer HMBLZAYY finished a 3,000-mile walk across America in 124 days. He raised nearly $200,000 to build a trade school for teenagers. HMBLZAYY survived being hit by two cars during his challenging journey. His perseverance inspired thousands of viewers who followed his progress online. The streamer's mission successfully supported underserved youth and their futures.

stories.title: Coast Guard airlifts ailing seafarer from ship off Gujarat coast despite rough seas, adverse weather
Can ICE or CBP read your deleted messages? Attorney says the answer is 'yes'
TMC’s Abhishek Banerjee meets Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, seeks early decision on disqualification of 20 rebel MPs
stories.summary: TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee met Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla regarding pending disqualification petitions. He urged the speaker to expedite decisions on twenty rebel Members of Parliament. Banerjee also requested a review of seating arrangements for his party's elected members. The speaker reportedly offered no clear response to the concerns raised. This meeting occurred after the TMC delegation submitted disqualification petitions.

stories.title: Quote by Andrei Tarkovsky: 'A book read by a thousand different people is a thousand different books'
stories.summary: Artistic interpretation is a reflection of the diverse experiences and perspectives of each reader. When a book is read by numerous individuals, it morphs into countless versions, each colored by personal insights. Reader-response theory emphasizes how our backgrounds inform our comprehension of texts, offering a valuable lens to tackle the complexities of modern communication and the challenges posed by digital divides.

stories.title: D4vd murder case: Court reveals Celeste Rivas allegedly threatened to kill singer before her death
stories.summary: Court testimony revealed text messages between D4vd and Celeste Rivas before her death. Celeste allegedly threatened D4vd one day prior to their meeting at his home. Prosecutors claim D4vd fatally stabbed and dismembered the 14-year-old. D4vd has pleaded not guilty to all charges against him. The preliminary hearing is ongoing as both sides present evidence.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Mehbooba faces heat over Jantar Mantar comment, opposition accuses her justifying use of force in UT
stories.summary: Mehbooba Mufti's statement on force in Kashmir has drawn criticism. She appeared to justify actions by citing militancy in the region. Chief Minister Omar Abdullah demanded an apology for her controversial remarks. The PDP defended her statement, claiming it was misrepresented by media. Other parties also condemned her comments, highlighting past suffering in Kashmir.

stories.title: Female African treefrogs mate with several males simultaneously; together they whip up...
stories.summary: Female African treefrogs engage in a fascinating mating ritual where multiple males collaborate to create larger foam nests. This teamwork is vital, as it shields hundreds of eggs from potential desiccation, ultimately boosting tadpole survival rates. The nesting-assistance hypothesis presents a fresh perspective on this widespread reproductive strategy, as males actively participate in nest construction and fertilization, solidifying their role in the survival of future generations.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Sun Tzu: 'If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear...' and an evergreen battle strategy
Quote of the day by Taylor Swift's husband Travis Kelce: "If you don't care about the guy next to you, one, you're a terrible…"
stories.summary: Travis Kelce emphasizes that caring for teammates is crucial for team success. He believes a lack of concern for others makes one a terrible teammate. This attitude directly hinders a group's ability to achieve meaningful collective victories. Genuine trust and responsibility build stronger teams and improve overall performance. Shared goals unite individuals, leading to healthier competition and collective achievement.

stories.title: Seth Rogen’s blunt response to YouTuber Yung Mooch sparks debate as Jonah Hill shares heartfelt career advice
stories.summary: A video filmed by YouTuber Yung Mooch captured an unexpected meeting with Seth Rogen and Jonah Hill on a Los Angeles production set. Rogen told Mooch not to interrupt people while they are working, while Hill offered kinder advice, telling him to enjoy life, be a kind person, and always be himself. The video was first highlighted by Dexerto.

stories.title: Iran's shadow oil billions vanish as trusties flee, Interpol red notices issued
Hummingbird hawkmoths may have their own version of being left-handed or right-handed
stories.summary: Hummingbird hawkmoths exhibit a distinct preference for one eye and feeding tube side when accessing nectar. This lateralization enhances efficiency by conserving cognitive resources during intricate maneuvers. Researchers found that this trait is instinctive, evident even in their initial flower interactions. By aligning a dominant eye with a favored proboscis side, these insects streamline complex feeding tasks, showcasing a remarkable adaptation that enables problem-solving with a small brain.

stories.title: Netflix executive reveals at company's trust-building retreat he once used ketamine, got fired from his $1.1 million job after return
In 1802, an explorer released pigs on Kangaroo Island; 224 years later, Australia has removed them
stories.summary: Australia celebrates a significant conservation victory with the successful removal of all feral pigs from Kangaroo Island. This initiative stands as the largest project worldwide to eradicate a persistent pest population. Launched post the devastating 2019/20 bushfires, it employed a blend of innovative technology and traditional hunting techniques to safeguard native wildlife and farming interests from potential harm.

stories.title: Paramount-WB merger: Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming and Benedict Wong urge UK to block deal
stories.summary: Actors Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming and Benedict Wong have called on the UK government to block the proposed $111 billion Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger, warning that the deal could cause "immense harm on the British public" by threatening jobs, independent filmmaking and media diversity. Their comments come as Paramount agreed to delay completing the takeover until a U.S. court rules on whether the transaction violates antitrust laws.

stories.title: A diamond mining operation uncovered a 500-year-old Portuguese shipwreck filled with gold and ancient secrets
This 71-year-old US mayor goes to a homeless shelter every Friday night, sleeps, serves breakfast Saturday morning. In 2021, he called 'homelessness' a choice
California’s ocean is up to 4°C hotter; whales are disappearing, pelicans are starving and sharks...
stories.summary: The rising ocean temperatures off California's coast are creating serious repercussions for marine life. Whales are being pushed away from their traditional feeding zones, while seabird populations face starvation. Additionally, great white sharks are venturing closer to shore, posing risks to beachgoers. The rise in toxic algae blooms is further contaminating the ecosystem and impacting local fisheries, with these shifts connected to climate change and El Niño phenomena.

stories.title: 'No legal action, FIRs being withdrawn': Bihar govt assures protesters in big win for students, CJP
47 GW battery storage, 23 GW pumped storage projects in pipeline
YouTuber Tana Mongeau shares blunt reaction after Clavicular’s livestream breakup with Lily Snyder raises tough questions
stories.summary: Tana Mongeau criticized Clavicular after his livestream breakup with Lily Snyder, calling his behavior “immoral and cruel” if it was done for views and revenue. Her comments followed the emotional stream in which Lily pleaded for the relationship to continue while Clavicular said his career came first. The incident has since divided opinion across social media.

stories.title: Indian-origin Uber driver charged with two counts of sexual assault in Canada
In 2005, scientists began reshaping an Inner Mongolia grassland; years later, plant-eating insects...
stories.summary: Research conducted over several years in Inner Mongolia has identified herbivorous insects as vital players in ecosystem stability. These plant-eaters manage the food web by producing varied population levels, which mitigate the risk of sudden food shortages for predators and safeguard plant diversity. This study challenges prior assumptions, underscoring the crucial function of herbivores in maintaining ecological balance and biodiversity.

stories.title: NHAI wins major arbitration, Rs 3,177-cr claim cut to Rs 46 cr
'Will support any decision taken in discharge of duty': CRPF leadership assures personnel
stories.summary: The CRPF headquarters has assured its personnel of full backing for decisions made in good faith. This assurance comes as the force investigates recent allegations of pellet gun usage. The probe will examine around nine to ten specific allegations based on available evidence. Any reckless or unjustified action by personnel will invite disciplinary measures. The force emphasizes that weapon choices must be justified and based on valid reasoning.

stories.title: Built in 1948, Mud Mountain Dam gets a $112 million fish passage project to help salmon migrate
Jeff Bezos, Eduardo Saverin to invest in Liverpool? Amazon, Facebook co-founders approached
stories.summary: Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) are in preliminary talks with a consortium led by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia over the sale of a minority stake in the Premier League club. Eduardo Saverin, the Singapore-based billionaire who co-founded Facebook alongside Mark Zuckerberg, has been approached to join the investment group. One of the biggest names linked to the proposed investment is Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.

stories.title: Europe is becoming too hot for some cold-blooded snakes, but one region could become their last major refuge
stories.summary: Climate change may significantly alter European snake habitats, impacting cold-adapted species. Western Europe faces declining suitability due to rising temperatures and drought conditions. The Balkan Peninsula is projected to become a crucial refuge for snake diversity. This region's varied microclimates offer protection against increasing heat stress. Conservation efforts should prioritize these complex landscapes for reptile survival.

stories.title: 'Different flags, same playbook': Sonam Wangchuk's wife slams BJP, Congress
Rs 1 crore in aid, website linking lawyers to protesters: How CJP plans to fight cases across India
For nearly 250 years, a notebook lay unnoticed until it revealed lost Mozart music
New rule for asylum seekers in the US: 'No interview, straight deportation', DHS calls it 'second chance'
Bihar's dairy push: New plant in Nalanda to boost farmer incomes, create jobs
'Modi govt fears truth and non-violence': Rahul Gandhi on Ken-Betwa protest crackdown
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi criticized the Modi government for fearing truth and non-violent resistance. Tribal communities protested the Ken-Betwa river project in Madhya Pradesh. They sought fair compensation and dignified rehabilitation for their land. Police dispersed the peaceful tribal satyagraha after fifteen days of protest. The Congress party pledged to ensure justice for the affected tribal people.

stories.title: Second man arrested in 2023 murder of Indian-origin food delivery driver in Canada
King Ratsnake eats deadly cobras and vipers; genome mapping reveals how it survives venom
stories.summary: Scientists have mapped the genome of the nonvenomous king ratsnake, a species known for hunting and eating deadly venomous snakes such as cobras and vipers. The new chromosome-level genome will help researchers investigate how the snake naturally resists venom. They say the findings could improve understanding of snake evolution, venom resistance and support future research into better antivenom therapies.

stories.title: NEET fast-track court's first hearing stalls as CBI skips proceedings
Most scuba divers believed they rarely touched reefs; underwater observers found more...
Parliament showdown: Debate on anti-paper leak Bill delayed amid oppn uproar; CJP gives ultimatum to Centre, says may restart protest - top developments
Mizoram minister Lalnilawma meets NDMA leadership; seeks 'disaster' status for African swine fever
stories.summary: The meeting focused on enhancing disaster preparedness in Mizoram, particularly given the state's vulnerability to earthquakes, landslides, forest fires, and other natural hazards.

stories.title: PoK protests: Thousands march to Muzaffarabad after failed talks; polls delayed in 2 districts
31 killed in first terror attack in Nigerian village, residents say army refused to respond
What is happening in Seattle now? Police searching for 2nd shooter; no details about arrested suspect revealed
stories.summary: A mass shooting occurred at Seattle Center's Bite of Seattle food festival. Three people died and four others sustained injuries in the chaotic incident. Police are actively searching for a second shooter involved in the event. The festival grounds were closed as vendors packed up their stands. Authorities are seeking information to identify and arrest any outstanding suspects.

stories.title: KFC's Colonel Sanders’ home, restaurant and engraved pressure cooker are going to auction
stories.summary: A unique collection of items linked to KFC founder Colonel Harland Sanders will be auctioned in Kentucky on July 28. The sale includes his former home, the Claudia Sanders Dinner House, personal belongings, business records, photographs and historic memorabilia that have been preserved by the Settle family for more than 50 years. Organisers say the collection is being offered to the public for the first time.

stories.title: 'Police showed respect for accused Sena corporator': Bombay HC on probe into doctors' assault case
stories.summary: The Bombay high court criticised police for showing favorable treatment to a Shiv Sena corporator. The court directed the Deputy Commissioner of Police to investigate the matter thoroughly. The accused corporator allegedly assaulted doctors and medical staff at a civic hospital. He was later granted bail, which the High Court had termed perverse. The court expressed surprise at his behavior towards the public he serves.

stories.title: Six orphaned rhinos give birth after mothers were killed by poachers
stories.summary: In a heartwarming turnaround, six orphaned rhinos from South Africa have welcomed new calves after years of rehabilitation. Their successful births signify a remarkable milestone in conservation efforts, providing renewed hope for endangered rhino populations. Wildlife officials emphasized that these births not only enrich the local ecosystem but also bolster South Africa's commitment to preserving this majestic species.

stories.title: Around 1200 BCE, major Mediterranean civilisations began collapsing; scientists have now reconstructed the climate conditions surrounding the crisis
stories.summary: A new study suggests prolonged drought pressured eastern Mediterranean societies. This drying significantly affected agriculture and food security across the region. Drought acted as a threat multiplier, worsening existing societal challenges. Warfare and invasions interacted with environmental stress during this period. Understanding past climate pressures informs our view of societal vulnerability.

stories.title: 200 years after the first dinosaur, scientists use brain scans on a 100-million-year-old snake fossil from Brazil
stories.summary: Palaeontology has transformed from examining fossil fragments to digitally reconstructing ancient creatures. A new Cretaceous snake fossil from Brazil showcases this remarkable scientific advancement. High-resolution micro-CT scanning revealed the snake's brain anatomy and lifestyle. This technology allows detailed comparisons across millions of years of evolution. Modern methods are reshaping our understanding of prehistoric life's diversity.

stories.title: UK's largest girls' organisation Girlguiding unveils first uniform redesign since 1990 — focused on ‘self-expression and confidence’
'No other...': Parents of Indian medical student Vaibhav Duggal who died by suicide seek $30 million from Texas Tech University
Evening news wrap: CJP warns of another protest; SC slams police action against students during NEET protest
Lonely whooping crane that refused to mate helped save one of the world’s rarest birds
518 million years ago, one tiny sea creature may have started the evolution of the fangs
The Great Pyramid was not built by slaves, but by paid workers who drank beer and ate meat.
stories.summary: Modern archaeology says that pyramid builders were not slaves but a respected workforce. These workers lived in a dedicated town and received good food and medical care. Their diet included meat, bread, and beer, ensuring strength for their labor. Burial in tombs near the pyramids honoured their significant contribution to ancient Egypt.

stories.title: In 1992, Hurricane Andrew may have helped giant Burmese pythons spread across Florida's Everglades, creating one of America's worst invasive species crises
Dutch scientist created bacteria that repair cracked buildings by turning cracks into stone, making concrete heal itself and saving billions in repair costs
Before ants began caring for their young, the brain circuits were helping them find food
'MPs sleeping, need wake-up call': Delhi transport bodies plan Parliament march on August 4 against E20 fuel
stories.summary: Delhi transport groups will march to Parliament on August 4. They demand the withdrawal of ethanol-blended petrol from the market. Concerns about vehicle problems and mileage reduction are being raised. The government defends the E20 fuel program as safe and beneficial. This protest aims to highlight issues with the mandated fuel blend.

stories.title: One of the world's largest rodents was imported for fur farming in North America; today it's devastating wetlands and riverbanks across US
stories.summary: Nutria, large rodents introduced for fur farming, now infest forty US states and Canada. These prolific breeders destroy vital wetland vegetation and agricultural crops like rice. Their burrowing weakens levees and dams, posing risks to infrastructure and public safety. Eradication efforts involve trapping, detection dogs, and bounty programs to control populations. These invasive creatures have caused millions of dollars in damage across affected regions.

stories.title: Researchers made flying harder for Alaskan Seabirds; only 67% returned, survivors bred better
stories.summary: Researchers clipped a few wing and tail feathers of wild black-legged kittiwakes in Alaska to make flying more energy-intensive and tracked them for several years. The birds struggled to raise chicks during that breeding season, and fewer survived to return the next year. However, those that did return migrated farther and were more likely to breed successfully, showing how energy spent in one season can affect the next.

stories.title: Joni Mitchell’s former Malibu home is listed for $27 million; its beachfront pool may be impossible to recreate today
stories.summary: Joni Mitchell's former Malibu Colony home is listed for twenty-seven million dollars. This oceanfront property features a rare beachfront swimming pool and spa. The residence offers five bedrooms and five bathrooms with direct beach access. Its Cape Cod-inspired architecture maximizes natural light and ocean views. The home highlights Malibu's evolving luxury housing market and coastal regulations.

stories.title: Rock shelter in Spain preserves the stories from hunting to farming around 8,000 years ago
'Govt breaching deal ... will protest again': CJP gives Centre ultimatum amid ongoing police action
Paris knife attack: Man arrested after three women stabbed near Porte de Clichy
stories.summary: A man was arrested after stabbing three women near Paris's Porte de Clichy on Monday. One victim, believed to be pregnant, is in critical condition after the attack. The 31-year-old suspect, who reportedly has mental health issues, was apprehended at the scene. Police found two knives in the possession of the arrested individual. An investigation into the incident has been officially opened by authorities.

stories.title: Why US strikes on Hormuz suddenly stopped despite Trump's bluster
Elon Musk says a future on Mars could help humanity survive pandemics, AI and global disasters
stories.summary: Elon Musk believes a Mars colony can protect humanity from global disasters. He argues the vast distance offers a crucial buffer against pandemics and cyber threats. A six-month journey to Mars acts as an automatic quarantine period for diseases. Digital attacks also face significant delays, providing time for mitigation efforts. This expansion ensures human civilization is not solely confined to one planet.

stories.title: Canadian TikToker with early-onset Alzheimer's ends her life through assisted dying
Ram Temple donation 'theft' case: SC tells SIT to submit status report within 2 weeks
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the Special Investigation Team to submit a status report. This report concerns the alleged theft of offerings at the Ayodhya Ram Temple. The court issued this direction while hearing petitions seeking a court-monitored investigation. The Uttar Pradesh government will add a forensic auditor to the SIT. This SIT currently comprises three IPS officers.

stories.title: 'It does not end in darkness': Sonam Wangchuk visits Rajghat, congratulates youth on protest
This California river once carried thousands of salmon every year. A 1942 dam changed it forever, and scientists are still trying to bring them back
stories.summary: Friant Dam construction in 1942 altered the San Joaquin River, impacting salmon populations. A 2006 settlement agreement initiated restoration efforts for the river and its fish. The program aims to reestablish spring-run Chinook salmon while managing water for agriculture. Multiple agencies collaborate on scientific research and habitat improvements for the river. Monitoring tracks progress and guides adjustments for long-term ecological recovery.

stories.title: They bought this Laguna Beach home for $16 million and spent $20 million rebuilding it. It is now listed for $112 million
stories.summary: A Laguna Beach oceanfront estate is now on the market for $112 million. The owners invested $20 million to extensively renovate the property over two years. This remarkable residence spans 14,400 square feet and includes six bedrooms. The owners are selling as they have relocated and no longer need the large home. This listing aims to set a new residential sales record for Orange County.

stories.title: Syngenta will stop selling paraquat in Australia after strict new safety rules, but generic versions of the controversial herbicide will remain available
stories.summary: Syngenta is ceasing paraquat sales in Australia after new safety regulations were introduced. This decision impacts product choice and market stability for Australian farmers. Generic paraquat will remain available, but Syngenta's exit raises supply concerns. New rules aim to reduce exposure risks for workers and the environment. Growers must now adapt to stricter conditions and potential market shifts.

stories.title: Pangolin collected in 1836 sat unnoticed in a museum until its DNA revealed a new species
Govt mulls PM Surya Ghar 2.0 with battery storage, shared rooftop solar
Logan Paul releases new limited-edition PRIME bottle honoring Oliver Tree's legacy
stories.summary: Logan Paul has launched a limited-edition version of PRIME inspired by Oliver Tree, with every dollar earned going to the late musician's foundation. The initiative honors the late singer and supports grants for young artists. It also carries forward Tree's vision of helping creators bring their ideas to life through hands-on artistic projects.

stories.title: MEA summons Ukraine ambassador after attack on ship with 4 Indians on board
'No one can change his decision': Karnataka minister Yathindra says father Siddaramaiah 'firm' on skipping 2028 polls
stories.summary: Yathindra Siddaramaiah confirmed his father's decision to retire from electoral politics. He stated that once his father makes a firm decision, no one can change it. The senior leader is prioritizing his health as he approaches eighty years old. He will remain actively involved in politics and champion vulnerable sections. Siddaramaiah previously announced the 2023 elections would be his last contest.

stories.title: Meet Nehemiah Turner: The 11-year-old Florida boy who spent more than 100 hours reading to shelter animals and changed countless lives by helping anxious pets find forever homes
Kapil Sibal challenges anti-defection law: SC to examine tenth schedule merger rule
Hamptons Mansion Auction Set: Libbie Mugrabi estate faces $11m court sale; experts warn on equity hit
stories.summary: Socialite Libbie Mugrabi's luxury Bridgehampton mansion is set to be sold in a rare court-ordered public auction after repeated attempts to sell the property privately failed. The auction follows a legal dispute over an unpaid $3.5 million loan secured against the estate. The property, originally listed for $25 million and later reduced to $19 million, will open for bidding at $11 million on August 28.

stories.title: As Lake Mead's water vanished after years of drought, human bodies, abandoned boats and decades-old mysteries began emerging from the lakebed
'Dharmendra Pradhan Zindabad': Ex-education minister gets rousing welcome in Parliament; oppn fumes
Saudi Land Restoration: 159m trees planted and restored 1 million hectares of land
E20 petrol row: Nitin Gadkari moves Bombay HC over 'defamatory' posts, deepfake videos targeting him
Nawapa Water Diversion Plan: 1960s scheme sought to reroute northern rivers
World's narrowest island capital just 150 metres wide could disappear beneath rising seas, World Bank warns
stories.summary: Majuro, capital of the Republic of Marshall Islands, confronts severe threats from rising sea levels. Coastal erosion accelerates due to increased wind speeds and human interference. Adaptation measures like sea walls and land raising are being considered by policymakers. However, migration may become a last resort for the Marshallese people.

stories.title: CRPF to conduct 'professional post-event assessment' of RAF action at student protests
stories.summary: The CRPF will conduct a professional post-event assessment of RAF actions. This review follows the conclusion of student protests and dispersal of demonstrators. Opposition MPs have raised concerns over alleged police brutality against students. Reports suggest AK-47 rifles were used against protesters in Bihar. The Union Education Minister has resigned amid sustained student demonstrations.

stories.title: 'Rajghat, then back to the mountains': Sonam Wangchuk discharged from Medanta Hospital
stories.summary: Sonam Wangchuk has been discharged from Medanta Hospital after his hunger strike. He will now visit Rajghat to honour Mahatma Gandhi before returning home. Wangchuk led a 26-day hunger strike demanding the education minister's resignation. The protest concluded after successful talks between the CJP and the Centre. Dharmendra Pradhan later resigned, and Pralhad Joshi was appointed as the new minister.

stories.title: A 95-year-old CEO bought a bankrupt furniture store for $80,000 in 1975, then quietly built an $858 million business and gave millions away
'All are invited': Kejriwal announces 'National Town Hall against E20' on August 1
NASA astronaut Chris Williams spent 241 days circling Earth before finally returning home
1993 Mumbai blasts case: SC reserves order on convict Abu Salem's plea for premature release
2,000-year-old Egyptian hat stayed hidden inside a museum for more than 100 years until experts finally restored it
NEET UG leak case: Delhi court asks CBI to appoint public prosecutor
CPWD deploys 3D printing to fast-track defence construction in border areas
A church, a Jesus statue and a border wall: Inside Trump's latest land acquisition battle
stories.summary: The US government seeks land for a border wall near Mount Cristo Rey. This sacred site is a pilgrimage destination for thousands of faithful people. The Roman Catholic Diocese of Las Cruces opposes the land acquisition and wall construction. Church officials argue the wall infringes upon religious freedom and desecrates the holy place. A legal battle is underway as the government pursues eminent domain for the project.

stories.title: Baby goat falls after suddenly freezing mid-jump; an inherited muscle condition explains why
stories.summary: Fainting goats do not actually faint. Also known as myotonic goats, they have a rare inherited muscle condition called myotonia congenita that causes their muscles to become temporarily stiff when they are startled. The breed is valued for its heavy muscling, meat production, strong maternal instincts and ability to thrive on forage-based farming, making it much more than its unusual behaviour.

stories.title: First puffin chick in 30 years just emerged from England's south coast after 15 weeks of careful monitoring, giving new hope to the country's last mainland colony

Quote of the day by Dave Bautista: "I'm a poor kid from the streets. What I've been able to achieve has really just been through hard work and…" - an inspiring lesson on resilience, self-belief and turning adversity into achievement
stories.summary: Dave Bautista highlights his humble beginnings and the hard work behind his success. He stresses that personal circumstances do not dictate future achievements. Bautista faced significant rejection before finding acting roles in Hollywood. His career shift from wrestling to acting took considerable time and effort. The actor encourages pursuing dreams despite obstacles and doubts.

stories.title: 'Amit Shah responsible': Kharge accuses home minister over police action on NEET protesters in Parliament
In 1996, Indonesia's 'crazy' tree planter who was mocked for his mission planted 11,000 trees and turned barren hills into a green paradise
‘Build new NTA’: Exam body begins major revamp, seeks experts for four senior roles
'Agitation does not mean lathicharge': SC on police action against students protesting paper leak
'Pellet guns in Delhi, AK-47s in Bihar': Rahul Gandhi attacks Modi govt over 'jaanleva' system against students
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi alleged the entire system is deadly against students. He cited reports of AK-47 bullets fired at students in Bihar. Gandhi questioned Prime Minister Modi's promises regarding student FIRs. He stated that pellet guns were fired at students in Delhi. The Congress leader demanded an apology and action against attackers.

stories.title: Kai Cenat announces first livestream with Tyla since she friend-zoned him on stream
stories.summary: Popular streamer Kai Cenat will livestream with South African singer Tyla again soon. This marks their first stream together since a viral 2024 moment. Tyla politely declined Kai's date request, becoming a popular internet meme. Fans anticipate their reunion, wondering if they will reference the past event. Both artists have achieved significant success in their respective careers.

stories.title: 'Former minister will be exposed': Vijay-led Tamil Nadu govt on DMK 'corruption' audit report
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu's finance minister will present an audit report on corruption during the previous DMK regime. This report will expose alleged irregularities in the collection of party funds. The minister also reiterated the government's commitment to abolishing the NEET exam. He stated that a permanent solution for the exam is being actively planned. The first budget of the new government will be presented on August 5.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Queen Elizabeth: "When life seems hard, the courageous do not lie down and accept defeat; instead, they…" - a timeless lesson on courage, perseverance and hope in difficult times
stories.summary: Queen Elizabeth II's 2008 Christmas broadcast offered wisdom on facing life's difficulties. She stated that courageous individuals struggle for a better future instead of accepting defeat. This perspective highlights that courage involves refusing to let fear or pain dictate actions. Staying determined after setbacks keeps future possibilities open, which is more important than immediate wins. Hope is an active pursuit, requiring effort to achieve improvements rather than passive wishing.

stories.title: 'Indian students made us all proud': Greta Thunberg joins London protest in solidarity
DMK demands immediate NEET ban, seeks probe into Jantar Mantar violence
stories.summary: The DMK party is demanding an immediate nationwide ban on the NEET medical entrance examination. MP TR Baalu submitted an adjournment motion notice in the Lok Sabha seeking this ban. This demand follows a NEET UG paper leak and student protests across the nation. The DMK also called for an inquiry into the alleged use of weapons against students.

stories.title: Unesco adds Mount Olympus, France's D-Day landing beaches to World Heritage List
'Crimes against humanity' complaints filed against Bangladesh ex-president
stories.summary: Complaints were filed against former Bangladesh President Mohammed Shahabuddin on Sunday. These allegations concern crimes against humanity during the 2024 uprising against the government. Shahabuddin resigned from his presidential post on Friday citing health complications. The home minister stated the allegations do not warrant consideration by the tribunal. However, the law minister confirmed Shahabuddin will face a corruption probe.

stories.title: US FDA nod for 1st pill to replace jabs to fight high cholesterol
At no point did government stop students from protesting: Nirmala Sitharaman
stories.summary: The government allowed student protests and focused on conducting the NEET re-examination promptly. Culprits involved in paper leaks were arrested and brought before the judicial process. A timely re-examination prevented a year's academic disruption for students. Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned after the successful re-examination process. India also faces inflation risks from external and internal factors this year.

stories.title: PM Modi hails youth for taking India to arenas once beyond reach
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised young Indians for recent achievements. PV Sindhu won the Japan Open badminton title, making the nation proud. India's first privately developed orbital rocket, Vikram-1, also achieved a successful launch. Students excelled in international science Olympiads, securing numerous medals. These accomplishments demonstrate the nation's confident and capable young generation.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Amid NH closure, Railways operates special trains to help stranded pilgrims
India saw more than 5,000 child adoptions last year, highest in a decade
stories.summary: India saw a record 5,022 children adopted between April 2025 and March 2026. Domestic adoptions accounted for 4,603 children, while inter-country adoptions numbered 419. Special needs children adoption increased by twenty-five percent, reaching 392 last year. Adoptions of girls also rose by eight percent, continuing past trends. Relative and step-parent adoptions saw a significant fifty percent increase.

stories.title: CJP's win fuels call by 'E20 Janta Party' for no-ethanol option
stories.summary: A new E20 Janta Party has emerged, demanding consumer choice for 100% petrol. This group seeks the resignation of Nitin Gadkari, the transport minister. Transporters are supporting this campaign, planning a march to Parliament against E20 petrol. The party advocates for transparent fuel labelling and data publication. They are not seeking subsidies but consumer choice and clear information.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Slavoj Žižek: 'The problem for us is not are our desires satisfied or not...'
stories.summary: Navigating modern life leaves many of us unclear about our true aspirations. The myriad choices presented by society can cloud our vision, making it hard to identify what we genuinely seek. Often, external factors influence our perceived goals, leading us to chase after things that don’t resonate with us. To find real fulfillment, we must delve into the origins of our desires and distinguish them from borrowed ambitions.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Thucydides: 'Self-control is the chief element in self-respect, and...'
stories.summary: Self-control is the foundation of self-respect, which ultimately nurtures genuine courage. Archidamus II of Sparta championed patience as a virtue over the urge for instant conflict. In Ancient Greece, ideas like sophrosyne highlighted the importance of achieving balance through self-mastery. In our fast-paced modern world, we often feel pressured to act impulsively. Cultivating self-discipline can enhance our decision-making capabilities across various situations.

stories.summary: Centre Tasked CSIR-NEERI To Cut Pollution Levels By 50%

stories.title: China’s new hybrid rice can preserve its high-yield traits across generations, allowing farmers to...
stories.summary: Innovative Chinese scientists introduced a self-cloning hybrid rice system that ensures impressive yields while allowing farmers to reuse seeds. This groundbreaking method cuts down on the need for yearly seed purchases, significantly lowering production costs for agricultural operations worldwide. Consequently, this advancement plays a crucial role in enhancing food security on both national and global scales, promising to bolster China's agricultural strength.

stories.title: Ethanol blended fuel damaged vehicles of people, claims Maharashtra Congress chief
TikToker Sara Gilson's final TikTok takes heartbreaking meaning after alleged murder-suicide by estranged husband
stories.summary: Famous TikToker Sara Gilson died after her estranged husband allegedly killed her. Police believe Jeremiah Duffey shot Sara before taking his own life. Court records show Sara had filed for divorce and received a protective order. Her final TikTok video now carries a heartbreaking and tragic meaning. A GoFundMe page was created to support her two children.

stories.title: A stormwater pond in Calgary appears filled with Prussian carp; the invasive fish can produce...
stories.summary: In Calgary, invasive Prussian carp are infiltrating the stormwater system, creating a serious threat to local ecology. These fish breed swiftly, endangering aquatic life and city infrastructure. Simultaneously, encounters with elk in Canadian parks are becoming more perilous than those with bears due to their massive size and unpredictable behavior, prompting authorities to implement management strategies to confront both wildlife conflicts and invasive species.

stories.title: 3 Indians die in workplace accidents in Gulf every week, shows MEA data
An 11-year-old boy cried after his first customer rejection; weeks later, his $10 business...
stories.summary: A young Canadian entrepreneur, just eleven years old, started a trash-bin cleaning service to earn some pocket money. His venture quickly attracted a large social media following and a multitude of clients, particularly during a tough summer job market for teens. With plans to keep the business growing into the colder months, he stands as an inspiring example for children worldwide to initiate their own entrepreneurial journeys.

stories.title: Opposition to take on government in Parliament over police action against protesting student
stories.summary: Opposition parties will strongly raise police action against protesting students in Parliament. Rahul Gandhi demanded accountability from Home Minister Amit Shah regarding the incident. He questioned the use of lethal force and deployment of plainclothes personnel. The INDIA bloc will finalize its strategy for parliamentary discussions on Monday. Opposition leaders are calling for a judicial commission to investigate the alleged assault.

stories.title: 'Every generation of Indians qualifies as ... ': Shashi Tharoor's reply to son Ishaan's 'ban Boomers on WhatsApp' remark
stories.summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor humorously responded to his son's social media call. His son suggested banning "boomers" from using WhatsApp. This exchange followed a debate on children's social media access. Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu proposed banning young children from social media. The discussion highlights differing views on digital platform usage for youth.

stories.title: ‘We are here to stay’: Indian-origin US lawmakers vow to fight anti-India hate in US
'Con job': Netanyahu celebrates ICC prosecutor's dismissal after arrest warrant battle
'No responsibilities': Mohan Bhagwat on live-in relationships; says marriage 'instils dharma'
stories.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat discussed marriage as a discipline instilling dharma. He noted live-in relationships as a modern alternative with consequences. Bhagwat also welcomed modernity while calling live-in relationships a blind imitation. He stressed that LGBTQ people are part of society and should be accepted. Elders should practice mobile discipline and engage in family conversations.

stories.title: 'Attempt to repair PM's tarnished image': Congress on high-powered exam reforms task force
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a high-powered task force for examination reforms. This move follows recent irregularities in national entrance examinations like NEET-UG. The Congress party criticized the initiative as an attempt to repair the Prime Minister's image. The government aims to establish a foolproof examination system through this task force. Recommendations from a previous committee have yet to be fully implemented.

stories.title: From Jantar Mantar to Parliament: Govt, opposition brace for fight over NEET row, other issues
stories.summary: As the monsoon session reconvenes, tensions rise again over the NEET-UG paper leak scandal. Opposition factions are determined to maintain pressure on the administration following significant protests. Prime Minister Modi has introduced reforms for examinations and established a dedicated task force for student welfare. In response, Rahul Gandhi is targeting the government over police conduct. The government aims to introduce a bill designed to eradicate malpractice in examinations.

stories.title: CDSCO cancels 7 clinical trial ethics panels over serious violations
stories.summary: India's drug regulator cancelled seven Ethics Committee registrations nationwide. Inspections revealed serious violations of clinical trial rules and guidelines. These committees oversee participant rights and safety during medical studies. The action followed a thorough compliance assessment and review process. This move ensures better adherence to regulatory standards for drug trials.

stories.title: PM Modi taps UIDAI architect Nilekani for exam overhaul
stories.summary: High-powered task force to recommend tech-driven, leak-proof reforms for NTA and public exams.

stories.title: ‘Responsible for brutal assault on innocent students’: After Dharmendra Pradhan, opposition turns heat on Amit Shah, seeks resignation
stories.summary: Opposition parties will intensify their Parliament attack on the government. They are demanding Home Minister Amit Shah's resignation over police action. This action involved students protesting the NEET paper leak issue. The government is also set to introduce amendments to the anti-paper leak law. Questions are also being raised about a key higher education secretary appointment.

stories.title: Infosys co-founder, Aadhaar architect: Who is Nandan Nilekani, set to lead high-powered exam reforms task force
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a high-powered task force for examination reforms. Nandan Nilekani, Infosys co-founder, will lead this important government initiative. The task force includes prominent figures from ISRO and IIT Madras. This development follows recent student protests and a minister's resignation. The government aims to address broader reforms within the education sector.

stories.title: The Chinese bahaba, a critically endangered fish was missing from Hong Kong for over a decade
stories.summary: A recent study has confirmed the presence of the rare Chinese bahaba in Hong Kong's waters through genetic material extracted from seawater. Nicknamed the 'Panda of the Sea,' this critically endangered fish had evaded scientific capture for over ten years. Researchers utilized cutting-edge environmental DNA technology, revealing traces of the fish's DNA across various western bays, thereby advancing non-invasive methods for marine population monitoring and conservation.

stories.title: Berlin police hunt 'Islamist suspect' after Pride attack kills one, injures 16
This Airbnb looks like a ship, has a secret treasure room and earns $80,000. Now it's for sale
stories.summary: Nestled in Salmon, Idaho, a captivating pirate-themed house is on the market for $799,000, boasting a remarkable annual income of around $80,000 from its Airbnb bookings. The property stands out amidst a collection of luxurious and historic homes detailed in market reports. Economic shifts are shaping the landscape of luxury real estate, with affluent baby boomers opting for more spacious residences as they transition into retirement.

stories.title: Romania shoots down third suspected Russian drone in three days, summons Moscow's envoy
stories.summary: Romania shot down a drone entering its airspace over the Black Sea. This marked the third such interception in as many days. President Nicusor Dan condemned these repeated violations as intolerable and unacceptable. Romania summoned the Russian ambassador to protest these airspace breaches. Investigations are ongoing into the drone incidents and border tensions are high.

stories.title: FBI's 'most wanted' suspect in $32 million Covid fraud arrested in Jamaica: Kash Patel
Slash-and-burn farming was blamed for destroying rainforests, but a study something different
stories.summary: In various small communities, unwritten agreements are crucial for sustainable land management. These norms not only restrict deforestation, fostering forest regeneration, but also bolster biodiversity by allowing flora and fauna to thrive. Research highlights the effectiveness of these traditions in safeguarding forest health over time. It is essential for policymakers to support and uphold these local practices for robust environmental conservation.

stories.title: These fish are born female & later become male; fishing may be changing them at molecular level
stories.summary: A new study has found that heavy fishing may be changing pearly razorfish at the molecular level. Researchers found no major changes in the fish's DNA but discovered differences in DNA methylation, an epigenetic process that affects how genes work. The study also found that marine reserves help preserve larger, older fish and maintain higher genetic diversity.

stories.title: The Taliban's Trojan horse: What really happened after Afghanistan's opium ban
Baby crib sent flying, 800,000 flee: Typhoon Noul hits China; scary visuals emerge
stories.summary: Typhoon Noul made landfall in southern China's Guangdong province early Sunday. More than 800,000 people were relocated to safer areas in Guangdong. Hong Kong experienced significant transport chaos with hundreds of flights cancelled. Dramatic videos of the storm's impact quickly went viral on social media. The typhoon weakened inland but heavy rain threats continue through Tuesday.

stories.title: Conservationists filled a 1.2km river channel, new Somerset wetland now attracts rare wildlife
stories.summary: A river restoration project in Somerset, UK, has shown major benefits within a year of completion. By reconnecting the River Aller with its floodplain, researchers found reduced flood peaks, cleaner water, higher groundwater levels and a sharp rise in wetland habitat. The restored landscape has also attracted more wildlife, including fish, birds and water voles.
